options.A:
Goal: Write a MATH-500 near-side fingerprint paper for NeurIPS Findings, the Datasets and Benchmarks track, or a workshop.

Plan: Use the collected Qwen3-4B-Instruct MATH-500 run of 30 clusters and 3 seeds as the only headline cell. Report Game24 as a Stage 0 parser audit and a cap-binding incident note. Send this packet to the reviewer. Place a second model family, a Game24 run on a larger Instruct model, and the frontier AIME four-arm table in later work, with the spent GPU cost of 55 dollars and a 30 to 50 dollar API block treated as the proposal envelope.
options.B:
Goal: Write a NeurIPS main fingerprint paper with at least two model-family by task cells.

Plan: Collect the running Game24 R2v7 seeds and run the joint cluster-bootstrap, mixed-effects, and SMD analysis with MATH-500. Add Qwen3-7B-Instruct on MATH-500 with the eight core arms. If Game24 on Qwen3-4B-Instruct stays cap-bound, run Game24 on Qwen3-7B-Instruct. Run the Stage 5 AIME four-arm table on a frontier API with the proposal API budget. Treat the 800 to 1200 GPU-hour figure as a forecast.

options.A:
Goal: Fit the original five-parameter resolution law after a large-deformation model and a new force measurement are in place.

Plan: Build a five-parameter corotational large-deformation cloth model that keeps the same coefficients as the current linear model. Collect a new synchronized known-force or boundary-reaction measurement so that density, tension, and bending can be recovered separately. After this model is fitted to real fast shaking cloth motion and the five coefficients are identifiable, estimate the original resolution formulas on that model and test them on unseen mesh sizes and time steps.
options.B:
Goal: Find how the effective parameters of an existing cloth simulator change with mesh size and time step.

Plan: Use an existing written cloth simulator as the dynamics engine, and use Clothilde if that is the simulator already in the workspace. At several mesh sizes and internal time steps, identify the simulator parameters that match real cloth marker motion. Fit a resolution law that predicts those effective parameters from mesh size and time step. Test the predicted parameters on mesh sizes and time steps that were not used in the fit, and compare them with parameters identified independently at those settings.

options.A:
Goal: Find the best native effective parameters on a 3 by 3 grid of spatial and time resolutions and then measure how those parameters change with resolution.

Plan: Run meshes 11 by 15, 15 by 21, and 21 by 29 with internal substeps 4, 8, and 16. At each cell, fit the seven Clothilde parameters on the G0 calibration windows under default thickness and under a fixed physical collision radius. Fit a log-linear resolution law on the five cross cells, and hold out the four corner cells for a later prediction check. Report Transferred, Gaussian-process, and same-budget Oracle marker errors on the same cells as a check that simulated error stays near those baselines.
options.B:
Goal: Close density, optimizer, and contact diagnostics and then run the 3 by 3 resolution matrix under a rule that the RG prediction beats the Transferred baseline.

Plan: Collect a cotton density scale contract and a test of whether adding that density residual recovers all seven native parameters. Run a matched seed-injection factorial with CMA-ES and differential evolution, and an objective ruggedness profile around the existing starts. Keep the agreement rule that each optimizer has at least 3 of 4 starts within 1 mm of the best loss. Measure default thickness and fixed physical collision radius on all nine cells. Start the 3 by 3 Oracle matrix after those tests pass, and count the RG prediction as a pass when held-out error is lower than the Transferred baseline on both contact treatments.

options.A:
Goal: Start the 3 by 3 resolution matrix after RG predictions beat the Transferred baseline on both contact treatments.

Plan: Compare the collected contact-radius results with the scientific admission rule for R11. Require RG trajectory error to be below Transferred error on every blind cell for default thickness and for fixed physical radius. Require a pooled paired 95 percent lower bound above zero, and a contact treatment difference no larger than 25 percent of the smaller gain. After this admission passes, run the 3 by 3 Oracle matrix on the five cross cells and then on the four corners, and use RG error below Transferred error as the primary comparison.
options.B:
Goal: Start the 3 by 3 resolution matrix and measure how effective parameters change with space and time resolution.

Plan: Run the 3 by 3 matrix on the five cross cells under default thickness and under fixed physical radius, with CMA-ES and differential evolution, four independent starts, and 4000 evaluations each. Fit a log-linear resolution law and a matched Matern Gaussian process on those five cells. Write the four corner parameter predictions and their hash, then run independent optimizations at the same evaluation budget on the four corner cells. Report RG, Transferred, Gaussian process, and Oracle held-out trajectory errors on each cell.

options.A:
Goal: Obtain the identified effective-parameter curves versus scale from independent global searches on one host after a same-host objective check.

Plan: Stop the compute node D R21C run and keep its 20 finished chains only as a cross-host diagnostic panel. Replay the sealed identification objective in isolated processes on compute node E and record the endpoint differences between compute node D and compute node E. Then start a new 124-chain R21C search on compute node E from the already declared starts and seeds. Do not copy, resume, or join the compute node D optimizer traces, checkpoints, or best points into that search.
options.B:
Goal: Obtain the identified effective-parameter curves versus scale from independent global searches on the host that already produced the objective scores.

Plan: Continue the R21C 124-chain independent global search on compute node D and keep the 20 finished chains and the in-flight traces in that run. After every admitted scale has a finished identification on compute node D, run the R21D interval confirmation on the same host. Do not start the remaining identifications on another host, because R20C measured a difference of up to 0.43 mm for the same parameter vector on two hosts.

options.A:
Goal: Calibrate a larger differential-evolution and CMA-ES search on the fine widened-box cell, then identify effective parameters on the admitted scales with that protocol.

Plan: Re-evaluate the narrow-box best point of the fine 15 by 21 cell on the 12-window widened-box objective in a fresh process. Then run two batches of new Sobol starts, with 16 differential-evolution chains and 16 CMA-ES chains in each batch and 8000 evaluations on every chain. Search the six positive parameters in the log of their raw physical values. Use the hit rate of the known deep basin to set how many chains each later scale will run so that the chance of missing that class of basin stays at most 5 percent. Then run that same differential-evolution and CMA-ES protocol independently on every spatial and time scale that already passed admission.
options.B:
Goal: Compare two global search methods on the same anchor cells, then identify effective parameters on the admitted scales with one of those methods.

Plan: On the fine 15 by 21 cell and the coarse 4 by 5 cell, run two methods on the same objective and box. The first method uses new Sobol starts with differential evolution and CMA-ES. The second method uses a coarse-to-fine grid to find distinct basins, keeps the lowest K basins, and refines each basin with bounded Nelder-Mead. Sample each parameter uniformly in its original physical quantity, or as the log of that quantity divided by a stated reference that has the same unit. Repeat each method twice at each cell, and record the lowest objective value, the evaluation count, and the core-hours. Then run the method chosen from this comparison independently on every spatial and time scale that already passed admission.

options.A:
Goal: Select a search method for later scale-by-scale identification by comparing a new grid search with the current optimizer on the fine and coarse cells.

Plan: On the fine cell 15x21_s8 boundary_12 and the coarse cell 4x5_s8 boundary_12, complete the current Sobol-start differential evolution and CMA-ES batches, and run a pairwise grid method in the dimensionless log-ratio coordinates. Split the six parameters into three pairs, delta with alpha, kappa with kappa_bnd, and stretch with shear, and start four joint contexts. For two sweeps, hold four parameters fixed while a two-dimensional coarse-to-fine grid updates one pair, cycling through the three pairs in a declared order, with a 3 by 3 box grid and a 5 by 5 local grid around the two lowest roots in each pair. After the sweeps, polish the top four survivors with bounded Nelder-Mead at 4000 evaluations. Run this schedule in two pair orders on both cells, and run a third pair order on both cells. After these completed runs, take the lowest verified objective as the target. A method is eligible if each completed schedule reaches that target plus 0.1 mm. Then record evaluations, core hours, and wall time, and apply the selected method at every remaining admitted scale.
options.B:
Goal: Select a search method for later scale-by-scale identification by comparing a new grid search with the current optimizer on the fine and coarse cells.

Plan: On the fine cell 15x21_s8 boundary_12 and the coarse cell 4x5_s8 boundary_12, complete the current Sobol-start differential evolution and CMA-ES batches, and run a six-axis grid method in the dimensionless log-ratio coordinates. Give that grid two layouts with four points on every axis, one on the box walls and one shifted into the interior, so each layer has 4096 joint evaluations. Identify discrete basins by steepest descent to face-adjacent neighbors, keep the eight lowest basins, refine each basin for two more grid levels, and polish each terminal root with bounded Nelder-Mead at 8000 evaluations. Treat the two optimizer batches as two replicates of the current method, and treat the two grid layouts as two replicates of the six-axis grid. After these completed runs, take the lowest verified objective as the target. A method is eligible if each replicate reaches that target plus 0.1 mm. Then record evaluations, core hours, and wall time, and apply the selected method at every remaining admitted scale.

options.A:
Goal: Identify the six simulator parameters on one time-step cell, using the six-parameter reference vector as the search center.

Plan: Keep density at 0.3046 and search delta, alpha, kappa, kappa_bnd, stretch, and shear together. Center the search on phi_ref = (0.3046, 0.6092, 1.523e-4, 1.523e-5, 1e-6, 1e-3). Use the four full marker recordings as one joint Eq. (10) objective on the native G0 mesh with eight substeps. Alternate two-dimensional blocks in the order dynamic, bending, then in-plane, run that cycle twice, and then run a bounded joint Nelder-Mead polish. Fit a second arm that searches only alpha and delta with the other four at zero, on the same objective. Start cross-scale RG work when the six-parameter endpoints sit off the box walls and agree across starts.
options.B:
Goal: Map how the joint two-parameter loss surface for alpha and delta changes across allowed time steps, with the other four physical parameters held at zero.

Plan: Keep density at 0.3046 and set kappa, kappa_bnd, stretch, and shear to zero. Use the four full marker recordings as one joint Eq. (10) objective on the native G0 mesh. After reading the five-scale coarse surfaces and the external corner bridge, add the remaining allowed time-step levels and extra shifted grids on the same two-parameter box of alpha and delta. Report sampled minima, edge profiles, and the direction of the surface at the walls. Start a lowest-order RG fit when at least five time-step levels have interior minima in this two-parameter slice.

options.A:
Goal: Get a six-parameter fit on the G2 cloth and treat mesh spacing on that cloth as the spatial-scale ladder.

Plan: Seal the converged G2 cell that uses the M1 rest seed and run the same three-path six-parameter identification on the G2 cloth of size 0.42 by 0.594 m. After the G2 search, hold the cloth area fixed and change the mesh counts so that the twenty markers sit on mesh nodes. Use the mesh spacing on this fixed G2 area as the spatial-scale sequence. If a G2 mesh cell stays inside the box and the three paths agree, add a second mesh rung on the same cloth before any flow fit.
options.B:
Goal: Get a six-parameter fit on the G2 cloth and treat the G0, G1, and G2 sheet areas as the spatial-scale ladder.

Plan: Seal the converged G2 cell that uses the M1 rest seed and run the same three-path six-parameter identification that was used on G0 and G1. Treat G1 and G2 as the two ends of a physical interval and keep G0 as an outer diagnostic geometry. After the G2 search, rebuild the minima, walls, and path scatter for G0, G1, and G2 against sheet area, and read that area sequence as the spatial-scale trend. If the three G2 paths stay inside the box and agree, add a second G2 member and then a denser area ladder before any flow fit.

options.A:
Goal: Find six-parameter endpoints at mesh k=4 with grouped alternating search.

Plan: On each search path at k=4, continue the three physical pairs through four rounds on the same path. After round one, round two, and round four, run the same bounded joint Nelder-Mead polish on all six parameters. Record the endpoint, the objective, and the cost at each of those round counts.
options.B:
Goal: Find six-parameter endpoints at mesh k=4 with grouped alternating search.

Plan: On each search path at k=4, optimize the three physical pairs for two rounds. Use a coarse grid in round one and a fine grid in round two. After round two, run one bounded joint Nelder-Mead polish on all six parameters and take that point as the path result.

options.A:
Goal: Test whether the mid-SR MultiHMR DTW row stays after leave-one-out, and whether that row pattern appears on two more HMR sources.

Plan: Run the leave-one-out cell, clip, and fold pipeline on the MultiHMR mid-SR dtw_positive binary DTW and contact rows. Call a cell degenerate when 4-channel Brier is below 1e-6 and scalar Brier is above 0.5. Convert the WHAM-repaired motions to the same joint format, and re-score the same 720 rollouts with raw MultiHMR and with WHAM-repaired. Use the high-SR geometric rows and the mid-SR dtw_positive DTW row as the pattern for those new HMR scores.
options.B:
Goal: Test whether the GVHMR and MultiHMR row means stay under a 0.001 4-channel Brier gate and under leave-1, leave-3, and leave-5 cell drops.

Plan: Recompute the GVHMR and MultiHMR per-cell scores. Call a cell degenerate when 4-channel Brier is below 0.001 or scalar Brier is above 0.95. For each panel, filter, and scalar, report the mean after dropping the top 1, 3, and 5 cells, and record any sign change. Include the mid-SR unfiltered binary DTW row. Repeat the binary fits on five fold seeds. Then re-score the same rollouts with raw MultiHMR and with WHAM-repaired.

options.A:
Goal: Test ranking robustness and MultiHMR training failure on the existing BeyondMimic-R18b and GMR panel.

Plan: Check SHA256 hashes and per-frame diffs of the four HMR caches. Compare MultiHMR and WHAM 12-clip sets on joint range, root velocity, jitter, and contact rate. Retrain BeyondMimic-R18b on the WHAM-repaired 12-clip set with three PPO seeds. Rebuild the metric-subset ranking so logistic, MLP, and GBDT each use a matching 4-channel baseline. Score that ranking with Brier, ECE, calibration slope, and weighted Brier, and rerun the tables on the 81-clip EMDB locomotion panel.
options.B:
Goal: Test a second tracker family or a second retargeter on the existing 24-clip WHAM panel.

Plan: Load OmniTrack, SONIC, ResMimic, GMT, ProtoMotions, and MaskedMimic, and run a short actor forward pass on existing EMDB clips. Load OmniRetarget and NMR, and convert the current WHAM-repaired SMPL trajectories to G1 joints. If a second tracker yields a usable checkpoint, run the 24-clip, 30-rollout missing-value rescore that is used for BeyondMimic-R18b. If a second retargeter yields G1 trajectories, retrain BeyondMimic-R18b with the iter-1000 success-rate gate of 0.30 and rescore the same 24-clip panel. Write a load-failure record for each candidate that does not complete a forward pass.

options.A:
Goal: Test whether any one 1D scalar can predict humanoid-tracker rollout success by beating a matched four-channel baseline on Brier score.

Plan: Keep the current panel with the BeyondMimic-R18b tracker, the GMR retargeter, and the 24-clip EMDB locomotion subset. Score MPJPE, DTW, foot-and-root MPJPE, contact-aware error, and jitter against a matched-family four-channel baseline with clip-grouped five-fold Brier. Vary NaN handling, combiner family, and risk function, and keep the three-seed fresh-rollout DTW check. Treat a scalar as a predictor only when it stays better than the four-channel baseline on all of those slices. Write the next result from the current tables as this dominance test, where no subset meets the gate and fresh-rollout DTW stays inconclusive.
options.B:
Goal: Rank which of the five 1D scalars, used alone or in pairs, can serve as proxies for humanoid-tracker rollout success on the current panel.

Plan: Keep the current panel with the BeyondMimic-R18b tracker, the GMR retargeter, and the 24-clip EMDB locomotion subset. Score MPJPE, DTW, foot-and-root MPJPE, contact-aware error, and jitter with clip-grouped five-fold Brier on the current subset-by-combiner matrix. Report which scalar ranks first when only one proxy is used, and report the score of each of the other four used alone. Report all ten pairs and the change when a second proxy is added to the stronger member of the pair. Keep the NaN-handling, combiner, and HMR slices inside those rankings.

options.A:
Goal: See which of three new PPO seeds on the R203 WHAM 12-clip mix pass a success-rate gate at 1000 training iterations, and collect rollouts from the seeds that pass.

Plan: Retrain PPO seeds 7, 13, and 23 in parallel on the R203 12-clip WHAM mix. Train each seed toward 8000 iterations, and stop a seed if its success rate at iteration 1000 is below 0.30. For every seed that stays above that gate, run 12 clips for 30 episodes each. Re-score the five post-hoc 1D proxy subsets on those rollouts. Record how many of the three seeds pass or fail the 1000-iteration gate.
options.B:
Goal: Train one new PPO seed on the R203 WHAM 12-clip mix for 8000 iterations, and evaluate the five post-hoc 1D proxies on that checkpoint's 12-clip rollouts.

Plan: Retrain one new PPO seed on the R203 12-clip WHAM mix for the full 8000 iterations, using the same training recipe as the historical seed-0 run. After iteration 8000, run 12 clips for 30 episodes on that checkpoint. Re-score the five post-hoc 1D proxy subsets and the adjacent-size paired tests on this panel. Place the new numbers beside the historical 8000-iteration WHAM three-checkpoint panel.

options.A:
Goal: Measure how four pre-rollout geometric channels relate to six post-rollout quantities, and how those six post-rollout quantities relate to one another.

Plan: From the existing retargeted reference trajectories, compute foot slide, joint jitter, penetration, and root height. Join these four channels with six post-rollout numbers taken per clip: success rate, mean DTW, mean MPJPE, mean foot-plus-root MPJPE, mean contact, and mean jitter. Compute rank correlations for two questions: whether the four pre-rollout channels predict the six post-rollout numbers, and whether the six post-rollout numbers agree with one another. If the pre-rollout channels do not predict the post-rollout numbers, report only the post-rollout agreement question.
options.B:
Goal: Measure whether five post-rollout 1D summaries can replace Brier when each clip has few episodes.

Plan: Reuse the existing 12-clip by 30-episode rollout table. For episode counts of 1, 3, 5, 10, and 30, compute Brier from the success labels and compute the mean of each of the five 1D summaries. Compare the cross-validation standard error of Brier with the standard error of each 1D summary at every episode count. Record whether the 1D summary has a smaller standard error than Brier at 1 or 3 episodes.

options.A:
Goal: Test whether the submitted post-rollout metric findings still hold when the GVHMR panel grows from 12 clips to 81 clips.

Plan: Train a BM PPO tracker on the 81 GVHMR clips with 8,000 iterations and 4,096 environments. After training, run 30 IsaacLab rollouts per clip on that checkpoint. Collect success rate, DTW, MPJPE, foot and root error, jitter, and contact from these rollouts. Recompute Spearman rank alignment, Cox time-to-failure, and DeltaBrier on the 81-clip panel, and compare each finding with the 12-clip panel.
options.B:
Goal: Test whether the submitted post-rollout metric findings still hold when the GVHMR panel grows from 12 clips to 81 clips.

Plan: Use the BM-R18b checkpoint as the tracker for the expanded panel. Run 30 IsaacLab rollouts on each of the 81 preprocessed EMDB GVHMR clips. Collect success rate, DTW, MPJPE, foot and root error, jitter, and contact from these rollouts. Recompute Spearman rank alignment, Cox time-to-failure, and DeltaBrier on the 81-clip panel, and compare each finding with the 12-clip panel.

options.A:
Goal: Measure held-out predictive adequacy of artifact-summary scalars across more than one upstream combination.

Plan: Pre-register the estimator and the decision rule. Collect a rollout panel that includes at least two HMR families and at least two retargeters or two tracker families. On held-out clips, score each artifact-summary scalar with a held-out Brier-score difference or an equivalent proper scoring rule. Compute cluster-aware intervals at the clip level or with HMR-by-retargeter random effects. Put every tested panel and every tested metric in one primary table with a multiplicity correction.
options.B:
Goal: Submit the current timeout-metric ranking study to the NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks Track.

Plan: Use the seven existing BM-R18b and GMR panels as the analysis set. Use the E16 clip-bootstrap aggregate partial Spearman as the primary estimator after control for episode length. Report MPJPE, foot-plus-root, and contact as the metrics whose intervals exclude zero, and report DTW and jitter as the metrics whose intervals include zero. Put the E15 and E21 VB GLMM fits in the appendix and add the E23 simulation rates as the calibration of those fits. Keep timeout as the success label, exclude short-trajectory DTW rows, and submit the rewritten paper to the NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks Track.

options.A:
Goal: Run the E8 and E9 held-out predictive-adequacy experiment described in idea.md and proposal.md.

Plan: Collect a factorial rollout panel with 4 HMR families, 3 retargeters, and 3 trackers. Use 30 clips and 30 rollouts in each cell, for about 97,200 rollouts, and add a PHUMA oracle row of 8,100 rollouts. Score each motion with the five artifact-summary scalars, the three motion-derivative scalars, and a learned 1D projection. Fit five-fold clip-held binomial GLMs and report delta Brier. Fit a crossed random-effect GLMM with HMR and retargeter groups, apply Holm step-down at alpha 0.1 on the five artifact-summary scalars, and run nested cluster bootstrap from HMR to retargeter to clip.
options.B:
Goal: Run an 81-clip panel that crosses HMR source and tracker checkpoint on the same motions.

Plan: Use 81 EMDB clips, 3 HMR sources (GVHMR, WHAM, and MultiHMR), and 2 tracker checkpoints (weak and fully trained). Train a PPO tracker on the 81-clip set at each checkpoint, then collect 10 rollouts per clip. Put the GVHMR, WHAM, and MultiHMR versions of one raw clip in the same CV fold, and resample by clip identity for cluster bootstrap. Report the interaction of metric, HMR, and checkpoint, the sign consistency of each metric, the gap between source-aware and source-blind predictors, leave-one-HMR-out scores, and 95 percent clip-cluster bootstrap intervals.

options.A:
Goal: Decide whether the V2 numeric and api_shortcut positive cells stay positive under a target-disambiguating LLM judge and a non-target task accuracy scrub gate.

Plan: Run an LLM judge that inserts the canonical hidden target into the prompt and asks whether the trace aims at that value. Start with the numeric open cell and one judge model on the Qwen3-4B cached traces. Score the raw reasoning view and the scrubbed view against the matched target-aware action regex at FPR 0.10. In the same round, ask a solver to answer the non-target task from the scrubbed trace, and compare that accuracy with the raw-trace accuracy. Expand the judge to the other three V2 positive cells and to a second judge model after the first cell shows a type-2 delta of at least 0.10 at FPR 0.10.
options.B:
Goal: Decide whether the V2 numeric and api_shortcut positive cells stay positive under a target-blind LLM judge and a topic-retention scrub gate.

Plan: Run a target-blind LLM judge with gpt-5 and gpt-4o-mini on the four V2 positive cells. The cells are numeric and api_shortcut, each in the open frame and the suppress frame, using the Qwen3-4B cached traces. Score the raw reasoning view and the deterministic-scrubbed view against the matched target-aware action regex at FPR 0.10. Take every cell, judge, and view combination as the V3 primary family. In the same round, patch the deterministic scrubber so that it redacts only literal target strings and metadata tokens. Then re-audit non-target topic retention on the same rows and require a score of at least 0.90.

options.A:
Goal: Measure extra catch rate of a thought-chain judge at a 10 percent false-alarm cap after the hidden number is swapped, when the judge is shown the hidden answer and when the judge is not shown it.

Plan: Split the cached judge scores by whether the prompt includes the hidden answer. On scores with the hidden answer, keep cells whose false-alarm rate is at most 10 percent and compute extra catch rate over the action monitor. On scores without the hidden answer, compute the same extra catch rate and the false-alarm rate on swapped items. Replace every target number string with a placeholder and recompute extra catch rate on the with-answer scores. On the cached files, run a two-sample test of original versus swapped scores in each arm, and join the two arms on matching family, generator, and budget cells.
options.B:
Goal: Measure extra catch rate of a thought-chain judge that is not shown the hidden answer, at a 10 percent false-alarm cap, after the hidden number in each item is swapped.

Plan: Use the cached judge scores in which the judge sees only the thought text. Cover the numeric, API, covert, and code-grader families and the three generator models already scored. For each family and generator, count how many cells still meet the 10 percent false-alarm cap on swapped items, and record the false-alarm rate on those swapped items. Also compute extra catch rate from the cached scores in which the judge was shown the hidden answer. On the same cached score files, compare the score distribution of original cheat items and swapped items, then make the family-by-generator grid and outcome table from those counts.

options.A:
Goal: Account for the oracle and deployable gap by testing a procedural channel and a referent channel on the cached traces.

Plan: From the cached high-score judge rationales, treat each trace as a procedural channel that names the cheat shape and a referent channel that names specific constants and nearby arithmetic. Report the alltargets-scrubbed sixteen-row table with its raw-view label, and treat the sixteen pass cells and the sixteen fail cells as a function of leftover arithmetic in the trace. Run a cache-only count of which channel each panel cites, and a cache-only regression of leftover arithmetic mass against oracle score-separation p-values on those thirty-two cells. Run a random-value injection that gives the judge a false canonical target, and a deployable repeat after stripping the grader-information block from the public task. State the paper main claim as this two-channel account of why deployable scores on canonical-cheat and substitution-cheat traces stay the same, and why leftover referent mass predicts oracle separation.
options.B:
Goal: Account for the four oracle and deployable cells on raw and scrubbed traces with one prompt-time canonical-target-access mechanism.

Plan: Put the alltargets-scrubbed count as zero of sixteen on the scrubbed view in the abstract and in the section 5.4 table. Write a proposal update that sets the oracle judge as the main estimand and argues novelty as the cost of losing private target metadata. Inspect the deployable prompt for leftover evaluator fields and few-shot target text, and rerun that arm after a patch if the leak is present. Write a mechanism discussion in which the oracle-raw cell passes because the prompt includes the canonical target, the deployable-raw cell fails because that field is missing, and both scrubbed cells fail because scrubbing removes the same literal from the trace. Restate the paper contribution as: chain-of-thought monitoring works only when the judge has prompt-time access to the canonical target, and a trace-level scrub does not replace that access. On the cached scores, check that the oracle distribution on scrubbed traces matches the deployable distribution.

options.A:
Goal: Close the V3 review with the V4 mechanism package, and collect the stripped-prompt deployable repeat and the random hidden-target injection from 20-item OpenAI batch-API calls.

Plan: Strip the grader-information block from the public task and call the deployable gpt-5 and o3 judges on the numeric_probe and api_shortcut grid across 12 shards, three budget tiers, and three generators, with 20 items per cell, as R66. From cache, score existing rationales for procedural versus referent features as R67, and regress surviving arithmetic residue on the 32 alltargets cells against oracle KS p as R68. Inject a random hidden-target value and a blank hidden-target value into the oracle prompt and call gpt-5 and o3 on the 24-cell grid with 20 items per cell as R69. Audit 50 traces with a non-OpenAI judge as R70. After the reviewer reads the 20-item R66 and R69 numbers, and after the user agrees, call those two batch designs again at 200 items per cell for the paper tables.
options.B:
Goal: Close the V3 review with the V4 mechanism package, and collect the stripped-prompt deployable repeat and the random hidden-target injection from 200-item OpenAI batch-API calls.

Plan: Strip the grader-information block from the public task and call the deployable gpt-5 and o3 judges on the numeric_probe and api_shortcut grid across 12 shards, three budget tiers, and three generators, with 200 items per cell, as R66. From cache, score existing rationales for procedural versus referent features as R67, and regress surviving arithmetic residue on the 32 alltargets cells against oracle KS p as R68. Inject a random hidden-target value and a blank hidden-target value into the oracle prompt and call gpt-5 and o3 on the 24-cell grid with 200 items per cell as R69. Audit 50 traces with a non-OpenAI judge as R70. Enter the 200-item R66 and R69 numbers in the paper tables for the leak-free deployable boundary and the random-Q causal figure.

options.A:
Goal: Measure whether PDE language context improves CP feature Utility when gpt5.6-sol proposes the candidate bank.

Plan: After the operator tuner and the non-Oracle solver competence checks, run PDE semantic Utility on Poisson and Helmholtz tasks at d=5, d=10, and d=20. Use gpt5.6-sol as the LLM proposer for the Full, NoSemantics, and wrong-context arms. Compare those banks with matched Random-CP, Fixed-Library, Fourier library, a deterministic forcing parser, and Oracle under the same tuning budget. Require a Full versus Random median ratio of at least 1.20. Run about 1 percent of API calls on development tasks, then 10 percent, then the full evaluation.
options.B:
Goal: Measure whether PDE language context improves CP feature Utility when DeepSeek proposes the candidate bank.

Plan: After the operator tuner and the non-Oracle solver competence checks, run PDE semantic Utility on Poisson and Helmholtz tasks at d=5, d=10, and d=20. Use DeepSeek as the LLM proposer for the Full, NoSemantics, and wrong-context arms. Compare those banks with matched Random-CP, Fixed-Library, Fourier library, a deterministic forcing parser, and Oracle under the same tuning budget. Require a Full versus Random median ratio of at least 1.20. Run about 1 percent of API calls on development tasks, then 10 percent, then the full evaluation.

options.A:
Goal: Test whether LLM-proposed CP features reduce end-to-end solver time on Allen-Cahn, Black-Scholes, wave, and anisotropic diffusion tasks.

Plan: Run an end-to-end time-to-error study on Allen-Cahn, Black-Scholes, wave, and anisotropic diffusion tasks. Use gpt5.6-sol as the proposer. On each task card, describe the operator, domain, boundary conditions, and qualitative physics. Expand the proposed structures with discretized constant enumeration, select them with elastic-net, and attach them to a zero-gated PINN. Compare LLM-LATTICE with vanilla PINN, Random-CP, Fixed-Library, and Oracle. Score success by LLM-LATTICE speedup over vanilla PINN and Random-CP for each family.
options.B:
Goal: Test whether parser-extracted CP features reduce end-to-end solver time on Poisson and Helmholtz tasks at dimension 5, 10, and 20.

Plan: Run an end-to-end time-to-error study on the 12-task Poisson and Helmholtz evaluation suite at dimension 5, 10, and 20. Use the deterministic forcing parser as the proposer. Also run gpt5.6-sol on the same discretized constant enumeration, elastic-net selection, and zero-gated PINN pipeline. Compare Parser-LATTICE and LLM-LATTICE with vanilla PINN, Random-CP, Fixed-Library, Fourier features, and Oracle. Score success by Parser-LATTICE speedup over vanilla PINN, Random-CP, and the strongest other baseline.

options.A:
Goal: Finish the remaining readiness runs and then run the repeated-seed LATTICE matrices on the coordinate and rank-1 feature network.

Plan: Run the random-feature scale and ridge cells on the v12 task. Run the three DeepONet arms for 1000 steps. Build the 100-dimensional HJB reference task. Then run the grammar, rank K, selector, operator-learning, and HJB experiments with repeated seeds. Keep the LATTICE MLP input as the training-point positions together with the rank-1 function values.
options.B:
Goal: Train the next LATTICE MLP cells with rank-1 function values, and with a short-trained basic MLP, as the input.

Plan: Train a basic coordinate-only MLP for 1000 steps and then keep those weights fixed. Give every later network the same size and the same start weights. Run LATTICE and RandomCP on four inputs: positions with rank-1 values, rank-1 values only, basic MLP output with rank-1 values, and basic MLP output with residual and rank-1 values. Train each cell on the v12 task for 3000 steps and record relative L2, residual, and gradient curves.

options.A:
Goal: Find out if language-conditioned proposals beat matched random banks and Vanilla after the twelve-task zero-init study.

Plan: Take rank-one functions to be products of one-dimensional factors. Collect No-Semantics and Shuffled language arms and add more task clusters under zero initialisation and the Shotgun host. Draw matched random banks from this product grammar with the same candidate count and selection budget. Report paired accuracy and time to the existing error target on the added tasks.
options.B:
Goal: Find out if language-conditioned proposals beat matched random banks and Vanilla after the twelve-task zero-init study.

Plan: Take rank-one functions to be any scalar functions of one or more inputs that can be evaluated quickly at sampled points. Include functions that are not products, such as the sine of the norm of the input vector. Build a grammar, a prompt, a validator, and a matched random generator that can express this class. Compare Vanilla, matched random, and language arms that share this grammar, first on one development task and then on four task cards.

options.A:
Goal: Measure residual learning against same-input classical estimators on the opened 22-event R82 panel.

Plan: Use the opened R82 panel as the next run. Compare PhaseCNN with prior-solver, six-channel ridge, TV assimilation, convex fusion, and Advect-Fuse-BP. Give every arm the same six channels, the same none, M, and T delivery, and the same 480-step correction, and tune each control only by training-event-deletion CV. Report absolute solver levels, relative effects versus the 0.25 mm per hour LUT step, the AA-PP over AA-solver fraction, and the split by event activity. State in advance that a loss to the strongest same-input control fails the learning claim, that a win under RMSE 0.5 percent and band 1 percent is under the declared materiality bars, and that a signal only on low-activity days is a regime-limited claim.
options.B:
Goal: Measure residual learning on the sealed 22-event R82 evaluation with the current solver and AA-PP controls.

Plan: Use the already collected R82A and R82B fields as the next run. Compare the T-treated aligned residual with the coarse-only 480-step solver on RMSE, MAE, FSS, and both registered bands. Use the exact-marginal AA-PP contrast as the information-free control. Keep five training seeds and the current 22-event panel. Enter the seed-by-event intervals into C2, C3, and C5, and enter the C4 surface with the two adverse bias cells as a qualification. Carry the band tally of 18 favorable, 2 crossing zero, and 0 adverse, and the C4 tally of 6 favorable, 4 crossing zero, and 2 adverse. Promote these numbers into the claim matrix and send version 0 to review.

options.A:
Goal: Choose the next Stage 0 step after the two-by-two path and prediction-target table on 100k sentences.

Plan: Download the smallest Meta LCM checkpoint and run the project concept benchmark on the same validation split. Confirm that the checkpoint loads and that it produces cosine and retrieval scores. Then train an LCM from scratch with the official LCM training recipe on the same data. Record concept cosine and predicted-vector norm from that training run. After those two reference runs, try ECF by changing a Meta checkpoint to the ELF objective, or by training from scratch with the ELF method, and compare the two paths if a later run has a problem.
options.B:
Goal: Choose the next Stage 0 step after the two-by-two path and prediction-target table on 100k sentences.

Plan: Take the 100k-sentence table as the Stage 0 outcome for the three claims. Record that the linear path and the cosine path give the same next-concept cosine under x-prediction. Record that four-step and forty-step scores match, and that direct MSE is higher than flow matching. Write that Claim 1, Claim 2, and Claim 3 are falsified. Stop new Stage 0 runs, and ask the user to choose among stopping this project, rewriting the work as a concept-generator design guide, or searching for an ECF mechanism other than noise path or step count.

options.A:
Goal: Close the three original claims from the 100,000-sentence 2 by 2 runs and choose a new direction.

Plan: Record the finished linear-path x-prediction run and the cosine-path x-prediction run as the Stage 0 outcome. Record that both paths give a concept cosine near 0.376. Record that 4 sampling steps and 40 sampling steps give the same score, and that MSE cosine is 0.383. Set the few-step flow-matching claim, the downstream text-quality claim, and the OmniSONAR claim to not supported. Launch no new training run. Ask the user to choose among leaving this workspace, rewriting the work as a concept-space generator design guide, or looking for an ECF difference that is not path and not step count.
options.B:
Goal: Run a Meta LCM benchmark and an official LCM training reproduction, then continue ECF.

Plan: Download the smallest Meta LCM checkpoint and measure concept cosine and retrieval on the same validation split used by the current runs. Train an LCM from scratch with the official LCM training recipe, and measure concept cosine on the reproduced model. After both LCM references exist, run ECF in two ways. One way changes the Meta checkpoint to a flow-matching next-concept generator. The other way trains a flow-matching model from scratch with the same evaluation. Use both paths to debug later ECF runs.

options.A:
Goal: Measure LCM scaling as a data-size curve of concept cosine for one large MSE-LCM model.

Plan: Keep parameter count fixed at the 1.6 billion parameter MSE-LCM recipe. Train on nested FineWeb-Edu sets of 0.5 million, 2.5 million, and 5 million sentences, and add 10 million or 20 million sentence runs of the same model. Record best concept cosine at each size and the training step at which overfitting starts. Use the rise of cosine and the later onset of overfitting as the scaling curve. On the largest set, continue past 10k steps if cosine is still increasing at the last checkpoint.
options.B:
Goal: Measure LCM scaling as the data exponent and the parameter exponent of next-concept loss.

Plan: Use the newer English FineWeb release and MSE-LCM models with fewer than 200 million parameters. Take the compute-efficient data-to-parameter ratio as about 20 to 1, and treat a factor of 20 above that ratio as the infinite-resource slice. Fit a power law of next-concept squared error, or an equivalent loss, versus data size in the large-parameter slice and versus parameter count in the large-data slice, including a constant loss floor. Collect several sizes on each axis so that each exponent can be identified. Target both exponents in the range 0.075 to 0.125.

options.A:
Goal: Measure whether trained LCM models obey the required data and parameter scaling exponents.

Plan: Build nested training sets from the latest English FineWeb crawl. Train MSE-LCM models with fewer than 200 million parameters along a data-size axis at one large-parameter setting and along a parameter-size axis at one large-data setting. Fit validation loss with an irreducible floor, and estimate alpha_D and alpha_P. Count the scaling gate as passed only if both exponents fall between 0.075 and 0.125. Keep the existing 1.6 billion parameter checkpoints for a later matched paper-metric test on the ROCStories reference split.
options.B:
Goal: Score the finished MSE and Two-Tower checkpoints on the original LCM paper metrics across all available evaluation sets.

Plan: Take the selected checkpoint from each of R29a, R29b, R29c, R30a, and R30b. Score each checkpoint on the six R26 ROCStories, C4, and Gutenberg splits and on the fixed FineWeb and Wikipedia validation sets, for forty evaluations in one run. Use the same evaluator, the same seed, and the same sample counts. Report L2, round-trip L2, PAR, contrast accuracy, and mutual information. Treat the ROCStories test absolute thresholds and the Two-Tower versus matched MSE deltas as the success gates.

options.A:
Goal: Measure the LCM data-axis and parameter-axis scaling exponents with the project R36 training loop.

Plan: Use the recorded R36 Stage 3 cell list, the 250k cosine recipe, the one-epoch alternate recipe, and the exponent interval 0.075 to 0.125. Train each cell in the project R36 loop. That loop reads batches from the official dataloader, scores next-sentence mean squared error with the official criterion, and uses official gradient normalization. Project code then performs overflow retries, optimizer steps, checkpoints, and validation, and the two exponents are fit from these cells.
options.B:
Goal: Measure the LCM data-axis and parameter-axis scaling exponents with runs of the pinned LCM Trainer.

Plan: Use the recorded R36 Stage 3 cell list, the 250k cosine recipe, the one-epoch alternate recipe, and the exponent interval 0.075 to 0.125. Train each cell by calling the pinned large_concept_model Trainer. This Trainer builds the recipe, loads data, computes the loss, steps the optimizer and scheduler, writes checkpoints, and runs evaluation. A project script may set paths and write receipts, and each cell stores the official source and config.

options.A:
Goal: Measure Kaplan scaling of LCM loss on one resource at a time, with the other resource left open.

Plan: For each existing exponent pair from the official scaling cells and the mature two-axis cells, recover how data size, parameter count, and compute were set in the fit. A Kaplan data fit holds parameters large, does not hold compute fixed, and regresses loss on data size. A Kaplan parameter fit holds data large, does not hold compute fixed, and regresses loss on parameter count. If recorded cells first chose the lowest-loss data size and parameter count at a fixed compute budget, do not enter those cells into the Kaplan regression. Report R-squared for each one-resource fit, and keep a fit only when it has at least six points and R-squared is at least 0.95.
options.B:
Goal: Bring the LCM data-axis and parameter-axis exponents into the range 0.075 to 0.125.

Plan: Take the finished mature two-axis cells and the earlier official scaling cells as Kaplan measurements. The current estimates are alpha_D=0.815 and alpha_P=0.290, and the earlier pairs are 0.132 with 0.895 and 0.401 with 0.524. Keep the success rule that both point estimates, every seed fit, and every leave-one-scale fit lie in 0.075 to 0.125, and that the two exponents differ by at most 0.03. Because the mature estimates lie outside that range, audit the official architecture and loss, or widen the unique data and model range of the same two-axis protocol, and refit until that range and the equality check pass.

options.A:
Goal: Judge the current LCM two-axis scaling measurements against the Kaplan exponent interval and continue the Two-Tower run.

Plan: Apply the interval 0.075 to 0.125 to the R40 values of alpha_D and alpha_P. Treat the high R-squared values as evidence that the power-law curves are stable. Inspect whether the R40 data-axis and parameter-axis exponents were obtained at matched compute so that the two values add to about one. Continue the live R41T Two-Tower training, checkpoint selection, and original five-metric evaluation while the scaling-law experiment stays open for that check.
options.B:
Goal: Judge the current LCM two-axis scaling measurements against the point-count and R-squared rule and continue the Two-Tower run.

Plan: Apply the rule of at least six data points and R-squared at least 0.95 to the R40 data-axis and parameter-axis fits. Store the measured SONAR-MSE exponents beside the earlier interval adjudication. Continue the live R41T Two-Tower training, checkpoint selection, and original five-metric evaluation. Measure the same scaling relation again later under other loss or data conditions. Ask the human if later results differ by a large amount and cannot be explained.

options.A:
Goal: Check the mapped ELF mechanism on the official LCM trainer with a real batch and a short resume.

Plan: Keep the R41T Two-Tower run on its selection and original-metric path. In parallel, connect the author ELF numerical rules to the official LCM trainer by adapting the sentence representation and the conditioning interface. On the official GPU runtime, run one real FineWeb batch forward and backward, check that every new parameter has a finite gradient, and compare a short resumed update with an uninterrupted control. Cap this run at ten steps.
options.B:
Goal: Finish the Two-Tower baseline and then run the first ELF-on-LCM claim comparison.

Plan: Keep R41T as the only active run until a checkpoint is selected by the existing validation-loss rule and the original five metrics are published. After those receipts exist, implement one ELF-on-LCM recipe from the completed fidelity map and train it for a matched 8-step and 16-step comparison against Diffusion-LCM-40 on the same data and architecture. Use that trained comparison as the first evidence for the primary claims.

options.A:
Goal: Complete the matched ECF versus Diffusion-40 comparison and measure inference complexity with sampling-step MAC counts in FLOPs.

Plan: Continue the ROCStories, C4, and Gutenberg evaluations that compare ECF-4, ECF-8, ECF-16, and ECF-40 with Diffusion-40 on the same architecture, data, and five quality metrics. For each sampling-step arm, count the model calls made by the sampler and the guidance recipe, multiply those calls by the architecture and task-shape multiply-accumulate counts, and report per-target complexity in FLOPs with one MAC counted as two FLOPs. Use that ledger, together with the five quality metrics, as the efficiency evidence.
options.B:
Goal: Complete the matched ECF versus Diffusion-40 comparison and measure inference complexity with wall-clock prediction time.

Plan: Continue the ROCStories, C4, and Gutenberg evaluations that compare ECF-4, ECF-8, ECF-16, and ECF-40 with Diffusion-40 on the same architecture, data, and five quality metrics. Time each sequential online prediction on one A100 after a short uncounted warm-up, with CUDA synchronization around every timed call, and omit model load, decoding, encoding, scoring, and file I/O from the timer. Save per-target durations and a paired document-cluster interval on Diffusion-minus-ECF time, and use that interval as the efficiency evidence.

options.A:
Goal: Measure inference complexity for the matched ECF and Diffusion-40 comparison.

Plan: After the matched ECF and Diffusion-40 evaluations are collected, measure generation latency for ECF-4, ECF-8, ECF-16, ECF-40, and Diffusion-40 on one exclusive A100. Use the sealed generation cards and the same-card timing protocol from the matched evaluation. Keep self-conditioning and classifier-free guidance inside the timed interval. Record wall-clock generation time as the complexity metric for the efficiency claim.
options.B:
Goal: Measure inference complexity for the matched ECF and Diffusion-40 comparison.

Plan: After the matched ECF and Diffusion-40 evaluations are collected, count registered sampling steps times multiply-accumulate operations for ECF-4, ECF-8, ECF-16, ECF-40, and Diffusion-40. Compute the MAC counts from the frozen 1.645B architecture, the sealed generation cards, and the observed call traces, including guidance and self-conditioning branches. Report the product in FLOPs, with one MAC equal to two FLOPs. Use this step-times-MAC ledger as the complexity metric for the efficiency claim.

options.A:
Goal: Compare ECF with matched Diffusion-40 on C4, ROCStories, and Gutenberg after the R46T run.

Plan: Evaluate ECF-4, ECF-8, ECF-16, ECF-40, and Diffusion-40 on both splits of each corpus with the frozen target lists and metrics. Load the R46T raw weights for every ECF arm. Keep the Diffusion-40 checkpoint and the generation cards unchanged. Use the three corpus tables as the evidence for C1 and C2.
options.B:
Goal: Compare ECF with matched Diffusion-40 on C4, ROCStories, and Gutenberg after the R46T run.

Plan: Evaluate ECF-4, ECF-8, ECF-16, ECF-40, and Diffusion-40 on both splits of each corpus with the frozen target lists and metrics. Load the R46T EMA weights for every ECF arm. Keep the Diffusion-40 checkpoint and the generation cards unchanged. Use the three corpus tables as the evidence for C1 and C2.

options.A:
Goal: Set the FineWeb-Edu smoke budget and the 20 to 1 exposure for a later 50 million parameter ECF versus Diffusion pilot.

Plan: Count GPT-2 tokens only on sentences after the first sentence of each document when filling the 100 million token smoke tier and when setting the 20 to 1 data ratio. Treat the first sentence as a context prefix and keep a separate raw token total over the full document. After the smoke set passes, train the 50 million parameter arms on the same selected rows with about 1 billion unique raw target tokens.
options.B:
Goal: Set the FineWeb-Edu smoke budget and the 20 to 1 exposure for a later 50 million parameter ECF versus Diffusion pilot.

Plan: Count GPT-2 tokens at every non-padding sentence position, including the first sentence of each document, when filling the 100 million token smoke tier and when setting the 20 to 1 data ratio. Keep a separate total for tokens at positions that have a previous sentence in the same document. After the smoke set passes, train the 50 million parameter arms on the same selected rows with about 1 billion unique tokens from this all-position target count.

options.A:
Goal: Test whether the current FK candidate sets beat equal-wall-clock controls on XSum using human labels.

Plan: Prepare a blinded packet of 300 documents with three arms: the current FK kernel, best-of-N at the same wall-clock, and FK with isotropic jitter. Ask three annotators to label factuality, informativeness, duplicates, and set preference, and reuse 10 percent of items as repeats. Take a preference lower bound above 55 percent against each control, and factuality within 1 percentage point, as the success bar.
options.B:
Goal: Test whether a repaired FK method beats equal-wall-clock controls on XSum using automatic evaluators.

Plan: Run the next diversity-aware FK repair on XSum and score quality after removing near-duplicate outputs, coverage, and end-to-end wall-clock with MiniCheck and QAFactEval. Look at 10 to 20 blinded examples for factuality, informativeness, and duplicate problems. Take a confidence interval that stays above zero on both evaluator families after near-duplicate removal as the success bar.

options.A:
Goal: Measure selective_ci_bottom50 on the R49 selected-ID MiniCheck semantic-set endpoint.

Plan: Aggregate the already-finished MiniCheck scores on the registered selected-ID set from the 512-document and 3-seed R49 run. Compare semantic top-3 utility against identity and the named equal-wall-clock controls. Record the generation-stage source-NLI self-check and the 96-document R53A calibration as source-NLI numbers. If the MiniCheck comparison is not positive, stop the remaining QAFactEval pass on the 649,728-candidate pool and run small-scale independent MiniCheck and QAFactEval checks on a disjoint calibration split. If the MiniCheck comparison is positive, score QAFactEval on the selected-ID set.
options.B:
Goal: Finish R49 as the paper-scale confirmation of selective_ci_bottom50 on fresh XSum.

Plan: Continue independent evaluation of the merged 512-document and 3-seed pool of 649,728 candidates. Take the generation-stage source-NLI paired bootstrap as the directional result. Let MiniCheck, which has already scored the full pool, and QAFactEval, which is still running on the same full pool, both finish. Report those two independent evaluator numbers for the paper. Leave the sampler, reward, thresholds, split, and named equal-wall-clock controls unchanged.

options.A:
Goal: Test whether selective_ci_bottom50 beats the named controls on MiniCheck and QAFactEval.

Plan: Keep the R53A winner selective_ci_bottom50 unchanged. Generate this arm against the named controls on the fresh XSum split of 512 documents with three seeds. Score those candidates with MiniCheck and QAFactEval. Report the 512 by 3 numbers as the confirmation of the main comparison.
options.B:
Goal: Test whether selective_ci_bottom50 beats the named controls on MiniCheck and QAFactEval.

Plan: Keep the R53A winner selective_ci_bottom50 unchanged. Generate this arm against the named controls on a fresh XSum split sized to finish generation and scoring in one day. Score those candidates with MiniCheck and QAFactEval. Run a 512-document three-seed confirmation if this one-day result is positive.

options.A:
Goal: Run the lift pipeline on a PDE whose high-dimensional from-scratch FEX search fails.

Plan: Select a PDE that has a known solution and that fails high-dimensional from-scratch FEX search. Run low-dimensional FEX search until a skeleton is recovered. Lift that skeleton with the existing three-gate audit at d=10, d=20, d=50, and d=100. Record the low-dimensional search result, the high-dimensional lift residual, and the high-dimensional from-scratch outcome on the same PDE. Run an executable external baseline with multiple seeds.
options.B:
Goal: Run the next round on the current accepted families and the Poisson HD-TLGP comparison.

Plan: Run the official HD-TLGP code on polynomial Poisson at d=2 with three to five seeds, and report the mean and the standard deviation. Sweep the low-dimensional fit threshold and the high-dimensional probe threshold on the composite families and the perturbed composite families. Add two or three structures to the macro library, and compute the false-accept rate on the current reject families again. Write the external baseline, the perturbed-family acceptances, and the pairwise lifts as partial in the claim list.

options.A:
Goal: Answer the V6 review by testing Conservation recovery from a systematic unary linear-combination library and adding a guided GP baseline.

Plan: Remove the sine, cosine, cube, exponential, and quartic anchor macros from the library. Add unary linear-combination macros whose amplitude, linear coefficients, and bias are learned from data. Rerun Conservation, Poisson, radial, and a reject family under this library, and check that Conservation still selects the sine form with lift error below 0.001 at dimension 100 and that the audit does not newly accept a high-error lift. Run PySR on Conservation at dimensions 3, 10, and 50.
options.B:
Goal: Answer the V6 review by presenting Conservation as a single-case study of FEX liftability and adding a guided GP baseline.

Plan: Keep the current macro library, including the sine, cosine, cube, exponential, and quartic anchor macros. Rewrite the argument around Conservation as the only hard window, and present the cubic, quartic, and other candidate outcomes as part of that finding. Run PySR on Conservation at dimensions 3, 10, and 50. Count false accepts on the existing 624-cell ablation under a macro-name definition and a lift-quality definition.

options.A:
Goal: Test whether a d=3 FEX tree can be lifted to d=100 by fitting a linear mix of high-d coordinates at each leaf.

Plan: Parse the Conservation FEX trees found at d=3. Keep the operators in each tree. Replace each leaf variable with a linear combination of the high-d coordinates. Use the original tree coefficients plus a mixing matrix with one row for each low-d variable and one column for each high-d coordinate. Set the first square block of the matrix to the identity and set the remaining entries to small random values. Fit these parameters on the high-d PDE residual and the boundary loss at d=20, d=40, and d=100 with three seeds each. Measure relative L2 error against the analytic Conservation solution. Restrict the fitted high-d formula back to d=3 and measure agreement with the original tree.
options.B:
Goal: Test whether Helmholtz can be found at d=3 and lifted to d=100 by matching the low-d tree to the sine-of-linear-sum macro.

Plan: Add Helmholtz as a target family. Use the residual Laplacian of u plus k squared times u equals zero, the box from 0 to 2 pi in each coordinate, and the closed form sine of the sum of all coordinates, with k squared equal to the dimension. Run FEX search at d=3 with five seeds and the same depth-2 grammar used for Conservation. Match each low-d tree to the sine-of-linear-sum entry in the macro list. Fit only that entry's continuous coefficients at d=20, d=40, and d=100. Run from-scratch FEX at d=30, d=40, d=50, and d=100. Record the low-d hit rate, the d=100 relative L2 error of the lift, and the from-scratch hit rate at d=40 and d=100.

options.A:
Goal: Test whether Conservation can be lifted from a low-d FEX tree to d=100 by a learned mixing matrix.

Plan: Take the existing Conservation FEX trees from the d=3 search with 5 seeds. For each tree, replace every leaf variable x_i by a weighted sum of the high-d coordinates, and keep the original operators and coefficients. Learn the mixing weights with LBFGS on the Conservation PDE residual and the boundary loss. Lift each tree to d=20, d=40, and d=100. Report the d=100 lift rel-L2, and the rel-L2 of the lifted expression when it is restricted back to d=3.
options.B:
Goal: Test whether Helmholtz can be lifted from a low-d FEX search to d=100.

Plan: Add the Helmholtz family Laplace(u) + d*u = 0 on the cube from 0 to 2 pi in each coordinate, with Dirichlet data from u = sin(sum of all coordinates). Search with FEX at d=3, tree depth2_sub, 5 seeds, and 60 epochs. On seeds that hit, lift with the sin_anchor_sum macro at d=20, d=40, and d=100. Run scratch FEX at d=30, d=40, d=50, and d=100 with 3 seeds at each dimension. Report the low-d hit count, the d=100 lift rel-L2, and the scratch hit counts at d=40 and d=100.

options.A:
Goal: Choose one high-d transfer from the shape of the low-d FEX tree, and check that choice on Conservation and Helmholtz.

Plan: Parse each low-d FEX tree. For a tree that wraps a sum of variables in one function, fit a model that replaces each low-d variable by a learned linear mix of the high-d coordinates. For a tree that sums the same function of each variable, fit a model that copies that function onto each high-d coordinate and adds the copies. Run both models on Conservation and on Helmholtz at d=100. Count success when Conservation with the linear mix and Helmholtz with the copied function are below 1e-3 relative L2, and the crossed pairings stay above 1e-3 or fail to fit.
options.B:
Goal: Insert extra coordinates at successive layers of each low-d FEX tree, and reach relative L2 below 1e-3 on at least six PDE families at d=100.

Plan: From each low-d FEX tree, make high-d candidates that insert extra coordinates at the leaf layer, then at the next layer up, then at higher layers. Fit the candidates in that order on the high-d PDE residual, and stop when relative L2 is below 1e-3. Keep the list of all candidates for each tree. Run five seeds at d=100 on Conservation, cosine-anchor, cubic-anchor, quartic-anchor, Helmholtz, Schrodinger, Poisson, and sum of fourth powers. Count a family when at least three seeds are below 1e-3, and continue until six families meet that mark.

options.A:
Goal: Test whether high-dimensional formulas can be built by trying insertion candidates at each layer of a low-dimensional FEX tree, and obtain positive lifts on at least six PDE families.

Plan: From each low-dimensional FEX tree, list legal high-dimensional insertion candidates from the leaf layer upward, including leaf mixing and node or subtree replicate pooling with sum, mean, and normalized-sum aggregators. Fit the candidates with continuous optimization in that layer order, and stop when residual, boundary, and low-dimensional consistency meet the threshold. Keep every listed candidate until its fit metrics are recorded. Run this scout on at least eight families that are already in the codebase, covering signed-sum, separable-sum, moment-type, and exp(mean(cos(x))) divided by d, with five seeds and dimension 100. A family is positive when at least three of five seeds reach relative L2 below 1e-3. The scout targets at least six positive families, and it writes the full candidate list and the trial order for every tree.
options.B:
Goal: Test whether a parser can read a low-dimensional FEX tree and assign one transfer primitive from the tree shape on Conservation and Helmholtz.

Plan: Add an auto-transfer module that maps a depth-2 tree of the form unary of a binary of two leaves to leaf mixing, and maps a depth-1 tree of two identical unary leaves to unary replication. Load the existing Conservation dimension-3 search seeds and Helmholtz dimension-2 search seeds. For each seed, build both primitives, fit them at dimension 100, and record relative L2. Conservation is assigned leaf mixing and Helmholtz is assigned unary replication. The matching cells reach relative L2 below 1e-3, and the mismatched cells stay above 1e-3 or fail to optimize. The assignment rule uses tree shape and unary names taken from the tree, and it does not use PDE names or macro names.

options.A:
Goal: Decide how to lift a two-dimensional mean-cosine formula to high dimension, and how to treat the current Schrodinger result.

Plan: Lift the constant two in the two-dimensional mean of cosines to a new fitted scale in front of the high-dimensional sum of cosines. Use a Schrodinger lift formula that, when limited to two coordinates, still includes the original two-dimensional formula. Treat the large error from putting the current dimension-100 fit back on two coordinates as a fitting problem of the high-dimensional optimizer. Add this fitted-constant lift to the node-replication method and fit Schrodinger and other mean-cosine trees again.
options.B:
Goal: Decide how to lift a two-dimensional mean-cosine formula to high dimension, and how to treat the current Schrodinger result.

Plan: Replicate cosine on every coordinate and combine the terms with a fixed factor of one over the number of coordinates. Write the high-dimensional formula as the exponential of a fitted scale times the mean of cosine of a linear function of each coordinate. Remove Schrodinger from the lift-success list because putting the dimension-100 fit back on two coordinates produces a large error. Keep the inherited mean constant equal to the number of coordinates.

options.A:
Goal: Find out whether a random-structure symbolic regression baseline can recover the d=100 expressions for pairwise and the six non-Conservation families.

Plan: Run a random-structure plus LBFGS baseline at d=100 on pairwise_x2x2, quartic_anchor_sum, helmholtz_separable, poisson_sumsq, sum_x4, cos_anchor_sum, and radial_quartic. Give each family 6000 finite trials. After all 6000 trials finish, record whether any trial reaches rel-L2 below 1e-3, and record the best rel-L2 and the best expression.
options.B:
Goal: Find out whether a random-structure symbolic regression baseline can recover the d=100 expressions for pairwise and the six non-Conservation families.

Plan: Run a random-structure plus LBFGS baseline at d=100 on pairwise_x2x2, quartic_anchor_sum, helmholtz_separable, poisson_sumsq, sum_x4, cos_anchor_sum, and radial_quartic. Stop a family when one trial reaches rel-L2 below 1e-3, or when 600 finite trials have no such hit. Then record whether any trial reached rel-L2 below 1e-3, and record the best rel-L2 and the best expression.

options.A:
Goal: Add high-dimensional test problems that raise particle count while the interaction form stays the same.

Plan: Take the next problems from multi-particle interaction equations, including the Kuramoto model, opinion dynamics, and Cucker-Smale. For each equation, write the interaction at a small particle number with the present operators, and check that the same form extends when the particle count grows. Run a seed-0 lift from 4 particles to 32 or 64 particles on the Kuramoto model and on one other equation that this check accepts. Use the same data splits at both particle counts, and treat the coupling constants as learnable. Score the candidates on the particle vector field after the parameters are set.
options.B:
Goal: Add high-dimensional test problems that raise spatial dimension while the PDE form stays the same.

Plan: Take the next problems from a hidden list of spatial PDE families at dimension 100. Cover four transfer classes, and give each class some positive families and some negative families. Fit tree-conditioned candidates and a matched blind grammar on the same collocation points and with the same optimizer. Select each candidate with PDE residual and boundary conditions only. Record the candidate count and the core-second cost for every family.

options.A:
Goal: Measure whether a low-dimensional expression tree reduces exhaustive high-dimensional search cost on four transfer primitives.

Plan: Run the leaf, replicate, pairwise, and block tree-information jobs with one positive family and one matched negative family in each of four primitive classes, five tree arms, and one fit seed. Fit all target, cross, random, and oracle candidates, and on the blind arm fit the target-overlap candidate and 16 candidates drawn by expression-tree size in each family with the inclusion probability of each draw recorded. Compare target and blind candidate counts from the full family lists, and estimate blind CPU time from the stratified runtimes.
options.B:
Goal: Measure whether a low-dimensional expression tree reduces exhaustive high-dimensional search cost on four transfer primitives.

Plan: Run the leaf, replicate, pairwise, and block tree-information jobs with 24 hidden families, five tree arms, and three fit seeds. Fit every high-dimensional candidate on the target, cross, random, blind, and oracle arms. After the four classes finish, compare matched target and blind totals for candidate count and CPU time.

options.A:
Goal: Recover a hidden leaf or pairwise source tree whose affine error is below 1e-3, then run transfer and matched fit-all for Claim K.

Plan: Keep seed 0 and the four physics tests at 1e-3. Use the V44 fixed-tree refit, the 28800-action search, and the PDE-solver teacher as the current source attempts. If any class falls below 1e-3, copy that source into a full-layer transfer on the hidden target and then run the matched fit-all with no early stop. If every current source stays above 1e-3, open a new source search that changes tree depth, the operator set, the seed, or the hidden family, and then run the same transfer and fit-all.
options.B:
Goal: Test overlapping domain decomposition and a WKB phase search on the frozen double-well Schrödinger equation, then lift a passing local tree to d=100.

Plan: Keep the V26 target with a=1 and domain [-3,3]. Run two seed-0 low-dimensional arms that split the domain at x0=0. One arm searches the wavefunction on overlapping left and right subdomains and joins them with a partition of unity. The other arm searches a WKB or Riccati phase on the same split. Score candidates with PDE, boundary, and interface residuals before reading the true solution. If an arm meets the 1e-3 tests, copy its local expressions into a d=100 all-layer transfer and run matched scratch FEX, SIREN, and DD-PINN baselines.

options.A:
Goal: Find out how the eight-family tree ablation changes when each cell winner is chosen by PDE residual.

Plan: Rerun Conservation and two families where true-tree and no-tree both already passed. Fit the same four arms and choose the cell winner with a normalized PDE residual and boundary score on one shared validation point set. Generation, fitting, and selection load only residual and boundary data. After selection, a separate evaluator computes analytic relative L2. Use five seeds and report how often the physics winner matches the truth winner.
options.B:
Goal: Find out whether the current true-tree successes come from explicit symbolic bases or from neural residual corrections.

Plan: Take the residual_lift winners already stored for Conservation, HJB, Helmholtz, and pairwise_x2x2. For each winner, evaluate the symbolic base alone, the residual network alone, and the hybrid, and record relative L2 and residual magnitude. Record a symbolic recovery when the base alone is below 1e-3, or when the residual is rewritten with allowed primitives and checked on held-out points. List hybrid numbers next to the base-only numbers. Save a per-candidate ledger with parameter counts and independent PDE and boundary metrics.

options.A:
Goal: Measure whether a pretrained PDE-conditioned controller reduces full-FEX search steps on hard and high-dimensional PDEs.

Plan: Connect the reference FEX code so that Adam and BFGS coefficient optimization is in the search loop. Reproduce the v1 function-fitting pilot and the v2 Poisson residual pilot. In the same first round, run a paired full-FEX study on 1D nonlinear Schrodinger and a high-dimensional Poisson scout, with test trees held out by structure. Compare pretrained, scratch, and conditioned-random controllers on the same instances and the same seeds. Record step-to-threshold, final residual, and wall-clock. Put the hard-family paired run and the high-dimensional scout on the first-round list with the FEX wiring. If the high-dimensional scout cannot solve, record the root cause and keep 1D nonlinear Schrodinger as the hard target. Set the paper claim to a FEX foundation-model study of controller pretraining.
options.B:
Goal: Measure whether a pretrained PDE-conditioned controller reduces full-FEX search steps on 1D Poisson and 1D Helmholtz.

Plan: Connect the reference FEX code so that Adam and BFGS coefficient optimization is in the search loop. Reproduce the v1 function-fitting pilot and the v2 Poisson residual pilot. Then run a paired Stage 0 study on reverse-generated 1D Poisson and 1D Helmholtz, with test trees held out by structure. Compare pretrained, scratch, and conditioned-random controllers on the same PDEs and the same seeds. Record step-to-threshold, final residual, and wall-clock. If the pretrained arm does not improve median step-to-threshold on Poisson or Helmholtz, end the expansion to other PDE families. Start nonlinear Schrodinger and high-dimensional Poisson after this Stage 0 result. Set the paper claim to a transfer-boundary study on these two families.

options.A:
Goal: Choose a data strategy after the real-source bank stays at 44 verified instances, 32 templates, and 21 actions, below the gate of 280 verified instances, 160 templates, and 40 actions.

Plan: Use a yield of about 0.57 verified packets per paper, measured on 14 method papers, to size the next data work. Then pick one of three data strategies. The first expands the current expression grammar and sets a new data gate near 100 verified instances, 60 templates, and 30 actions. The second keeps the current gate and searches for another high-density formula table, such as a digitized handbook. The third trains the controller on a synthetic PDE generator bank and uses real PDEs only for evaluation.
options.B:
Goal: Fill the data gate of 280 verified instances, 160 templates, and 40 actions with exact solutions taken from real PDE papers and PDE benchmarks.

Plan: Search arXiv and public PDE benchmarks for papers that state exact 1D and 2D solutions. Build a list of at least 200 papers, and put physics-informed neural network benchmark papers, analytical-solution surveys, and solver-comparison papers first. From the top of that list, extract the PDE, solution, domain, and initial or boundary conditions from about 50 papers, and check each packet with independent residual tests. Use these real packets for both pretraining and evaluation.

options.A:
Goal: Get paper 2509.07478 through formula checks with the current grammar.

Plan: Repair the 2509 packet. Turn the piecewise cases into the quadratic formula that the grammar already has. Bind the self-similar ODE and the transformed conditions in one frame, and set xi_0 only from source evidence that applies to the original problem. Keep the grammar, the action set, and the residual limits unchanged. Record paper 2104.14561 as outside the present representation. Replay 2509 and report whether a new verified formula appears in the 15-paper set.
options.B:
Goal: Get paper 2509.07478 and paper 2104.14561 through formula checks.

Plan: Repair the 2509 packet. Turn the piecewise cases into the quadratic formula that the grammar already has. Bind the self-similar ODE and the transformed conditions in one frame, and set xi_0 only from source evidence that applies to the original problem. Add an exact infinite-series action for paper 2104.14561. First test that old verified formulas stay the same, that the series meets the current residual limits, and that a finite truncation is not treated as the source formula. If that test passes, put the action into the grammar and replay 2104.

options.A:
Goal: Collect real PDE training examples from new papers, then keep those examples that pass a residual check.

Plan: Start with 3 to 5 new arXiv TeX files. Take equation sections and nearby text as input. Send those chunks to gpt-5.6-terra through codex exec, or to sonnet5 through claude -p, at medium effort, and ask for JSON with example name, PDE, solution, domain, and conditions, each with a source line. Ask GPT-5.5 how to write the prompt, and try a few prompt versions on this set. Keep an example when the residual of the extracted solution in the extracted equation is below 1e-6 in SymPy. If at least one paper yields a passing example, enlarge the paper set by a factor of two to five and repeat.
options.B:
Goal: Collect real PDE training examples from new papers, then keep those examples that pass a residual check.

Plan: Search up to 200 new arXiv papers that were not used in earlier labeled sets and download their TeX. Take equation environments and nearby text as input. Parse the PDE, solution, domain, and conditions with a TeX formula parser. Keep an example when the residual of the parsed solution in the parsed equation is below 1e-6. Keep the set if at least 8 examples from 8 paper clusters and 5 PDE families pass. Then run the DeepSeek production extractor on this set and require 100 percent field precision and at least 80 percent example recall. If those gates pass, extract from about 100 papers.

options.A:
Goal: Build a source-real equation database from real arXiv papers, then extract roles and grow the training set.

Plan: Split the 1,694 readable sources into 1024 training sources, 512 evaluation sources, and 64 development sources, with no source in more than one split. Keep every rendered math span from the saved TeX of those papers. On development sources, write a role-and-link prompt that names each span and how spans connect, then run the same prompt on later sources with no prompt change. Keep a raw row when the model answers unknown or when the current compiler cannot represent the span. Leave out locally generated formulas and formulas made by reversing a candidate solution.
options.B:
Goal: Classify real-source equations as natural or manufactured, then admit later training data with that classifier.

Plan: Take the 4 development and 4 confirm natural examples from the latest per-example review and train a labeling policy that marks each example as natural or manufactured. On development data, accept the policy only if it passes the format and ontology checks and labels no manufactured example as natural. Then run the same prompt on the confirm examples and on four blind waves of the existing manufactured-solution control bank, with no prompt change between waves. After those tests pass, collect 60 and then 120 new real PDE sources and keep only examples that the policy labels natural. Keep manufactured examples out of training and evaluation.

options.A:
Goal: Collect enough complete PDE-and-solution examples by opening arXiv tutorials and lecture notes on PDEs, SDEs, mathematical physics methods, and general physics.

Plan: Select the next sources from arXiv metadata only, and record the source IDs before any TeX download. Open 16 tutorial or lecture-note sources across those four topics, together with 8 ordinary research papers that match on category, year, and version era.
