Run the current v3 extractor on both groups, keep every rendered equation, and count complete PDE-and-solution links per opened source. Then open a new set of 64 tutorial or lecture-note sources and 32 matched ordinary papers and extract them the same way.
options.B:
Goal: Collect enough complete PDE-and-solution examples by finishing extraction on the current 1,694 arXiv research papers and then opening more papers from the same source lists.

Plan: Continue the current v3 extractor on the remaining train, eval, and reserve slices of these 1,694 arXiv research papers. Keep every rendered equation from those papers. After the last slice is complete, count strict train rows, templates, actions, and held-out executable targets against the gates of 200, 80, 40, and 200. If those counts are below the gates, open the next ordinary arXiv research papers in groups of 256 from the existing citation, venue, and repository lists and extract them with the current v3 extractor.

options.A:
Goal: Recover complete PDE, condition, and solution tuples from real arXiv papers for the FEX training bank.

Plan: Cut every rendered math span from each paper with a rule-based TeX parser. Send each span to gpt-5.6-terra and ask whether that span is a governing PDE, a boundary or initial condition, or a solution, and which other spans it pairs with. On the 16 already opened papers, run Sonnet 5 over the same 181 equation spans without showing it the first model's labels, and report per-field precision and recall with exact span readback. Ask GPT-5.5 to critique one prompt revision. If that independent pass reaches precision 1.0 and recall of at least 0.80, apply the same per-span questions to 16 new tutorial and lecture papers.
options.B:
Goal: Recover complete PDE, condition, and solution tuples from real arXiv papers for the FEX training bank.

Plan: Send each paper's full TeX source to gpt-5.6-terra or Sonnet 5 in one call. Ask the model to list every PDE, domain and conditions, and solution tuple in a fixed schema, and to fill fields that the paper leaves incomplete. Ask GPT-5.5 to critique the prompt, then test that prompt on four already opened papers, and require each accepted field to cite exact source bytes. Keep model-completed fields out of the real train and eval banks. If tuple precision is 1.0 and recall is at least 0.80 on those four papers, apply the same prompt to 16 new tutorial and lecture papers whose identifiers are chosen from metadata before the TeX is read.

options.A:
Goal: Prepare the pretrained versus no-pretrain comparison by compiling more of the current real-source equations.

Plan: Increase the allowed expression tree depth and operators so more of the equations that were already extracted can compile. Replay the current GitHub and arXiv banks through that compiler, keep the labels from the current extraction pipeline, and split train and evaluation by source repository. Start the pretrained versus no-pretrain comparison on this replayed bank when the split counts pass.
options.B:
Goal: Prepare the pretrained versus no-pretrain comparison by collecting more real PDE examples.

Plan: Collect more real PDEs from documented papers, tutorials, and code repositories until training and evaluation meet the existing row, repository, template, and action counts. Take each label from the written solution formula in the source, not from nearby prose. Start the pretrained versus no-pretrain comparison after that bank is in place.

options.A:
Goal: Calibrate the FEX search baseline on 11 real PDEs and then compare a pretrained controller with a same-architecture controller that has no pretraining.

Plan: Run R89a on the 11 source-native PDEs with the same cells, seeds, threshold, and budgets, including 1000 and 2000 steps on the Adam 100, BFGS 100, and weight 10 arm. Read the next real sources from a preset source list. Append only rows whose labels come from the source formulas, and rerun the R89e train and evaluation gates on that bank. Build 64-dimensional features from the operator, the domain, and the conditions for every training row. Build executable packets of the original PDE, boundary conditions, and initial conditions for every evaluation row. Launch R89f when R89a, the new bank gate, and this feature and runtime bridge all pass. Compare pretrained FEX with the same architecture with no pretraining.
options.B:
Goal: Calibrate the FEX search baseline on 11 real PDEs and then compare a pretrained controller with a same-architecture controller that has no pretraining.

Plan: Run R89a on the 11 source-native PDEs with depth-4 trees, threshold 1e-3, and three seeds. Cross Adam 20 plus BFGS 20 with Adam 100 plus BFGS 100, and cross condition weight 100 with condition weight 10, at budgets 200 and 500. Extend the Adam 100, BFGS 100, and weight 10 arm to budgets 1000 and 2000. If that arm solves at least 3 of 11 PDEs at budget 500, stop the ladder at budget 500. Add real PDEs until the bank gains 7 extra strict rows and the train count of 40 and the evaluation count of 20 both pass. Use the 20-dimensional feature vectors from the R89d controller check as training inputs, and use the R89d runtime contract as evaluation packets. If the combined arm meets the solve gate and the bank counts pass, launch R89f as pretrained FEX versus the same architecture with no pretraining.

options.A:
Goal: Find out whether a pretrained real-source controller beats the same network with no pretraining on a 20-row held-out comparison after the depth-lock study and the training split.

Plan: Complete the depth-6 versus depth-4-lock study with the same controller, seeds, objective, and optimizer. Save every proposal, the action probabilities, and the exact-tree refits under both masks. Complete the 27-row training versus evaluation split, and run the depth-6 64-dimensional check whose only arm difference is loading pretrained weights. Train on the frozen 46 training rows and 20 evaluation rows plus accepted training rows. Compare the pretrained controller with the same network with no pretraining on the 20 held-out rows, using source-native objectives and intervals grouped by source and PDE.
options.B:
Goal: Find out whether the local runtime matches the authors' FEX example and whether real features predict source trees before a 20-row pretrained search comparison.

Plan: Pin the authors' Finite-expression-method code at the reference revision. On one authors' example, run a short CPU trajectory in both codebases with the same topology, actions, collocation points, coefficient start, Adam and LBFGS settings, reward, and policy loss, and record every difference. Train a supervised model on training-only rows and 64-dimensional solution-independent features under a repository and template holdout. Score that model against an action-frequency baseline and a feature-shuffled baseline on cross-entropy, tree accuracy, top-k recall, and calibration. Start the 20-row pretrained search comparison only if the supervised model beats both baselines.

options.A:
Goal: Collect real-source PDE training records from documented external examples.

Plan: Take the DeepXDE 1D Poisson problem on [-1, 1], with residual π² sin(πx) and solution sin(πx). Open the source file, copy the PDE and solution quotes with byte offsets, build depth-6 labels from the formula, compute 64-dimensional operator features, and run the training-record validator. Add the record to the training bank only after that check passes, and collect each later real-source PDE by the same steps.
options.B:
Goal: Use the extracted source rows as the training set for the next controller tests.

Plan: Take the 46 training rows and the 20 held-out rows from the latest source expansion, and the accepted pairs from the 27-row readjudication. Compute 64-dimensional features and depth-6 labels from these rows. Train the controller on this set and compare it with the exact same architecture that does not load the prior, on the same held-out PDEs.

options.A:
Goal: Instantiate depth2_rml controllers with hidden width 1 and collect the additional real templates that this topology needs before the next training run.

Plan: Build new treatment and control controllers as depth2_rml networks with hidden width 1. Collect additional real templates until the bank holds at least 57,200 distinct occupied decisions, which needs at least 11,433 new templates if each template adds one tuple. Later training and learnability runs use only these new controllers.
options.B:
Goal: Train a structural prior on the current official-representable rows and compare treatment against control on the four frozen real evaluation PDEs.

Plan: Train three checkpoints for 200 epochs on the ten rows that compile under the current depth2_sub controller with hidden width 50. Save the matching pre-load twins as the controls. Then run each of the four frozen real PDEs with the registered full search budgets, three paired seeds, and source-native objectives.

options.A:
Goal: Give a G3 bridge from the restricted two-arm witness to the FEX Poisson controller on the full depth-2 action space.

Plan: Write a bridge proposition that lists assumptions for percentile selection, inner coefficient fitting, and product-policy gradients. Enumerate all 2187 depth2_sub templates of the Poisson grammar. Run a 12-seed sweep of the product, jointnorm, and joint-tabular controllers on this full action space, and record collision probability and slot-gradient conflict. Then run a 10-seed reward-gap sweep on subsets of size 16 and 64 from the same grammar.
options.B:
Goal: Give a four-gate discoverability theorem that applies to symbolic-regression search systems.

Plan: Write a theorem on a search system given by a grammar, a sound rewrite relation, a policy, and a coefficient loss. Prove that class exposure, policy-gradient geometry, and coefficient feasibility can fail independently under stated conditions. Give constructive witnesses in this abstract setting. Then record how the existing FEX quotient recurrence, e-graph containment result, and two-arm G3 witness instantiate the theorem.

options.A:
Goal: Measure whether marginal-dominance forecasts match FEX controller search traces.

Plan: Run the FEX controller on a Poisson target with the depth-two grammar, the operator set of each slot, residual reward, and coefficient fitting. Record slot probabilities, gradient norms, and the time to hit a good class. Score the reward table of that run with the original action counts, and compare the forecast with the recorded traces.
options.B:
Goal: Measure how often the marginal-dominance corner conditions pass on stored FEX reward tables.

Plan: Read the existing per-class FEX reward cache. Cut each reward table into slices that keep two actions per slot. Score every slice on MD0, MD1, MD2, and the corner linear program. Report the pass rate at each level, and write a mapping note that treats each expression-tree slot as a two-action product-softmax factor.

options.A:
Goal: State a class-exposure lower bound and a link from that bound to two-action policy-gradient geometry.

Plan: Write a lower bound on the expected number of trials for a reward-blind sampler to hit a good quotient class. Add a tightness argument and extend the bound to non-uniform sampling. Write a result that relates this waiting time to the time of a policy-gradient model that uses two actions in each slot. Give a bound and a counterexample for the gap between that two-action model and a model with more actions in each slot.
options.B:
Goal: Measure whether the FEX controller finds a good expression on a Poisson equation.

Plan: Run the FEX controller with a multilayer perceptron and sequential tree generation on a Poisson equation. Use action sizes 9, 3, 9, and 9 at the four slots. Log logits, gradient norms, slot probabilities, and the time to hit a good quotient class. Compare that time with a blind sampler on the same classes, and compare the logged path with the two-action marginal-dominance predictions.

options.A:
Goal: Prove the class-exposure bound and the G2 to G3 bridge for the FEX depth-2 nine-operator grammar.

Plan: Restore the G3 proof files that are missing from this branch. Mark the factored-bridge lemma as conditional. Use the blind-sampler formulas on this grammar, with 1539 classes, one good class, and expected discovery time 770, as the class-exposure theorem. Use a two-action product-softmax proxy to place this grammar in the regime where blind sampling is slow and policy-gradient geometry can still succeed. Record these FEX depth-2 numbers and the proxy placement as the Version 7 theorems.
options.B:
Goal: Prove that discoverability factors into independent dimensions for any symbolic regression system that meets named conditions.

Plan: Write a list of conditions X that a symbolic regression search system must satisfy. Prove that under those conditions, the gap from an expression existing to a controller finding it splits into independent dimensions, including quotient relevance, class exposure, policy-gradient geometry, and coefficient feasibility. Prove that none of these dimensions implies another. Give the FEX depth-2 grammar with nine operators and the 1539-class count as a numerical example of this statement.

options.A:
Goal: Test the frequency prior on the current single-frequency Helmholtz and convection-diffusion problems.

Plan: Use a depth-two expression tree and two-dimensional single-frequency manufactured PDEs with uniform samples. Remove the true solution from the Gate 2 frequency check. Repeat the clean, decoy, contamination, and prior-width tests on the 7-pi Helmholtz, 8-pi Helmholtz, and two-dimensional convection-diffusion cases. Collect a full target-frequency probability trajectory on the convection-diffusion case.
options.B:
Goal: Test the frequency prior on multi-frequency, nonlinear, and nonuniform PDEs.

Plan: Raise the expression tree to depth three so a two-frequency Helmholtz problem can be written. First test whether a fixed two-frequency expression can reach low error, then run standard search and oracle-soft search on that problem. Run a nonlinear PDE whose solution spectrum and right-hand-side spectrum differ, and run an estimator test with nonuniform samples. Remove the true solution from the Gate 2 frequency check and use residual fitting on these runs.

options.A:
Goal: Measure the paired AIC gap at one large-n cell on the R35 prediction line.

Plan: Run one cell at gap 0.18, n 4096, and noise 0.003, with 5 master seeds and 500 bootstrap replicates. Reuse the existing lambda overrides for this cell. Pool the paired absolute AIC difference across the 5 seeds and report the 90 percent interval. Compare that mean with the R35 power-law value 0.0272 at gap 0.18. Send the next workshop version after this cell is collected.
options.B:
Goal: Send the next workshop version on the synthetic evidence that is already collected.

Plan: Keep the 27-cell label-swap fallback table, the 51-cell finite-n sign record, and the R35 per-gap power-law fit as the main numbers. Report the stopped R39 and R41 partial chunks only as extra sign checks. Add deprecation notes at the closed-form theory section and at the real-data claim in the proposal. Then send this version for workshop review.

options.A:
Goal: Check the R35 power-law prediction with the gap=0.18 cell at n=4096 as a paired primary-versus-fallback test.

Plan: Use the five-seed pooled mean absolute AIC delta of 0.0480, with a 90 percent CI from 0.0328 to 0.0680. Divide 0.0480 by the R35 prediction 0.0272 at n=10^4. Record a pass if the ratio is in [0.5, 2.0], and record a miss only if the mean is above 0.082. Write 0.0523 at n=1536, 0.0480 at n=4096, and 0.0272 at n=10^4 as a monotone decay chain. Use this n=4096 result as the paired check of the large-n floor.
options.B:
Goal: Check the R35 power-law prediction with a gap=0.18 paired primary-versus-fallback test at n=1024, and read the n=4096 cell for primary excess.

Plan: Use the five-seed pooled mean absolute AIC delta of 0.0480, with a 90 percent CI from 0.0328 to 0.0680. Read the five master-seed label-swap excess values on the n=4096 cell. If every seed is -1.0 with zero spread, report 0.0480 as the distance of primary excess from -1.0. Use the gap=0.18 cell at n=1024 with 25 master seeds as the paired primary-versus-fallback test of the R35 direction. Keep the n=4096 value 0.0480 as the primary excess at large n.

options.A:
Goal: Use the label-swap fallback as the main estimand and take finite-n magnitude from the R29, R34, and R42 cells.

Plan: Keep the label-swap symmetrized fallback as the main estimand. Read finite-n magnitude from the existing R29 25-seed n=1024 paired-bootstrap interval, the R34 n=1536 point, and the R42 n=4096 point, all at gap 0.18. Use the R42 ratio to the R35 power-law prediction as the large-n check. Send the next review with no new cell.
options.B:
Goal: Use the label-swap fallback as the main estimand and take finite-n magnitude from a new n=2048 paired cell.

Plan: Keep the label-swap symmetrized fallback as the main estimand. Launch a gap=0.18 n=2048 cell with several master seeds. Measure the paired primary-versus-fallback difference on that cell and use it as the finite-n magnitude. Record the R42 n=4096 point as a large-n consistency check.

options.A:
Goal: Measure the paired primary and label-swap AIC delta at gap 0.18, sigma 0.003, and n=2048, then send Version 6.

Plan: Aggregate the 500 R28 chunk files that already exist for this cell and 5 master seeds, using the same paired-bootstrap method as R29. Report the pooled mean of the absolute AIC delta, the 90 percent interval, the sign on all 5 seeds, and the ratio of that mean to the R35 power-law value at n=2048. Count a ratio between 0.67 and 1.5 as a pass. Put this cell on the finite-n chain between n=1536 and n=4096. Send Version 6 after the aggregate file is written.
options.B:
Goal: Measure the paired primary and label-swap AIC delta at gap 0.40, sigma 0.10, and n=1024, then send Version 6.

Plan: Launch a chunk pool for this cell with 5 master seeds and 500 bootstraps. Draw those master seeds from outside the seed lists used in R28, R29, R34, and R42. After the chunks finish, compute the pooled mean of the absolute AIC delta and the 90 percent interval with the same paired-bootstrap method as R29. Report the 5-seed sign and the share of chunks where the label-swap value sits at the bound. Add this cell to the finite-n evidence at gap 0.40. Send Version 6 after the pool manifest is written.

options.A:
Goal: Measure current methods on the hidden test by using the five daily Kaggle submissions.

Plan: Turn methods that already run into competition notebooks, beginning with the public-checkpoint inference pipeline and other distinct baselines or variants. Submit five different notebooks or configs today, record the public score, private score, and rank for each, and keep filling the daily quota on following days while local training work continues.
options.B:
Goal: Finish the local outer-fold baseline chain first, then begin hidden-test submissions.

Plan: Continue the 50-epoch public-architecture retrain on outer fold 0 until it finishes. After that run, compare matched component changes and the sparse-supervision and temporal-association pilots on the same fold. After those local pilots are collected, start offline notebooks and hidden Kaggle submissions as the later generalization stage.

options.A:
Goal: Retrain the public TemporalUNet3D, Node Transformer, and ILP pipeline in five-epoch segments on the first embryo-held-out fold to obtain a matched public baseline.

Plan: After the official data, metric, and embryo-fold contracts are in place, write a development split inside the training embryo and measure step time on two or three GPUs. Train the public architecture for five epochs, stop, and inspect loss, recall, node count, and sample plots. If loss is falling and recall is not near zero, resume from the checkpoint to 20 epochs, inspect again, and then resume toward 50, with each segment limited to 6 hours and a resume checkpoint.
options.B:
Goal: Retrain the public TemporalUNet3D, Node Transformer, and ILP pipeline for 50 epochs on the first embryo-held-out fold to obtain a matched public baseline.

Plan: After the official data, metric, and embryo-fold contracts are in place, run a short job on two samples that lasts at most 30 minutes, then train the public architecture from scratch for 50 epochs with seed 0 on one GPU. Treat this retrain as one job with a budget of 18 to 36 GPU hours. After all 50 epochs finish, cache the predicted nodes and edge scores, and then run the detector, association, and solver comparisons on that cache.

options.A:
Goal: Measure how synthetic root hubs and off-volume forks change the hidden Kaggle score with the rest of today's submission slots.

Plan: Reuse the R3 kernel v3 prediction file and do not rerun detection or association. The two submissions already sent today are that file with a root hub and five forks placed outside the imaged volume. Fill the last three daily slots with the clean file, the same file with a root hub and zero forks, and the same file with a root hub and ten forks. Save each file hash and public score as the hidden-metric readout of those graph transforms.
options.B:
Goal: Measure how different detectors and association settings change the hidden Kaggle score with the rest of today's submission slots.

Plan: The two submissions already sent today used the R3 public checkpoint notebook. Fill the last three daily slots with the collected R2 DoG and Hungarian baseline, the R3 public checkpoint at a different detection threshold, and the R3 public checkpoint with a different motion gate. Write those three prediction files locally and compare their in-volume node and edge rows before sending them. Save each public score as the hidden-metric readout of that method.

options.A:
Goal: Measure the association quality of the clean public-architecture retrain and continue that training for five more epochs.

Plan: Load the R7 epoch-2 checkpoint and run full predict, solve, and official evaluate on the 27 inner-dev samples to obtain edge Jaccard, official score, and division Jaccard. Resume from the epoch-5 checkpoint and train epochs 6 to 10 with the same 3-GPU configuration, and run the same full graph evaluation after every epoch. For the day's five Kaggle submissions, send the R7 epoch-2 checkpoint, the R7 epoch-5 checkpoint, an R3 edge-threshold variant, an R3 and R7 ensemble, and an R7 epoch-10 or non-maximum-suppression variant.
options.B:
Goal: Reproduce the 0.913 and 0.914 public-notebook cluster and measure how much of that score comes from a clean inference pipeline.

Plan: Freeze the exact source, inputs, and dependencies of the public notebooks that sit at 0.913 and 0.914 on the leaderboard. Run three matched Kaggle replays that differ in only one place: the exact clean no-hack notebook, one high-cluster notebook, and that same high-cluster notebook with negative-time or out-of-volume nodes turned off. Compare the visible submission files and the hidden scores of these arms with the current 0.877 public-weight chain.

options.A:
Goal: Continue self-training of the public architecture and use the next hidden submissions for the current 0.877 pipeline.

Plan: Use the remaining daily Kaggle submissions on the R7 epoch-2 and epoch-5 checkpoints. Also submit detection-threshold and ensemble variants of the public TemporalUNet3D pipeline that scores 0.877 on the hidden test. Resume the R7 run from epoch 10 on the 27 validation samples from the held-out embryo, and train the next 5-epoch segment with three GPUs. After each epoch, compute official score, adjusted edge Jaccard, and division Jaccard. If those graph scores rise, continue R7 in later 5-epoch segments and then ablate association and ILP on fixed candidate nodes.
options.B:
Goal: Reproduce the 0.913 public notebook method and evaluate it together with the current 0.877 pipeline on the official metric.

Plan: Download the public notebooks and checkpoints that produce the 0.913 leaderboard group and the 0.877 leaderboard group. Keep their original source, weights, and post-process code. Replay the 0.913 notebook as published. Replay the 0.877 public checkpoint with the extra test-time and tracking steps taken from the 0.913 notebooks. Score both replays with the official metric on the 27 validation samples from the held-out embryo, and submit both replays to the hidden leaderboard. Record the finished R7 official scores as the self-trained reference on the same split.

options.A:
Goal: Measure whether the public checkpoint with TTA, ILP, and the extra post-processing steps reaches the 0.913 leaderboard cluster on hidden test.

Plan: Build a Kaggle kernel that loads the public support-pack checkpoint and runs TTA, ILP, gap close, short-track filtering, and line-fit. Submit that kernel on the next hidden slot. Take a hidden score between 0.908 and 0.918 as a match to the 0.913 cluster from this checkpoint and this pipeline. Use the local public-checkpoint score of 0.918 on 27 validation samples as the expected range.
options.B:
Goal: Locate the exact public notebook whose linked submission sits in the 0.912 to 0.914 leaderboard cluster.

Plan: Search Kaggle discussion threads and saved historical kernel versions for a source whose linked submission score is in 0.912 to 0.914. Compare that source with the no-hack notebook that already scores 0.908. Record whether the extra points come from tracking post-processing or from a graph-augmentation step that changes the division Jaccard term. If the live kernel version does not match, recover the historical script version that owns a 0.912 or 0.914 receipt.

options.A:
Goal: Identify the public notebook method that scores 0.913 to 0.914 on the leaderboard and reproduce it on hidden data.

Plan: Search the Kaggle discussion forum and public notebooks for kernels whose linked submissions score 0.913 or 0.914. Compare those kernels with the R10 source audit, which currently ties exact sources only to 0.908, 0.885, and 0.884. For a candidate in that score cluster, record the kernel version, the attached datasets, and the submission that is linked to that source. Write down the inference and post-processing steps in that notebook. Submit the same notebook on the hidden leaderboard.
options.B:
Goal: Reach the 0.913 leaderboard cluster by training the current public checkpoint and the R7 run for more epochs.

Plan: Fine-tune the public 50-epoch checkpoint for 5 epochs on the full training data from both embryos. Use detection weight 10, division weight 1, time window 2, and half of the public learning rate. Resume the R7 run from epoch 9 and train 10 more epochs at half learning rate. Score each new checkpoint on the local official metric. If a checkpoint scores above the local public result of 0.918, attach it to the current inference pipeline and submit it on the hidden leaderboard.

options.A:
Goal: Find how much of the 0.028 score gap to the 0.908 public fork comes from the motion-relink and safe-division kernels that are already built.

Plan: Record the R22 public-notebook fork hidden score of 0.908 as the current public control. Treat the old 0.913 leaderboard group as gone after the division-metric patch. At the next daily hidden quota, submit the five visible-complete kernels R26, R29a, R29b, R29c, and R29d. After those hidden scores arrive, compute the score change of motion relink, safe division, their interaction, and the patched augment variants against R19a at 0.880. After that analysis, take a user choice among a new checkpoint, a new post-process, or an ensemble as the next C3 path.
options.B:
Goal: Find how the public 0.913 score is produced, and test two owned single-factor changes on that control.

Plan: Record the R22 public-notebook fork hidden score of 0.908. Also copy the public dual-seed plus frame-retention notebook that still reports 0.913 and has no active exploit primitive. On the same samples, TTA, thresholds, and evaluator, run three local arms that turn on single seed, then dual-seed blend, then the frame-retention guard. On the dual-seed control, run one arm that rescues primary-only candidates on low-retention frames when a neighbor frame supports them within 6.5 µm, and one arm that turns on DeepCenter safe-division veto at threshold 0.12. At the next daily hidden quota, submit the same five kernels R26, R29a, R29b, R29c, and R29d, and keep those scores for the motion-relink and safe-division analysis.

options.A:
Goal: Measure an anisotropic 3D U-Net, a windowed association Transformer, and an Ultrack cue tracker on one split and the official metric.

Plan: Train an anisotropic 3D U-Net on sparse cell centers, infer nodes, and score the graph with the official metric. Train a windowed association Transformer on fixed candidate nodes, predict edges, and score the graph with the official metric. Fit intensity and DoG cues on the training movies, run Ultrack on the development movies, and score the graph with the official metric. Use the same four training movies and the same four development movies for all three methods. Write a legal submission file from each method after the first train and infer cycle.
options.B:
Goal: Measure how PU losses and training scope change official scores on the TemporalUNet3D tracker.

Plan: Keep the TemporalUNet3D detector, the Node Transformer, and the ILP graph solver. Split the training objective into BCE with fixed class weights, legacy weighted PU, standard uPU, and standard nnPU. On a short train from one fixed checkpoint, record the first update where the non-negative correction becomes active. Start all later runs from that same checkpoint. Train the full model and the association head only under each objective, on two embryos and two seeds. Score every run with the official metric and record the scores by training scope and by objective.

options.A:
Goal: Send five prepared hidden submissions at the start of the quota day.

Plan: During the preceding day, build seven cores that differ from all past submissions. At 22:30Z, set a fill order that places any new U core, V-distance core, and X-flat core first if each can produce a legal test-format submission, then fills remaining slots from the knob variants margin050, edge_weight005, edge_weight030, edge_weight020, edge_threshold050, margin020, and edge052. After 00:00:30Z, submit five arms once each in that order under a single owner. Keep that order unchanged when the preceding day's public scores arrive. Collect five unique refs with one attempt each.
options.B:
Goal: Send five hidden submissions at spaced decision times during the quota day.

Plan: Keep all five slots unused from 00:00Z to 06:00Z. At 06:00Z, 12:00Z, 18:00Z, 21:00Z, and 23:15Z, send at most one new arm after reading the latest local and public scores. Leave unused slots open for same-day U, V, and X results until 22:30Z. After 22:30Z, fill leftover slots from backups that have a closed local loop, a distinct prediction file, a passing test-format run, and a card that states the question, why the slot is used, and how the score will change the next choice.

options.A:
Goal: Set the next round of route experiments on the existing train4 and dev4 split.

Plan: Run a new two-by-two on the 0.913 dual-seed Temporal U-Net and Node Transformer pipeline. The first factor uses dual-seed z-flip or primary-only z-flip. The second factor uses the learned post-processing or the geometry post-processing. Build new detections and new graph solves on the existing matched samples. Compare the combined cell with the current primary-only local score. Train the anisotropic 3D U-Net detector as its own named route on one GPU with this split and the official metric. Train the shifted-window detector as a second named route on the same GPU, split, and metric.
options.B:
Goal: Set the next round of route experiments on the existing train4 and dev4 split.

Plan: Run a traditional DoG and Hungarian calibration. Run an Ultrack solve that uses public image cues and no count prior. Open a Query Tracker association run on nodes that are already computed. Put a convolutional detector and a shifted-window detector in one group named U, and train them together as a same-device architecture and padding factorial. For the 0.913 dual-seed Temporal U-Net and Node Transformer pipeline, repair the daily submission controller and fill the missing primary-reflection and guard-off cell in the existing submission bank. Give T, U, X, and E each a successor run after the first batch.

options.A:
Goal: Test whether a voxel PU objective improves the anisotropic 3D U-Net over the dense control.

Plan: Train the anisotropic 3D U-Net on all training videos with labelled-centre voxel positives, unlabeled samples from the train embryo grid, and three class-prior values, and train a dense control with the same host and seed. Keep checkpoints at 40, 120, 300, and 600 steps. For each objective, sweep threshold, peak spacing, and peak cap on the training videos, keep the selected setting, and then read the held-out embryo once.
options.B:
Goal: Test whether a voxel PU objective improves the anisotropic 3D U-Net over the dense control.

Plan: Train the anisotropic 3D U-Net with a voxel PU objective for 40 to 120 steps on three training videos, hold out the fourth training video, and compare it with a dense control on that held-out video. If official score and centre rank both beat the control, train all training videos and continue to 300 and 600 steps. Choose the operating point on the training videos and then read the held-out embryo once.

options.A:
Goal: Find the first source of the parent-score gap, and test whether legal binary nnPU beats same-host dense BCE on the anisotropic 3D U-Net.

Plan: Run the parent identity comparison on all 54 matched samples in one launch. At the same time, train four U-Net runs on the current train split: dense BCE and legal binary nnPU at half, full, and double the recorded class prior, with checkpoints at 40, 120, 300, and 600 steps. When every run has finished, sweep threshold, NMS, and peak cap on train, then read the held-out dev split once.
options.B:
Goal: Find the first source of the parent-score gap, and test whether legal binary nnPU beats same-host dense BCE on the anisotropic 3D U-Net.

Plan: First compare parent identity on two samples, one from each embryo, and train one legal nnPU run plus one dense BCE run for 40 and 120 steps on one train fold. Read official score, labelled-center rank, and the positive-class share of risk. Expand the parent check to all 54 samples only if the two-sample identity run recovers the parent score. Expand nnPU to the half, full, and double prior grid and to 300 and 600 steps only if the short reading shows a visible positive-class term and beats dense BCE on rank and official score. Then choose the operating point on train and read the held-out dev split once.

options.A:
Goal: Continue the 0.913 system, the traditional detector, and the U-Net as three routes, and split the daily Kaggle slots across those routes.

Plan: Measure the reverse-weight surface of the 0.913 system on matched54, and run a division diagnosis on those same graphs. Run the next traditional and U-Net tests as their own routes after the local scores that used only 44b6 samples. Submit each improved traditional and U-Net configuration for a first Kaggle test score. Use three of the five daily Kaggle slots on non-mainline routes and two slots on the current highest-score mainline.
options.B:
Goal: Open a division route on the 0.913 system and spend the remaining Kaggle slots on 0.913 variants.

Plan: Classify why the 0.913 graphs miss most ground-truth divisions. Sweep the geometric division gate on matched54. Also run the reverse-weight surface on matched54. Take one 6bba development read on the traditional detector and one on the U-Net. Assign the two remaining Kaggle slots to a harmonic-weight arm and a division-off arm of the 0.913 system.

options.A:
Goal: Choose the next T and V hidden packages from the notebook driver code in the repository.

Plan: For T, use a package that retries a failed sample with a per-frame threshold, then skips that sample and writes the rows that finished. For V, copy that same per-sample skip and partial write into the V notebook driver, which already accepts a sample list. Register each package from these driver edits and spend the next T hidden slot and the next V hidden slot on those packages.
options.B:
Goal: Choose the next T and V hidden packages from the exception in the Kaggle hidden rerun log.

Plan: Open the Kaggle kernel pages for R55t and R55v and read the hidden rerun log. The Kaggle command-line tool does not return this log. Use the exception class and the error text from that log to choose the next edit in the T notebook and the next edit in the V notebook. Spend the next T hidden slot and the next V hidden slot after that log has been read and each edit has been matched to the exception.

options.A:
Goal: Raise the current 0.913 Kaggle score by testing association changes and by getting official readings on the U and V routes.

Plan: Submit a copy of the public 0.915 and 0.916 notebook with no parameter change. On that parent, test local ranker on and off with three-frame lookahead on and off, and test the public harmonic-association method on and off. For U, measure predicted nodes over the GEFF estimate on each video and set a train-only per-movie node budget, then read the official score on the report videos. For V, collect the pending hidden outcome and choose the next arm from that reading.
options.B:
Goal: Complete the local cost ledger, receipts, file inventories, hashes, and owner account for this round.

Plan: Assign tasks that bind each run cost to a commit and write ledger lines from receipts. Add checks that evidence files and compact inventories stay in sync. Finish the owner listing fields, the count-scan coverage check, the round-end receipt, and the match between online submission refs and the owner account. If a receipt field, hash, or account line is missing, assign another task to fill it before a new scoring experiment starts.

options.A:
Goal: Measure the official score of an anisotropic 3D U-Net with channels 32, 64, and 128 against the traditional LoG detector.

Plan: Train the U-Net on the two-embryo holdout splits, with each embryo held out in turn. Run training in segments of at most 5.5 hours and save checkpoints at 2k, 5k, 10k, and 20k updates. Continue while the held-out embryo score still rises. Score the traditional LoG detector on the same movies and the same metric. Register a Kaggle card when the pooled score and both embryo scores, official and raw, all exceed the LoG scores.
options.B:
Goal: Measure the official score of the 600-step U-Net nodes under min-cost flow and Hungarian matching.

Plan: Keep the 600-step U-Net nodes with channels 8, 16, and 32, and keep their scores and node counts fixed. Score those nodes with Hungarian matching. Score the same nodes with two min-cost-flow backends, one with out-degree one and one with out-degree two. Set any division parameters on the train embryo only. Register a Kaggle card when an arm raises official score and raw edge on both embryos.

options.A:
Goal: Train a U-Net detector that has higher official and raw-edge scores than the traditional detector on the same local split.

Plan: Train an anisotropic 3D U-Net with channels 32, 64, and 128. Train on one embryo and score on the other, then swap the two embryos. Use dense BCE and learning rate 3e-4. Save the model and optimizer every 5.5 hours and keep training from those checkpoints until inner-dev official stops improving for two segments in a row. Score official and raw-edge on both embryos with the same association method used for the traditional detector. Build and submit a Kaggle package when U official and raw-edge scores are higher than that traditional detector on the pooled set and on each embryo.
options.B:
Goal: Test whether a linker that can make cell-division forks raises the official score of the current U-Net nodes.

Plan: Use the detections from the existing 600-update U-Net with channels 8, 16, and 32 as a fixed node set. Score those nodes with the current Hungarian matcher and with a min-cost flow that can give a parent two children. Choose the flow division radius and extra cost on the train embryo only. Report official, raw-edge, and division scores on both embryos. If the flow arm passes the local official and raw-edge gates on both embryos, pack those graphs and submit them as the U Kaggle entry.

options.A:
Goal: Find out whether an ILP division-topology change is still present in the graph that the official metric scores.

Plan: On a few videos, lower the division weight so the solver emits extra daughter edges. Compare the solver graph, the graph after motion relink, and the final scored graph, and record whether those extra edges are present in the scored output. Keep the detector and ordinary edges the same. If the extra edges are absent from the scored graph, locate the stage that replaces the solver edges. If they are present, run a middle-weight probe on those videos, and go to all 54 matched videos when division true positives and raw edge both rise.
options.B:
Goal: Find out whether a training-domain ILP division weight can raise scored division true positives on the public parent and the self parent.

Plan: On two videos, lower the division weight and confirm that the solver can emit forks and that a multi-child drop filter does not remove them. Then build division weights from second-daughter edge scores on the training embryo, and add the shipped weight and a zero-weight control. Keep the detector, ordinary edges, and motion relink the same. Run this set of weights on all 54 matched videos for the public parent and for the self parent. If a middle weight raises division true positives on both embryos, keep that weight as a hidden-submission candidate.

options.A:
Goal: Get official and raw scores for the two mainline single-factor cards on the four visible samples that have local ground truth.

Plan: Score the existing parent, secondary-source-off, and primary-retain-off outputs against the four local train ground-truth files with the official evaluator. Record official, raw edge, node adjustment, and division for each sample and both embryos. Read an official rise with no raw fall and no embryo conflict as a quality gain, and read an official rise that comes only from the node multiplier as a node-count effect.
options.B:
Goal: Get private-leaderboard scores for the two mainline single-factor cards on the public .916 parent.

Plan: Place the secondary-source-off card and the primary-retain-off card on today's two mainline private-leaderboard slots. These cards replay the exact .916 parent, change the final graphs on both embryos, and pass the submission eligibility checks. Use the private-leaderboard score as the official and raw reading for each card. Read a higher, equal, or lower private score as the removed factor being harmful, unnecessary, or helpful.

options.A:
Goal: Judge the size of the new R79 improvements and choose which interventions to turn into visible packages.

Plan: Read the official scores of the mainline restore runs and the U-Net Hungarian gate-7 run on the same 54 samples. For add-only, re-parent-only, joint restore, and gate-7, record the official-score lifts +0.004831, +0.022225, +0.028112, and +0.008358 against their own controls. For the same four runs, record the error-rate reduction as each lift divided by one minus the control official score on those samples. Use the error-rate reduction as the measure of improvement size. Build a visible package for each mainline single action that is positive on both embryos.
options.B:
Goal: Judge the size of the new R79 improvements and choose which interventions to turn into visible packages.

Plan: Read the official scores of the mainline restore runs and the U-Net Hungarian gate-7 run on the same 54 samples. For add-only, re-parent-only, joint restore, and gate-7, record the official-score lifts +0.004831, +0.022225, +0.028112, and +0.008358 against their own controls. Use these official-score lifts as the measure of improvement size, and place gate-7's +0.008358 and add-only's +0.004831 on that same absolute scale when you rank size. Build a visible package for each mainline single action that is positive on both embryos.

options.A:
Goal: Choose the next particle-filter experiment from the hidden score of the 500-particle 192-seed config.

Plan: After the daily quota reset, submit five notebooks: the 500-particle 192-seed particle-filter config, the full-data GBDT stack, a selector warmup blend, a selector smooth variant, and a 500-particle 256-seed or two-config ensemble. Begin the remaining four folds of the 500-particle 192-seed config only if that hidden score is below 8.582. If the hidden score is 8.582 or worse, record a negative config result and then run a well-level failure analysis on the saved fold-0 predictions. Keep other local particle-filter studies off until the hidden score is known.
options.B:
Goal: Collect new local particle-filter evidence on the same day as the five hidden-score submissions.

Plan: After the daily quota reset, submit five notebooks from the current particle-filter assets, including the 500-particle 192-seed config, the GBDT stack, selector variants, and a two-config ensemble. Begin the remaining four folds of the 500-particle 192-seed config on local CPU, together with the 256-particle 64-seed aggressive config. Run the well-level error analysis on the saved fold-0 particle-filter predictions, grouping wells by particle spread, well length, and GR gaps. Test a well-wise mix of the two profiles using an out-of-fold threshold on particle spread.

options.A:
Goal: Score the current particle-filter and GBDT candidates on the current leaderboard, and start the next local runs after those scores are known.

Plan: Package five Kaggle submissions: the 500-particle 192-seed particle filter, the full-data GBDT stack, the selector warmup variant, the selector smooth variant, and a 500-particle 256-seed or two-config mix. Submit them after the daily quota resets, then wait for the scores. If the 500-particle 192-seed leaderboard score is below 8.582 ft, run the remaining grouped validation folds of that config. If that score is 8.582 ft or higher, record a negative result and then run a well-level failure analysis to choose a new direction.
options.B:
Goal: Score the current particle-filter and GBDT candidates on the current leaderboard, and start the next local runs before those scores are known.

Plan: Package five Kaggle submissions: the 500-particle 192-seed particle filter, the full-data GBDT stack, the selector warmup variant, the selector smooth variant, and a 500-particle 256-seed or two-config mix. Submit them after the daily quota resets. At the same time, run the remaining grouped validation folds of the 500-particle 192-seed config and the 256-particle 64-seed config. Also run a well-level error analysis on the predictions that already exist, and use those failure modes to design the next particle-filter config mix.

options.A:
Goal: Measure whether F-Path-CFM and A-Track-Pointer beat the particle-filter selector on sealed fold 0.

Plan: Train each method with seeds 20260724, 20260725, and 20260726 using the same inputs, fold split, and compute budget. Compare each method with a matched deterministic control and with the R2 selector on pooled RMSE, signature bootstrap intervals, and catastrophic-well rate. If a gate fails, save reconstruction, rollout, and coverage diagnostics and repeat the same recipe on the same fold.
options.B:
Goal: Move the hidden leaderboard score by expanding the current particle-filter profiles across all five typewell-group folds.

Plan: Run the 500-particle 192-seed standard profile and the 256-particle 64-seed aggressive profile on folds 1 to 4, and form a 0.5/0.5 mean with the existing fold-0 files. On fold 0, assign each well one of those two profiles by an R2 particle-std threshold that is fit on folds 1 to 4. Collect public high-rank notebooks and discussion posts and turn unused particle-filter or stacking ideas into the next submission files.

options.A:
Goal: Test a whole-well two-dimensional alignment model on fold 0 as the next attempt to move about 2000 leaderboard ranks.

Plan: On fold 0 of the signature split, resample typewell GR, lateral GR, and trajectory into a two-dimensional heatmap and predict several path modes. Use the current selector as the comparison on the same wells. Score the selected mode and the average of the path modes with pooled RMSE, and add a GR shuffle control and a no-GR control. If fold 0 does not beat the selector by 0.20 ft, stop further work on this representation.
options.B:
Goal: Test F-Path-CFM and A-Track-Pointer on sealed fold 0 as the next attempt to move about 2000 leaderboard ranks.

Plan: On sealed fold 0, train F-Path-CFM on spline path residuals with conditional flow matching and endpoint error, and train A-Track-Pointer with typewell pointers, continuous offsets, and global re-anchoring. Use three seeds, matched deterministic controls, and the current selector on the same rows. Compare pooled RMSE with signature-cluster intervals, catastrophic-well rate, and boundary error. If a pre-gate fails, localize that implementation and continue the other route.

options.A:
Goal: Test whether jointly training the Rep-Translator and the shared LoRA can produce a K>1 depth gain.

Plan: Use the finished four-interface translator-only warm-up, where LoRA stayed at zero, as the no-LoRA Rep-Translator experiment. Next, on the existing FineWeb warmup data, train the Rep-Translator and the shared LoRA together with a K mix of 1, 2, and 4. Put the KL preservation term only on K=1 batches. Score held-out NLL at K values 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8, and compare that curve with the frozen-LoRA warm-up. After this joint pilot, run a Rep-Translator-only ablation in the later attribution stage.
options.B:
Goal: Test whether a no-LoRA Rep-Translator can translate Recurrent Block states so that K=1 and K=2 language loss stay close.

Plan: Train only the Interface-I Rep-Translator, with no LoRA modules and with all pretrained Qwen weights frozen. Compare the K=1 path of prelude, Recurrent Block, then coda with the K=2 path that inserts the translator between two Recurrent Block passes. Train that K=2 path with next-token loss only, with no KL term toward the K=1 distribution and no skip that copies the entry state. On a held-out set, record whether K=2 NLL stays close to K=1 NLL, and whether the translated state differs from the entry state.

options.A:
Goal: Test whether a representation translator with no LoRA can map loop-exit states back to usable loop-entry states.

Plan: Train only the Interface-I representation translator and add no LoRA modules. Keep every pretrained Qwen parameter frozen. Compare the K=1 path P then R then C with the K=2 path P then R then translator then R then C. Train with next-token loss at K=2 only, with no KL term toward the K=1 base output and no identity skip. On held-out data, measure next-token loss at K=1 and K=2. The pass condition is that K=2 stays close to K=1 and the translator output is not the entry state.
options.B:
Goal: Test whether training the representation translator together with shared recurrent LoRA produces a real depth gain at K>1.

Plan: Train the translator and the shared LoRA together on all four recurrence interfaces. Include a K=1 LoRA control and a direct-repeat control with no translator. First run a small overfit check on a fixed batch. Then run the joint training on the planned 20K nested supervised set. On held-out data, measure next-token loss at K=1, K=2, and K=4. The pass condition is that K=2 beats K=1 and K=4 improves further on K=2.

options.A:
Goal: Build the SFT pilot with a SWE slice of 2,000 unique issue groups.

Plan: Add a second source of SWE trajectories and keep the example length at 8192 tokens. Draw 2,000 unique issue groups from the combined sources. Build the 20,000-example pilot from 9,000 Math groups, 5,000 Science groups, 4,000 Instruction groups, and these 2,000 SWE groups. Keep 2,000 SWE groups in the later subsets that use 36,000 Math groups, 20,000 Science groups, and 16,000 Instruction groups.
options.B:
Goal: Build the SFT pilot with a SWE slice of 973 unique issue groups.

Plan: Keep the example length at 8192 tokens. Use the 973 unique SWE issue groups from the current source. Build the 18,973-example pilot from 9,000 Math groups, 5,000 Science groups, 4,000 Instruction groups, and these 973 SWE groups. Keep 973 SWE groups in the later subsets that use 36,000 Math groups, 20,000 Science groups, and 16,000 Instruction groups.

options.A:
Goal: Jointly train Rep-Translator and shared LoRA on the four interfaces after the translator-only warm-up.

Plan: Start each interface from its translator-only warm-up endpoint and insert a new shared LoRA with zero output. Train Rep-Translator and LoRA together for the full joint token budget. Use the same learning rate for both parameter groups on every joint step. Run this joint training on all four interfaces with the same token budget.
options.B:
Goal: Train Rep-Translator and shared LoRA in two-step and three-step schedules on the four interfaces after the translator-only warm-up.

Plan: Start each interface from its translator-only warm-up endpoint and insert a new shared LoRA with zero output. Train both modules together with a lower learning rate on the translator. In a three-step schedule, first train only LoRA with the translator weights at the warm-up values, then train both together with a lower learning rate on the translator. Use the same joint token budget on all four interfaces.

options.A:
Goal: Find out whether extra loop depth raises scores on the development and preservation benchmarks for the two-step routes.

Plan: Send one real sample from each registered benchmark through tokenize, forward, and score. If a required field is missing, or if the scores are all zero, all null, or all the same, the full panel stays unstarted. Measure items per second, report the wall-clock time, and score all options and all K values in one forward pass. Then run the II-twostep, IV-twostep, and I-twostep checkpoints taken at 25 percent and 100 percent of joint training with K = 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.
options.B:
Goal: Find out whether extra loop depth raises scores on the development and preservation benchmarks for the two-step routes.

Plan: Run the full panel on the II-twostep, IV-twostep, and I-twostep checkpoints taken at 25 percent and 100 percent of joint training. Use every registered development and preservation benchmark, and for each question evaluate K = 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8. Walk through the items in order and give each answer option its own forward pass at each K. Write per-item scores, option NLL values, and family macros from this run.

options.A:
Goal: Repair the panel scorer and then test one candidate on a small real-task set for a positive depth effect.

Plan: Correct the multiple-choice option span and replace the IFEval placeholder with the official verifier. Score one current candidate at K=1, 2, 4, and 8 on a small real-task subset that will not be used again for later confirmation. Run the full II, IV, and I panels on the 25 percent and 100 percent checkpoints only if that small set shows a positive depth effect.
options.B:
Goal: Repair the panel scorer and then run the full real-task panels for the current training routes.

Plan: Correct the multiple-choice option span and replace the IFEval placeholder with the official verifier. Score the Base model and the II checkpoint at K=1 and K=2 on all seven benchmarks to obtain chance, floor, and the smallest detectable K=1 versus K=2 difference. When those checks finish, run the full II, IV, and I panels at K=1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8 on the 25 percent and 100 percent checkpoints.

options.A:
Goal: Measure whether one depth candidate gains from extra recurrence steps on a small real-task split.

Plan: Let the three G10 depth-horizon training arms finish, and select the candidate with a G10 adjacent-depth proxy gain. Score that candidate at K equals 1, 2, 4, and 8 on a small held-out real-task split. Record the class-balanced paired macro intervals for K2 minus K1, K4 minus K2, and K8 minus K4, and record each preservation axis. Start the II, IV, I, and control panel matrix after those adjacent-depth intervals lie above zero and no preservation axis has an interval that excludes zero in the worse direction.
options.B:
Goal: Measure whether the II, IV, and I two-step routes beat K1 on the seven-benchmark development and preservation panel.

Plan: Finish the remaining production-equivalence and throughput checks on the current scoring path. Then run II-twostep, IV-twostep, and I-twostep at K equals 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8 on all seven development benchmarks and the preservation vector, using the joint 25 percent and 100 percent checkpoints. Keep the three G10 depth-horizon training arms running in parallel. Use these panel scores as the next evidence that extra recurrence depth helps on real tasks.

options.A:
Goal: Measure whether the current two-step routes beat K=1 on the full real-task panel.

Plan: When the scoring instrument, provenance, and power gates pass, run the full II, IV, and I two-step panels. Score all development benchmarks and the preservation vector at K=1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8 for the joint_025 and joint_100 checkpoints. If a benchmark is still at an empirical floor or the paired minimum detectable effect is larger than the observed K=1 versus K=2 gap, set the official task prompt on a held-out calibration split, rerun the full Base versus II K=1 and K=2 power panel, and then start this same three-route matrix.
options.B:
Goal: Measure whether one frozen candidate has a positive real-task depth signal on a disjoint pilot split.

Plan: When the scoring path is correct, freeze one trained candidate and score it at K=1, 2, 4, and 8 on a real-task split that does not overlap prompt calibration. Compute paired class-balanced macros for K=2 versus K=1, K=4 versus K=2, and K=8 versus K=4, and report the preservation axes. Start the full II, IV, and I panel matrix if those adjacent-depth 95 percent confidence interval lower bounds are all greater than zero, the four class K=8 versus K=1 point estimates are all at least zero, and no preservation axis has a 95 percent confidence interval that excludes zero against the candidate.

options.A:
Goal: Test whether extra recurrence depth helps after one change to training support, loop input, or loss, then score one passing model on a small real-task set.

Plan: Finish the three G10 schedule arms that share the same start point and data order. Start further arms that do not use each other's scores: one trains depths 1, 2, 3, 4, and 8, one gives the translator a signal for the current loop, and one adds a loss that compares only adjacent depths. Score every arm on the same 1,000-document proxy. Then choose a candidate and, if it passes the adjacent-depth gate, score it on the small real-task split that does not overlap prompt calibration.
options.B:
Goal: Test whether extra recurrence depth helps after a change to the training loss, then score one passing model on a small real-task set.

Plan: Finish the three G10 schedule arms that share the same start point and data order. If the replay arm and the equal-call deep-tail arm both fail the adjacent-depth gate on the 1,000-document proxy, start one follow-up arm that keeps the same start point, data, order, steps, and recurrent-block count and adds a next-token loss at every earlier depth. Wait for this follow-up arm to finish. Then choose a candidate from these runs and, if it passes the gate, score it on the small real-task split that does not overlap prompt calibration.

options.A:
Goal: Test whether a stronger loop-count input to the Translator can improve extra-loop next-token loss under the G20 depth-grid K schedule.

Plan: Keep the G20 depth-grid schedule and train on K=1, 2, 3, 4, and 8 with the same step, token, and call counts as that arm. Add a fixed loop-count feature to the Translator input at 5 percent of state RMS and at 15 percent of state RMS. Train those two signal arms on the shared Interface II route. After training, score extra-loop gain with held-out next-token loss at K=4 versus K=2 and at K=8 versus K=4.
options.B:
Goal: Test whether extra loops improve next-token loss when the Translator has no loop-count input and training uses only K=1, 2, and 4.

Plan: Train only on K=1, 2, and 4 with a three-stage schedule. In the first 20 percent of training, sample K=1 and K=2. In the remaining stages, sample K=1, 2, and 4, and keep at least 25 percent of batches at K=1 in every stage. Give the Translator no current-loop or depth feature. After training, evaluate K=1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8, and read K=3, 6, and 8 as untrained depths.

options.A:
Goal: Record training and inference MFU on the formal G26b config and continue B3 and B4 from the existing checkpoints.

Plan: Add effective FLOPs, timing windows, and MFU to the training and inference logs for the current B3 and B4 config. Run a short smoke that must show training MFU and inference MFU both above 60 percent. If the value is below 60 percent, change kernels or batching and run the smoke again. Then restart B3 from step 1766 and B4 from step 3163.
options.B:
Goal: Continue the B3 and B4 curriculum control trainings from the existing checkpoints and add MFU logging after those runs complete.

Plan: Restart B3 from step 1766 and B4 from step 3163 on the same host with the same data, curriculum, and optimizer. Keep the current step receipts that already log tokens per second and elapsed time. After these two arms finish, add MFU, effective FLOPs, and timing windows to the training and inference logs.

options.A:
Goal: Build a four-class real-task development set whose Base-K1 accuracy is about 50 percent.

Plan: Score the current six benchmarks with Base K1 and no adapter. Select whole task, subject, and official-difficulty strata by their calibration accuracy. Mix those strata so that the four-class development mean is between 45 and 55 percent, the 95 percent interval covers 50 percent, and each class mean is between 40 and 60 percent. If the current strata miss those bands, add more same-class benchmarks from the proposal list and repeat the Base-K1 calibration. Keep 256 rows in each of qa, science, math, and code after the bands are met.
options.B:
Goal: Build a four-class real-task development set that covers Base-K1 accuracies near 25 percent, 50 percent, and 75 percent.

Plan: Collect published or similar Base accuracies for each candidate benchmark and use those figures to choose which tasks to score. Score Base K1 with no adapter and assign strata to the 25, 50, and 75 percent bands, with more rows in the 50 percent band. Remove tasks whose Base accuracy is near chance or near ceiling. If a class-by-band cell is empty, add same-class benchmarks or official difficulty splits and score those. Keep at least 1024 development rows after the three bands are filled.

options.A:
Goal: Count the finished G26 curriculum arms as comparison endpoints, then run the four-class real-task selector.

Plan: Take the completed II-AdamW, II-Muon, state-hinge, B3, and B4 runs as the endpoints for this round. Apply the 60 percent MFU rule only to training jobs that start later. Score every endpoint at K = 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8 on the four-class development set with forced-option multiple-choice scoring and the official generation graders. Freeze one candidate with the original adjacent-depth real-task gates.
options.B:
Goal: Get training MFU and inference MFU above 60 percent on the formal configuration, then continue the real-task comparison.

Plan: Write effective FLOP counts, timing intervals, and MFU into the training and inference logs. Profile the formal training shape at K = 1, 2, and 4 and the formal inference batches. Change kernels, batching, or compile settings until both training MFU and inference MFU are above 60 percent on that configuration. Start new claim training and the five-endpoint real-task selector only after this MFU gate is met.

options.A:
Goal: Decide how the 30 percent MFU gate applies to multi-GPU training and mixed precision, and take the next training measurement.

Plan: Judge the finished two-rank DDP job by each rank's own MFU, and require every rank to exceed 0.30. Use the BF16 dense peak as the denominator on the G33 precision ladder, including the FP32 L0 to L3 rungs. Score those existing receipts with this per-rank BF16-peak rule. On the BF16 formal recipe, measure stage and kernel time from A1 to T0 on the same card, implement one exact kernel change that preserves output, loss, gradient, and update, and remeasure K equals 1, 2, and 4 twice. Count a K as a pass only when its per-rank MFU is above 0.30 with the BF16 dense peak.
options.B:
Goal: Decide how the 30 percent MFU gate applies to multi-GPU training and mixed precision, and take the next training measurement.

Plan: Judge the finished two-rank DDP job by one aggregate MFU. Use the sum of parsed model FLOPs across ranks, one shared steady-state wall window, and the sum of each device's dense peak at the arithmetic dtype that ran. When a rung uses FP32, put the FP32 dense peak in that denominator. Score the DDP receipt and the G33 FP32 L0 to L3 rungs with this formula. Run the FP32 recipe on the formal reference checkpoint at K equals 1, 2, and 4, twice each, with the same output, loss, gradient, and update checks. Count a K as a pass only when its MFU is above 0.30 with the dense peak of the dtype that ran.

options.A:
Goal: Determine how to pass the 30 percent training and inference MFU requirement.

Plan: Load the 2B and 4B formal models with the same recurrence and adapter layout used for 0.8B. Measure training MFU and inference MFU for both sizes, and record wall time and the semantic gates with each measurement. The 30 percent requirement is met if at least one of 0.8B, 2B, or 4B has both training MFU and inference MFU strictly above 0.30. Then choose the size with the shortest projected total training wall time, and run later development and science experiments on that size.
options.B:
Goal: Determine how to pass the 30 percent training and inference MFU requirement.

Plan: Work on the current 0.8B formal model. On training, measure the live BF16 path with the same output, loss, gradient, and update gates used for the FP32 candidate, and complete the skipped 32-step finite, resume, and held-out NLL trajectory. On inference, collect a new owned time profile after the fused decode change, and apply a joint-owner change only if every profiled cell has an MFU upper bound above 0.30. Start science runs only after this 0.8B candidate passes correctness, arithmetic, and the 0.30 MFU gate on both train and inference.

options.A:
Goal: Decide whether any of 0.8B, 2B, or 4B meets the training and inference MFU requirement, then choose the size with the shortest total training time.

Plan: Restore a declared inference source path. For 0.8B, 2B, and 4B, collect training MFU and inference MFU at K=1, K=2, and K=4. For each of these six cells, choose one reasonable batch size by the shortest end-to-end wall on a fixed workload, then take MFU from two fresh runs at that batch size. A size passes when all six cells are above 30 percent MFU. Then choose the passing size with the shortest total training wall.
options.B:
Goal: Decide whether any of 0.8B, 2B, or 4B meets the training and inference MFU requirement, then choose the size with the shortest total training time.

Plan: Restore a declared inference source path. For 0.8B, 2B, and 4B, collect training MFU at K=1, K=2, and K=4, and collect inference MFU for MCQ, generation, and joint at batch 32 and at batch 64. A size passes when each training K and each inference segment at both batch sizes is above 30 percent MFU on two fresh runs. Then choose the passing size with the shortest total training wall.

options.A:
Goal: Decide how the 30 percent MFU code gate is tested on the 0.8B, 2B, and 4B models after G40.

Plan: Restore source authority for inference, then measure six cells on each of 0.8B, 2B, and 4B: training and inference at K=1, 2, and 4. For each cell, choose one batch size that minimizes total wall time on a fixed workload, and score MFU on that batch size. A model passes when all six cells exceed 30 percent MFU. If more than one model passes, select the model with the shortest total training time. If no model passes, locate the failing cell.
options.B:
Goal: Decide how the 30 percent MFU code gate is tested on the 0.8B, 2B, and 4B models after G40.

Plan: Use the G40 result of zero passing sizes as the current code-gate contract. For training, stay on 4B with sequence length 8192 and microbatch 1, attribute K=4 non-GEMM time, and apply one owner change so that K=1, 2, and 4 all exceed 30 percent MFU. For inference, restore source authority, replay the 4B K=2 run at batch 32, and require MCQ, generation, and joint MFU all to exceed 30 percent. Then run batch 64 and require every batch cell to exceed 30 percent. A size passes when training at all K and inference at all segments and batches exceed 30 percent.

options.A:
Goal: Test whether extra recurrence depth improves quality when training covers every depth from K=1 through K=8.

Plan: Run two training arms that share one initialization, one data order, one token budget, and one Recurrent Block call budget. One arm samples K=1, K=2, and K=4. The other arm samples every integer K from 1 to 8. The Translator input contains no loop index. The training loss has no KL term that matches a K>1 output to the K=1 output. At each depth from 1 to 8, report adjacent NLL, real-task scores, and how well the Translator output serves as the next Recurrent Block input.
options.B:
Goal: Test whether extra recurrence depth improves quality after training on K=1, K=2, and K=4.

Plan: Train the Translator and the shared LoRA with the staged curriculum that samples only K=1, K=2, and K=4. Use the current next-token objective and the K=1 preservation term. After training, evaluate K=1, K=2, K=3, K=4, K=6, and K=8. Treat K=3, K=6, and K=8 as a check on depths that were not sampled in training. Report adjacent-depth NLL and real-task scores at each of these depths.

options.A:
Goal: Measure training and inference MFU for the 0.8B, 2B, and 4B models at K equals 1, 2, and 4 on a 16-update workload, and then score the six-cell MFU gate on those measurements.

Plan: Keep the pinned Qwen3.5 Base checkpoints, BF16, sequence length 8192, and Interface II. For each model size and each of those K values, pick a candidate micro-batch size that fits in memory and change only gradient accumulation so that tokens and steps per update stay the same. Run 16 updates, stop after the registered steady timing window, and report MFU from two new processes on the training side and on the inference side. A model size passes if its six cells are all strictly above 0.30, and one passing size is enough for the code gate. Give each training-size run this 16-update workload and then exit.
options.B:
Goal: Measure which micro-batch size gives the shortest full-curriculum training wall for the 0.8B, 2B, and 4B models at K equals 1, 2, and 4, and then score the six-cell MFU gate on those batch sizes.

Plan: Keep the pinned Qwen3.5 Base checkpoints, BF16, sequence length 8192, and Interface II. For each model size and each of those K values, time candidate micro-batch sizes on the full curriculum of 3598 steps at K equals 1, 4386 steps at K equals 2, and 2544 steps at K equals 4. Change only gradient accumulation so that tokens and steps per update stay the same. Choose the batch size with the lowest complete-training total wall, then start two new processes at that batch size and report MFU together with the summed curriculum wall. Run the same full-workload batch search for inference. A model size passes if its six selected-batch cells are all strictly above 0.30. Give each training-size run a budget of 3 A800 hours.

options.A:
Goal: Set the training optimizer after the physical batch size is chosen.

Plan: First choose the physical batch size that gives the shortest end-to-end wall time for a fixed workload. Then search learning rate, weight decay, and warmup on a small parallel screen. After warmup, use a linear decay or a cosine decay, and search the weight-decay timescale between 5 percent and 20 percent of the full training horizon. Set these values separately for each training stage and for each parameter group. Use the screen results to choose the next small batch of candidates.
options.B:
Goal: Set the training optimizer after the physical batch size is chosen.

Plan: First choose the physical batch size that gives the shortest end-to-end wall time for a fixed workload. Then set the LoRA learning rate to 2e-4 and set the translator learning rate from the uniform, two-step, and three-step ratios. Set weight decay to 0.01 and warmup to 32 steps. After warmup, hold the learning rate constant for the rest of the run. Use this weight decay, warmup, and constant schedule for every training stage.

options.A:
Goal: Set the experiment size to 4B from the six-cell 25 percent engineering pass and start the 4B 10,528-step matched-call quality pipeline.

Plan: Write a versioned code-gate decision that sets selected size to 4B, because 4B is the only size whose twelve fresh train and inference cells all exceed 25 percent, and keep 0.8B and 2B out of the size contest because each already has a valid inference-gate failure. After provenance repair, a new 12-cell tiered real-task asset, and the 4B physical batch-size receipt are closed, run a stage and group hyperparameter batch on 4B. When that batch writes a selection receipt, start in the same round the two 10,528-step shallow-versus-deep matched arms and the B5 and B6 controls on 4B. The 10,528-step pair is a must-run in that same round once the hyperparameter receipt exists.
options.B:
Goal: Choose the experiment size by total training time and collect a 64-step matched-call hyperparameter sample on that size.

Plan: Write a versioned code-gate decision that records 4B as a passing size and sets selected experiment size to none. On the same A800 board, time 0.8B and 2B under the same training kernel across translator-only, LoRA-only, and joint stage profiles, and reuse the closed 4B physical batch-size receipts for the 4B profiles. Select the size with the shortest projected three-stage training wall, build the 12-cell tiered asset on that Base, then train four 64-step matched shallow and deep hyperparameter candidates. Collect their loss curves, adjacent NLL, and a 96-row development probe, and end the round when those four candidates are analyzed.

options.A:
Goal: Finish the real-task tier asset after the 0.8B Base-K1 calibration stopped at 8 of 12 cells.

Plan: Keep 0.8B as the selected size, and keep the 25, 50, and 75 percent accuracy layers, the quotas, and the official metrics. Grade generations with the official LiveCodeBench stop and extract functions, and stop a panel when any benchmark group scores all zeros. Regrade or regenerate the LiveCodeBench and word-sorting groups. Add official CRUXEval, ASDiv, and SciBench sources on this 0.8B Base. Write the 12-cell asset after all 12 cells are filled. Start the four matched-depth micro-runs after that asset exists.
options.B:
Goal: Finish the real-task tier asset after the 0.8B Base-K1 calibration stopped at 8 of 12 cells.

Plan: Keep the current LiveCodeBench, MATH, and GPQA items. Score the same registered code, math, and science subset on the 2B Base with the same calibration plan and the same method that graded the 0.8B outputs, using about 1700 rows. If 2B fills the missing cells, set the selected experiment size to 2B and write the 12-cell asset. If 2B still misses cells, widen the accuracy layers on 0.8B or change the official tasks after that measurement, then write the asset. Start the four matched-depth micro-runs after that asset exists.

options.A:
Goal: Obtain the remaining 22x scale readout and the matched-call K=1 through K=8 curriculum readout.

Plan: Continue the main H8/r48 joint training until it reaches 22 tokens per LoRA parameter. Continue the parameter-matched K1 training until it uses the same total input tokens as the main method. In the same step, train two matched-call arms from the existing LoRA-only checkpoint, one with Translator updates and one with Translator frozen, using the same steps, tokens, data order, and R-call budget, with training depths covering K=1 through K=8. After each finished endpoint is sealed, evaluate it on the registered 1,000-document held-out proxy and the 128-row MedMCQA development set.
options.B:
Goal: Obtain the remaining 22x scale readout and the endpoint comparisons that depend on those checkpoints.

Plan: Continue the main H8/r48 joint training until it reaches 22 tokens per LoRA parameter. Continue the parameter-matched K1 training until it uses the same total input tokens as the main method. After the main endpoint is sealed, evaluate that checkpoint on the registered 1,000-document held-out proxy and the 128-row MedMCQA development set. After the K1 endpoint is sealed, evaluate the K1 floor and the block-damped and layer-damped baselines on the same calls.

options.A:
Goal: Measure whether ordinary LoRA trained on official MedMCQA train data improves MedMCQA accuracy at 5 tokens per LoRA parameter.

Plan: Build a train-only supervised set from the official MedMCQA train split. Put the gold option as the first target token, and keep every development and confirmation identity out of training. Train ordinary parameter-matched LoRA from the same base model on this set to 5 tokens per LoRA parameter, and score the same 1,280-row MedMCQA development set against the original Base model. If accuracy does not rise, change the training sources or replace the benchmark and run the ordinary LoRA check again. After ordinary LoRA improves on a pair of training data and benchmark, compare Looped LoRA with ordinary LoRA on that same pair.
options.B:
Goal: Measure whether full-horizon Looped recurrence improves MedMCQA accuracy relative to K=1.

Plan: Continue the deep-updated, deep-frozen, and shallow-frozen Looped arms from the existing joint256 checkpoints to the full 7,658-step horizon, with the same data order, token budget, and LoRA schedule. Evaluate the four cells at K=1 through K=8 on the current 1,280-row MedMCQA development set and the held-out proxy. Add damped Euler controls from the K=1 state of each deep endpoint. Keep paired item accuracy as the primary readout, and use the full-horizon results to decide the depth-gain claim and the next structure or scale change.

options.A:
Goal: Measure how close Muon-preprocessed training updates are to the Marchenko-Pastur spectrum, and collect published evidence for that claim.

Plan: Use singular-value spectra taken only after SOAP, trust blend, and Schatten-4 scaling. Report a direct distance from those spectra to the Marchenko-Pastur law that matches the matrix shape.
