Write the distance rule and pass synthetic tests on known Marchenko-Pastur draws. Recompute that number on the existing seed 0, 2, and 3 spectrum files. At a few late checkpoints on two new seeds, hold the model and optimizer still, run several independent minibatches through the same preprocessing, average the spectral distributions from those batches, and then compute the distance by operator. Read papers on gradient spectra, random-matrix theory in neural training, and Muon, and record each source as direct theory, indirect observation, or counter-evidence.
options.B:
Goal: Test whether the V3 Newton-Schulz schedule beats the exact 12-step schedule after each method uses its own muon learning rate and cautious weight decay.

Plan: On seed 0, run Track 3 training from step 0 to 2900 on a 3 by 3 grid of muon learning rates 0.035625, 0.0375, and 0.039375 and cautious weight decay 0.020, 0.025, and 0.030. Launch 16 new runs, eight for the exact schedule and eight for V3, and reuse the two center cells from earlier clean runs. Keep the V3 coefficients the same on every cell. Watch all Newton-Schulz matrices and mark a cell failed if any singular value goes above 1.5. Inside each method, pick one complete safe cell from the late-loss tail on steps 2600 to 2750. Confirm the two chosen settings on unused seeds 3 and 4 with the same 2690-step paired-loss and safety gates.

options.A:
Goal: Study selected-feasibility failures on the finished 8-benchmark screen and one Williams coverage repair.

Plan: Keep the completed 2304-cell screen as the main experiment. Report selected gaps together with the alpha-tightening and dose-response frontiers on those cells. Run one coverage repair on Williams-Otto with the symbolic surrogate, choose the repair from random coverage only, and record the new coverage, selected gap, and baseline cost. Treat that cell as a case study in a baseline-gated evaluation of selected feasibility.
options.B:
Goal: Produce at least two valid hard cells under the current gates and test scale-aware selected-risk calibration on them.

Plan: Repair Williams-Otto symbolic coverage by choosing training and calibration size from random coverage only, then remeasure the selected gap and the alpha-tightening, dose, and trust-region frontier. Run a stress suite that varies residual pocket width, amplitude, location, and boundary-biased objective risk, and report every grid cell. On cells that pass the current coverage, gap, violation, and cheap-baseline tests, run k-nearest-neighbor scale-aware selected-risk calibration and the same baseline frontier.

options.A:
Goal: Produce hard cells that can support a method-necessity claim under the 0.88 random-coverage threshold.

Plan: Keep the 0.88 random-coverage threshold. On the Williams-Otto symbolic cell, choose one coverage repair from a pre-registered train and calibration grid using only random coverage, then measure selected gap, alpha-tightening, dose response, and kNN scale-aware calibration. In parallel, run a parameterized stress suite with spatially localized residual pockets and objective distributions that put mass on high-risk boundaries. Apply the same coverage, gap, violation, and cheap-baseline gates to every cell in that grid, and run kNN scale-aware selected-risk calibration on the cells that pass.
options.B:
Goal: Recast the project as a baseline-gated evaluation of when optimizer selection breaks conformal constraint learning.

Plan: Keep the 0.88 random-coverage threshold. Use the completed 2304-cell screen as the study sample, and report that alpha-tightening or a small dose margin closes large selected gaps at low cost. Keep the Williams-Otto symbolic cell as an exploratory case study. Choose one coverage repair on that cell from a pre-registered train and calibration grid using only random coverage, then measure selected gap and simple baselines. If the selected gap disappears after coverage rises, record that outcome as evidence that a stronger random certificate can replace selected-risk calibration.

options.A:
Goal: Find optimizer-selected feasibility failures on the eight existing benchmarks where cheap controls do not close the gap, and test selected-risk calibration and LLM-guided symbolic constraints as repairs.

Plan: Repeat the eight-benchmark hard-cell screen with coverage_min of 0.88, selected gap of at least 0.08, static selected violation of at least 0.15, and cheap controls given by tighter alpha, dose penalties, and trust regions. Add residual-hotspot and boundary-pressure objective modes that push the solver toward high-residual and near-boundary points using only train and calibration data. On cells that pass all gates, and on the top selected-gap cells if none pass, run additive SRC and kNN scale-aware SRC with hyperparameters chosen on objective-cal data and a single held-out objective-test report. Generate LLM-guided symbolic constraint candidates for methane, Williams-Otto, and any new target cells, then evaluate them with the same selected-feasibility and cheap-control gates.
options.B:
Goal: Find localized residual hard cells whose random coverage sits above 0.895, and test a boundary-conditioned residual-scale estimator on the remaining no-candidate cells.

Plan: Join the R25 hard-cell list with the R29 calibration-only k and q choices and the R30 independent 5000-point coverage results, and keep cells that pass the coverage_min of 0.88 gate and the calibration-only selection rule. Generate a new localized residual suite around the successful families, using larger train and calibration sizes, independent n_random_test of 5000, boundary and interior-near-boundary locations, and the same alpha, dose, and trust controls. Keep the hard-cell gate at coverage_min of 0.88, and record which cells also reach coverage_min of 0.895 or 0.90. On the no-candidate and cost-borderline cells, train residual-scale estimators that use distance-to-boundary and local residual density from random-calibration data only, select the estimator on objective-cal UCB, and evaluate once on held-out objective-test data.

options.A:
Goal: Choose the next experiment after the Williams LLM-SR coverage rescue reported coverage min 0.8787.

Plan: Keep the R40 expression, training split, and pinball tau fixed. For each of seeds 0, 1, and 2, draw a new calibration set of 1000 points and a new independent random test set of 20000 points. Measure coverage and selected gap again on the three objective modes with the same solver settings. Place the original seed-level coverage values, including the seed 0 interval around 0.8787, next to these locked measurements.
options.B:
Goal: Choose the next experiment after the Williams LLM-SR coverage rescue reported coverage min 0.8787.

Plan: Continue the R38 dense k and q sweep on the remaining selected-risk targets. Count a Williams LLM-SR cell as eligible only if coverage min is at least 0.88. With coverage min 0.8787, stop further Williams LLM-SR coverage work and keep the R40 expression, the calibration size of 300, and the current random test set unchanged. Wait until an R38 target has all three seeds with violation at most 0.10 and matched cost at most 5 percent.

options.A:
Goal: Find whether a non-Williams target in the R38 selected-risk repair passes the per-seed strict test on the targets that already have complete calibration.

Plan: Take the R38 targets whose calibration checkpoints are already complete as the target set. Apply the calibration-only selection rule to this set. Then run a held-out test on new objectives for the selected configs and report the per-seed strict pass or fail results. If a later calibration of the unfinished oscillatory_box_4d targets yields a selected config, evaluate that config on a new held-out split.
options.B:
Goal: Find whether a non-Williams target in the R38 selected-risk repair passes the per-seed strict test after every calibration target is complete.

Plan: Continue the R38 dense k and q calibration sweep until all 18 targets have complete calibration checkpoints, including the two remaining oscillatory_box_4d targets. After all calibration checkpoints are complete, apply the calibration-only selection rule to the full 18-target set. Then run a held-out test on the selected configs and report the per-seed strict pass or fail results. Include the oscillatory_box_4d targets in this selected set once their calibration checkpoints exist.

options.A:
Goal: Decide the low-cost claim by comparing each selected row to the recorded 5 percent relative-cost rule.

Plan: On the existing R41 objective IDs, keep the low-cost claim as a per-seed test that relative cost is at most 5 percent. Also compute paired absolute cost, cost divided by the decision-box objective range, and cost divided by the static P95 to P05 scale for the selected rows and the strong controls. On a new performance split, report the same cost quantities and the control frontier, and do not set a new success threshold. Record heteroscale seed 0 at 5.5098 percent as a miss of the 5 percent rule. If a new threshold is needed, wait for a human to write that number.
options.B:
Goal: Decide the low-cost claim by reading the observed cost behavior on the existing R41 decisions.

Plan: On the existing R41 objective IDs, recompute paired absolute cost, cost divided by the decision-box objective range, and cost divided by the static P95 to P05 scale for each selected row and each strong control. Read the origin-shift audit and the control frontier. Include the heteroscale seed 0 relative cost of 5.5098 percent and the 289 times that a constant objective shift changes the 5 percent label. State whether each selected row is cheap relative to the controls that meet the risk target on every seed. On a new performance split, report the same cost quantities and interpret them from the observed gaps. The 5 percent figure may be changed after this reading.

options.A:
Goal: Measure selected feasibility on the eight-benchmark matrix with the linear OCL solver, and test a constant floor that uses the same proposal queries as the learned envelope.

Plan: Run the original eight benchmarks, three surrogates, six objective laws, and three seeds with the linear OCL solver, the 0.88 coverage gate, and the existing alpha, dose, and trust controls. On each new hard cell, fit a smooth max-affine correction on 300 proposal objectives per seed, certify the frozen rows on a new objective split, and draw a fresh frontier against static conformal and those controls. On the frozen methane and Williams contexts, give a constant-floor family the same 300 selected-point oracle queries per seed, freeze each seed at its lowest-cost safe strength, and certify the envelope and the floor on the six objective laws.
options.B:
Goal: State a selected-risk mechanism on a two-region family, and test a positive-neighbor methane scale and a non-chemistry real-domain cell.

Plan: Construct a two-region OCL family and name a deployment-cost interval where a location-dependent correction has selected risk at most alpha and every constant-margin policy has selected risk above alpha. On the locked R43 methane expression and the same training and calibration splits, score each point by the largest positive residual among its neighbors and by a density-weighted positive severity, and evaluate both scales on the same objectives, solver, and oracle queries as the kNN quantile and the two-part estimator. Rescreen portfolio3d with residual-hotspot and boundary-pressure objectives, and if that screen still has no hard cell, add one published non-chemistry OCL benchmark and run the same selected-feasibility and cheap-control measurements.

options.A:
Goal: Obtain a repaired 54-unit R68b solver matrix on the 200-objective sample set for every unit.

Plan: Use the current 200-objective sample, with identifiers that are multiples of 5, as the matrix that each unit must complete. Finish the remaining sample shards so that all 54 units have a nested 20, 100, and 500 start result. On those rows, report method and control ordering, solver status, infeasible rows, optimal value, and nested ladder movement. Then report paired risk and cost intervals on this 200-objective 54-unit matrix.
options.B:
Goal: Obtain a repaired 54-unit R68b solver matrix on the 1000-objective set for every cell.

Plan: Use the current sample gate to choose cells for full replay, with nested ladder change as one of the triggers. The measured sample already sends 53 of 54 units and all 18 cells into that replay. On each selected cell, run the repaired nested 20, 100, and 500 start ladder at 1000 objectives with the same methods and controls. Then report paired risk and cost intervals on this 1000-objective 54-unit matrix.

options.A:
Goal: Measure the V8b deletion-help rates after prompt-level filters and build a multi-unit organic set with a ShareGPT chat-host arm.

Plan: Re-aggregate the existing R32 Qwen and Mistral unit-outcome parquets with prompt-level sha256 dedup, a minimum of 3 sentence units per organic prompt, a prompt-level Y_noop band of 0.05 to 0.95, and source-proportion IPW. Report R_real, CF_math, and CF_chat on that filtered set with a per-source and per-multi-unit table. Write a coverage audit that records how many prompts remain after each filter step. Mine a fresh WildChat, ShareGPT, AgentIF, and CodeChat sample under the same dedup and multi-unit rules. Build a ShareGPT conversation-host chat anchor with middle, density-2, plain injection. Choose Branch A, B, or C from the filtered aggregate.
options.B:
Goal: Report the V8b Branch B finding on the current organic backbone and send it to review.

Plan: Use the collected R32 and R33 drop-regime aggregate as the paper headline. Keep the organic set as 425 prompts (420 MBPP, 2 WildChat SQL, and 3 filtered AgentIF) and keep the R28 HumanEval-host chat anchor. Report R_real = 0.074 with lower 90% CI above 0, CF_math = 0.266 with CI excluding 1, and CF_chat = 0.215 with P(CF_chat > CF_math) = 0.37. Write the paper claim as weak Claim 2 held and Claim 3 falsified. Record the MBPP-heavy mix, the n=2 WildChat SQL cell, and the two floor-bound AgentIF prompts in limitations. Send this STATE to review for NeurIPS Findings, and keep the R28 recipe and the drop and fill Pattern 7 check as supporting material.

options.A:
Goal: Produce the next V9 review package for the organic-prompt calibration study.

Plan: Finish the R38 inference on the R34b-v2 set of 455 organic prompts. Use Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 with the four intervention arms and six samples per unit. Then run R39 to merge the R34b set of 50 prompts with R34b-v2 into one combined set of at least 100 organic prompts. Send that combined package to the V9 reviewer after R39 completes.
options.B:
Goal: Produce the next V9 review package for the organic-prompt calibration study.

Plan: Send the R36 results on the R34b set of 50 organic prompts to the V9 reviewer. Use this package to obtain a review of the matched per-sentence protocol, the hygiene pipeline, and the CF_math claim. If that review reports a defect in method, code, or argument, fix the defect on this 50-prompt scale and send another review. Run the R34b-v2 inference on 455 organic prompts after a review that names experiment scale as the remaining issue.

options.A:
Goal: After the V12 not-ready review, run a V13 batch of three experiments over up to two days of wall time, then send one review, and keep the target venue as a choice among NeurIPS main, NeurIPS workshop, and stopping the project.

Plan: Remine 30 fresh WildChat prompts and score Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on delete versus no-op with two samples per unit, about 1200 forwards, to test whether the Qwen mean deletion effect on WildChat is below zero, above zero, or crosses zero. In the same dispatch, score 30 LMSYS hosts with the GSM-IC distractor under an objective verifier and a judge, with two samples per unit, to test whether the LMSYS mean effect matches the HumanEval host or the ShareGPT host. Also run LLMLingua-2 on the existing 50 organic prompts and compare ROC-AUC and precision at the 14.5 percent tail with random delete. After all three runs finish, send one V13 review.
options.B:
Goal: After the V12 not-ready review, set the target venue to NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks, run one WildChat remine of at most one hour of wall time, and then send that result to review.

Plan: Write NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks as the target venue in the idea, the proposal, and STATE. Remine 30 fresh WildChat prompts that do not overlap the current organic WildChat set. Score Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on delete versus no-op with one sample per unit, using at most the three longest units in each prompt, for at most 180 forwards and at most one hour of wall time, and record whether the Qwen mean deletion effect is below zero, above zero, or crosses zero. If mining yields fewer than 30 WildChat prompts, switch the source to ShareGPT inside the same one-hour budget. When this run finishes, send the result to review and write the next experiment from that review.

options.A:
Goal: After the V14 review, wait for the user to choose a project path before any V15 experiment.

Plan: Do not start a V15 run and do not lock the next run protocol. Present four options to the user. One option is another one-hour V15 experiment. One option is a bundled cycle that tries to close at least three must-fixes, with a prompt-compression baseline, an organic re-run that uses the length-null arm, and a rewrite of STATE sections 1 to 6. One option is to send the current V14 paper to NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks and archive the workspace. One option is to rewrite the idea as an ICLR or EMNLP short paper. Wait for the user reply before any of these starts.
options.B:
Goal: After the V14 review, run the next V15 experiment under the one-hour cadence.

Plan: Re-aggregate the existing R34b drop-strict six-prompt headline subset. Compute A_real as delete minus length-null on the same-prompt-only matched units. Report paired prompt-cluster bootstrap 90 percent confidence intervals. Also report the same-prompt unit count and the cross-prompt fallback rate. If the parquet has no length-null arm, abort this run and write a six-prompt length-null GPU pilot for the next dispatch. After this run, send V15 to review.

options.A:
Goal: Close the Stage 0 closeout gaps reported by the latest audit.

Plan: Update the closeout checker so the official receipt checker runs on every verdict-reachable run. Treat a missing or failing receipt as a blocker. For any dirty reachable run, require a receipt pass and a machine proof that the dirty files are not load-bearing before the run can stay as a warning. Bind each latest-audit issue to a predicate with the same meaning. Then recompute a Stage 0 closeout. Start the MuJoCo controller-versus-RL comparison only after that closeout reports no unresolved blocker, critical, or major findings.
options.B:
Goal: Reproduce PPO on the Gymnasium MuJoCo v5 environments listed in the task cards.

Plan: Use the six MuJoCo v5 task cards and the PPO sources they name from RL Baselines3 Zoo and CleanRL. First train a short PPO smoke on InvertedPendulum-v5 and Hopper-v5. Then train PPO on those six v5 environments with the published hyperparameters and several seeds. Record eval returns, learning curves, and the recipe source for each run. Compare the eval returns with the published v3 and v4 reference ranges stored on the cards.

options.A:
Goal: Close the Stage-0 audit findings that remain after the v25 closeout.

Plan: Run a v26 strict closeout that treats a predicate source outside the evidence graph as a BLOCKER, registers the self-receipt file in the manifest, and resolves audit issues from the coverage, receipt, and graph reports. Keep MuJoCo PPO and SAC baseline training unstarted until this closeout reports zero BLOCKER, CRITICAL, and MAJOR findings.
options.B:
Goal: Reproduce PPO on Gymnasium MuJoCo v5 from public recipes.

Plan: Take PPO hyperparameters and training code from public sources such as Stable-Baselines3 RL Zoo and CleanRL continuous-action PPO. Record the source URL and commit for each setting. Run those settings on InvertedPendulum-v5 and Hopper-v5, then train InvertedPendulum-v5, Hopper-v5, Walker2d-v5, and HalfCheetah-v5 with the same recipe and three seeds.

options.A:
Goal: Collect the remaining public PPO wave2 cells by waiting for the current remote jobs to finish in launch order.

Plan: Leave the InvertedPendulum and Hopper seeds running on compute node A, and leave the Walker2d, HalfCheetah, and Ant seeds running on compute node B. After the Ant-tuned cells reach 10 million steps, start the Humanoid cells from the same Ant-Humanoid launch script. When a group writes wave_status.json, copy summaries, checkpoints, and replay files back to the workspace. After all six environments are collected, use this wave as the public PPO baseline for later comparison with the proposed method.
options.B:
Goal: Collect the remaining public PPO wave2 cells after measuring throughput and running Humanoid in parallel under the public recipe.

Plan: Record steps per second, CPU and GPU use, checkpoint cost, and remaining time for each active PPO cell. Start the pending Humanoid seeds on compute node B or compute node C in parallel with the running Ant seeds, and do not duplicate cells that are already in progress. Train baseline cells with DummyVecEnv and n_envs=1. Run a short SubprocVecEnv or RL-Zoo native smoke on InvertedPendulum, Hopper, and Ant, and record it as a throughput diagnostic if it changes PPO batch or rollout size relative to the public recipe. Sync each finished environment when its wave_status file exists.

options.A:
Goal: Test a four-stage Hopper hopping controller against standing-still tags and absolute-speed thresholds.

Plan: Add an explicit Hopper controller with crouch, push, flight, and land stages. Tune it on the train seeds, then evaluate once on test seeds that were not used for tuning. Declare success if the standing-still tags drop, or if mean absolute horizontal speed is at least 0.5 and vertical speed variation is at least 0.3.
options.B:
Goal: Test a four-stage Hopper hopping controller against the PPO Hopper on the same task.

Plan: Add an explicit Hopper controller with crouch, push, flight, and land stages. Tune it on the train seeds, then evaluate once on test seeds that were not used for tuning. Compare signed forward speed, episode length, and fall rate with the PPO Hopper baseline of mean return 3630, full 1000-step episodes with no fall, and forward speed of about 1 to 2 meters per second.

options.A:
Goal: Begin S1 by scoring a Swimmer traveling-wave controller against a Swimmer PPO mean from the public Zoo recipe.

Plan: Train Swimmer PPO with the public Stable-Baselines3 Zoo recipe that uses observation normalization, and record the mean and run hash as the PPO baseline. Implement a two-joint traveling sine-wave controller with frequency, phase lag, amplitude, bias, and damping. Search those parameters on the train seeds with a budget of 50,000 simulator steps. Report the test normalized return against that PPO mean.
options.B:
Goal: Begin S1 by scoring a Swimmer traveling-wave controller against the S0 Swimmer PPO mean of 111.

Plan: Write a Swimmer task card and a protocol that sets the PPO mean to 111. Implement a two-joint traveling sine-wave controller with frequency, phase lag, amplitude, bias, and damping. Search those parameters on the train seeds with a budget of 50,000 simulator steps. Report the test normalized return against 111.

options.A:
Goal: Build a humanoid motion-imitation benchmark so the explicit controller can be scored against a published tracking baseline on held-out motions.

Plan: Download a PHC checkpoint and a motion set from AMASS or BONES-SEED. Write a split of 100 train motions, 50 tune motions, and 100 held-out motions by family. Load the checkpoint and score tracking metrics on about 20 validation motions, and stop if the gap from the reported PHC numbers is larger than 10 percent. Treat the MuJoCo head-to-head table as complete and mark HalfCheetah as not available. After these benchmark files exist, start a Humanoid-v5 head-to-head controller.
options.B:
Goal: Raise an explicit Swimmer controller toward the PPO return with typed patches and a replay gate, then apply the same loop to other MuJoCo environments.

Plan: Search the 13 parameters of the Swimmer traveling-wave controller with CMA-ES, and report return divided by the PPO value 358.23. Build a Swimmer failure ledger and a bucket replay gate. Start typed-patch rounds from a mid-search config with return near 200, and accept a patch only when the target bucket improves and protected buckets do not get worse. After at least one accepted patch and a higher normalized return, run the same loop on Ant. Do the humanoid motion-imitation benchmark after a MuJoCo environment is near or above PPO.

options.A:
Goal: Test whether a Hopper controller made of phase, joint-target, PD, and balance rules can keep Hopper from falling on new seeds.

Plan: Write a Hopper controller that updates an internal phase from height and foot touchdown, sets joint angle targets from a small table of knots or if-else rules, turns tracking error into torque with PD gains, and adds a torso pitch balance term. Search these scalar parameters with CMA-ES on training seeds in the simulator. Measure fall rate, return, and forward speed on seeds 20 to 29 against the Hopper PPO baseline return of 3630.3. The runtime map from observation and phase to torque uses only those parameters.
options.B:
Goal: Test whether smooth neighbor and ensemble models trained on Hopper PPO rollouts can keep Hopper from falling on new seeds.

Plan: Collect about 200,000 observation-action pairs from the Hopper PPO teacher on training seeds. Fit a distance-weighted K-nearest-neighbor regressor, random forests, and a depth-7 decision tree on that data. Measure fall rate, return, and forward speed on seeds 20 to 29. If all models still fall every episode, run five DAgger rounds on the two best models. In each round collect on-policy states, query the PPO teacher for actions, and refit. Treat any smooth model with holdout fall rate below 0.5 as a success. Store the teacher examples for runtime lookup. Do not call a neural network when the controller acts.

options.A:
Goal: Reuse Walker2d environments across candidates and compare search methods on the contact-phase controller.

Plan: Keep the running three-family HZD and Bezier CMA-ES search with eight restarts and about 6000 evaluations per restart. Then implement a worker that keeps one Walker2d environment and resets it for each episode, and check that those rollouts match the path that creates a new environment every time. After that check, search the existing contact-phase velocity controller with CEM, random shooting, coordinate search, and CMA-ES started from known good parameters, using the same seeds and episode budget. Keep the Walker2d held-out target of 6175.5.
options.B:
Goal: Change CMA-ES population and restart settings for Walker2d explicit-controller scouts.

Plan: Keep the running three-family HZD and Bezier CMA-ES search with eight restarts and about 6000 evaluations per restart. Create a new Walker2d environment for every candidate episode, then roll out 32 seeds of 1000 steps. For later scouts, raise the CMA-ES population size so more workers can run at once, start new restarts from parameters already found, or use fewer restarts. After this scout, use the same CMA-ES pattern on the next explicit controller family, with the Walker2d held-out target of 6175.5.

options.A:
Goal: Test whether a new hand-written Walker2d gait program can walk and raise return above the n90 baseline.

Plan: Write a new explicit controller that replaces the n90 spline targets with multi-regime gait laws and an outer speed schedule. Predeclare a few programs, including harmonic joint targets, a capture and push-off law, and a walk or jog mode bank. Run each program on a few Walker2d tune seeds and compare them with n90 on the same seeds. If no program is both stable and faster, use the rest of the tune budget for one rewritten program. Set parameters from physical intuition and from this small set of episodes, with no CMA-ES job. If a program meets the fall and speed gates, evaluate it on heldout seeds and a mini robustness set.
options.B:
Goal: Test whether a residual overlay on the n90 Walker2d controller can raise speed after a small CMA-ES start and one manual edit.

Plan: Keep the n90 phase-spline controller and its parameters as the walking base. Add an explicit residual overlay with at most twelve new speed, capture, or posture parameters. Run CMA-ES only on those overlay parameters, with population at most twelve, at most eight generations, and at most 96 tune episodes. After this init run, inspect the safest traces and apply one manual physical edit. A candidate may go to heldout seeds and a mini robustness set only when that manual edit is the selected controller.

options.A:
Goal: After the recent negative Walker2d speed families and the Hopper semantic-capacity scout, set the next work to a new return target or a new action interface.

Plan: Record the Walker2d families of local parameter edits, gait-program replacement, residual overlay, scalar cap, and pre-bound allocation, together with the Hopper semantic-capacity scout, as the finished explicit-controller set. The next scheduled work is a review of the success number given returns near 60 percent of PPO, or a move of the next tests into impedance control or joint-position control.
options.B:
Goal: After the recent negative Walker2d speed families and the Hopper semantic-capacity scout, set the next work to more structurally distinct explicit controllers until 60 approaches have real results.

Plan: Write a registry of at least 60 structural signatures and mark the current Walker2d and Hopper families as already tried. Launch a first Hopper batch with new mechanisms, including CPG, VMC and SLIP, Raibert landing, contact FSM, and bang-bang limit cycles. Measure per-joint raw and post-bound action headroom on the current Hopper spline in the same round. Count one architecture family as one approach. The success target stays at plus 50 percent of PPO.

options.A:
Goal: Run a ResNet depth ladder and MLP and PirateNets pilots as the next experiments, and close the five unfinished n=6 pairs.

Plan: Finish the five unfinished n=6 ResNet pairs with the current staged configs and the default direct configs. Run a ResNet depth ladder on five PDEs at 12, 18, and 24 layers with three seeds, and compare staged and direct at each depth. Run MLP and PirateNets pilots on two PDEs at 6 and 24 layers. Set the n=6 paired target to at least 5 wins out of 17. Put a matching autotune of the direct side in an appendix.
options.B:
Goal: Run per-PDE retune and a matching direct autotune on the n=6 17-PDE comparison, and run a ResNet depth ladder and MLP and PirateNets pilots.

Plan: Finish the five unfinished n=6 ResNet pairs. For each PDE where staged currently loses, run at least ten trials over BC and IC weights, stage split, and fine-tune learning rate. Give the direct side at least ten autotune trials per PDE on learning rate, loss weights, warmup, and gradient clip. Re-run the best staged config and the best direct config on three seeds. Run a ResNet depth ladder at 12, 18, and 24 layers and MLP and PirateNets pilots. Set the n=6 paired target to at least 11 wins out of 17.

options.A:
Goal: Measure whether staged training or direct training attains the lower L2RE when each method searches its own training hyperparameters.

Plan: Keep both methods on a ResNet with 6 layers, width 100, and the Adam optimizer. Run Optuna TPE first on Burgers1D, Poisson2D_Classic, and Heat2D_Multiscale, with 50 trials per method, and keep the top trials as priors for later PDEs. Then run 30 Optuna trials per method at 20000 training steps on all 17 PINNacle PDEs. Direct training searches learning rate, initialization, boundary-weight multiplier, warmup, minimum learning-rate ratio, and gradient clipping. Staged training searches those knobs and also stage split, stage-3 learning-rate ratio, and stage-1 learning-rate multiplier. After the 17-PDE round, retrain each winning configuration on seeds 0, 1, and 2, and score each PDE by the lower of the two best L2RE values.
options.B:
Goal: Measure whether staged training or direct training attains the lower L2RE when each method searches its own training hyperparameters.

Plan: Keep both methods on a ResNet with 6 layers, width 100, and the Adam optimizer. Open four Optuna TPE studies, each with its own database: Poisson2D_Classic with direct training, Poisson2D_Classic with staged training, Heat2D_VaryingCoef with direct training, and Heat2D_VaryingCoef with staged training. Direct training searches learning rate, initialization, boundary-weight multiplier, warmup, minimum learning-rate ratio, and gradient clipping. Staged training searches those knobs and also stage split, stage-3 learning-rate ratio, and stage-1 learning-rate multiplier. Each study runs 30 trials, and each trial trains for 5000 steps. After the four studies finish, score each of the two PDEs by the lower of the two best L2RE values.

options.A:
Goal: Choose the next experiment after the Layer-1 Optuna studies on Poisson2D_Classic and Heat2D_VC.

Plan: Take the four 30-trial studies as the paired result for staged training versus direct training at 5000 iterations, with the same trial count on both methods. Use the Poisson gap and the Heat near tie to forecast the 17-PDE win count. Next, run the same Optuna recipe at 5000 iterations on five more PDEs: Heat2D_Multiscale, Burgers2D, NS2D_LidDriven, PoissonBoltzmann2D, and HeatND. After that, rebaseline the depth ladder under Optuna on a small PDE set and present the depth result as the new main claim, with the n=6 table as per-PDE evidence.
options.B:
Goal: Choose the next experiment after the Layer-1 Optuna studies on Poisson2D_Classic and Heat2D_VC.

Plan: Keep the next run on Poisson2D_Classic and Heat2D_VC, and leave the Layer-1 direct best in place. Run a new staged-only Optuna search centered on that direct best after a half-depth first-stage transfer, with every staged knob still free inside bounds around the center. Search weight-init scale as a continuous log-uniform axis and keep bias init at zero. Delay pruning until a trial can finish the first stage, and reuse the Layer-1 staged trials as starting observations. Fit the run into one hour of wall time. If a best value sits near a bound, widen that bound and continue from the existing trials.

options.A:
Goal: Test whether the L1B Optuna recipe can give staged training a lower L2RE than direct training on the five PDEs that currently favor direct training.

Plan: Run a staged-only Optuna search on Heat2D_Multiscale, Heat2D_ComplexGeometry, Poisson2D_ManyArea, NS2D_LidDriven, and Burgers2D. Use 80 trials per PDE at 5000 iterations and the same ten hyperparameters as L1B. Warm-start each study from that PDE's earlier direct-best and staged trials. After each study, run one staged probe and one direct probe at 20000 iterations. Count how many of the five PDEs flip to a staged win, and use that count to decide whether a 17-PDE full-fidelity search is viable.
options.B:
Goal: Locate the staged hyperparameter basins on Poisson2D_Classic and Heat2D_VaryingCoef with a wider search range.

Plan: Use ResNet with 6 layers on Poisson2D_Classic and Heat2D_VaryingCoef. Widen the Poisson learning-rate upper bound from 7.5e-3 to 2e-2 and the Heat fine-tune learning-rate-ratio lower bound from 3e-2 to 5e-3. Load the 80 L1B trials into each new study and add about 30 new trials per PDE at 5000 iterations. After the round, check that the new bests sit inside the widened bounds and that L2RE is no worse than L1B. If a new best is on a bound or L2RE is higher than L1B, widen that bound and run another short round on the same two PDEs.

options.A:
Goal: Continue Step-3 hyperparameter search on Poisson2D_Classic and Heat2D_VaryingCoef after round 2 found a new high learning-rate basin at 5k steps.

Plan: Warm-start the existing 140-trial Optuna study and add 40 trials per PDE. Raise the Poisson learning-rate upper bound from 2e-2 to 5e-2, and add unused stage splits, lower fine-tune learning rates, and higher bc_mult. Place six enqueue seeds on both known basins at high learning rate, three with s30_60_10 and three with s20_60_20. Place six more seeds on settings such as very low fine-tune learning rate, very long S3, kaiming with high learning rate, and large init scale. After the 5k search, run 20k probes that keep the 5k fractions, that keep the S1 fraction and set S3 to 2000 steps with extra steps in S2, and that set S3 to 4000 steps. Also replay the round-1 Poisson config at 20k.
options.B:
Goal: Continue Step-3 hyperparameter search on Poisson2D_Classic and Heat2D_VaryingCoef after round 2 found a new high learning-rate basin at 5k steps.

Plan: Warm-start the existing 140-trial Optuna study and add 30 trials per PDE. Raise the Poisson learning-rate upper bound from 2e-2 to 5e-2. Place all six Poisson enqueue seeds inside the new 5k basin with stage split s20_60_20, fine-tune learning rate 8e-3, warmup 0.01, and grad clip 5.0, and only move learning rate and init scale around that basin. Place the six Heat seeds on the large init-scale mode. After the 5k search, take the new 5k-best config and run one 20k probe that keeps the same stage-split fractions. Keep that 20k number if it still beats the L1B baseline.

options.A:
Goal: Get a 20k-iteration staged error for vanilla MLP on Poisson2D_Classic and on Heat2D_VaryingCoef.

Plan: Run a 40-trial staged Optuna search at 5k iterations on each PDE. Retrain the top three 5k configurations of each PDE for 20k iterations. Also retrain a few configs near the 5k winner by changing the stage split, the learning rate, or the last-stage learning rate. Report the lowest 20k error from this set as the staged MLP result.
options.B:
Goal: Get a 20k-iteration staged error for vanilla MLP on Poisson2D_Classic and on Heat2D_VaryingCoef.

Plan: Run a 40-trial staged Optuna search at 5k iterations on each PDE. Rank the trials by their 5k error and keep the winner of each PDE. Retrain that winner once for 20k iterations. Report that 20k error as the staged MLP result.

options.A:
Goal: Measure staged and direct L2RE at ResNet depths 12 and 24 on Poisson2D_Classic and Heat2D_VaryingCoef, and at depth 6 on three other PDE families.

Plan: Train ResNet models at n=12 and n=24 with seed 0 on Poisson2D_Classic and Heat2D_VaryingCoef. Staged runs reuse each PDE's n=6 hyperparameters and set the stage split as a fraction of depth. Direct runs use a 6-trial Optuna search over learning rate and init scale at 5k iterations, then a 20k run of the best trial. Also train ResNet n=6 with seed 0 on Burgers1D, Wave2D_LongTime, and Heat2D_Multiscale. For each new PDE, run an 8-trial staged Optuna search at 5k iterations inside the learning-rate, init-scale, and stage-split ranges taken from the two existing PDEs, then 20k probes and a 6-trial direct search. If a staged best trial sits on a search bound, widen that bound by one decade and search again.
options.B:
Goal: Measure whether stage-1 of staged training changes the curvature of a vanilla MLP PINN loss in the same way a ResNet skip connection does at initialization.

Plan: On Poisson2D_Classic and Heat2D_VaryingCoef, evaluate three n=6 networks at seed 0: a vanilla MLP at direct-training initialization, a vanilla MLP after stage 1 of staged training, and a ResNet at direct-training initialization. Do not run further training. For each of the six settings, compute the top 50 Hessian eigenvalues of the full PINN loss with 50 Lanczos iterations, the NTK condition number of the PDE residual kernel on 256 collocation points, and the ratio of the largest Hessian eigenvalue to the tenth. Mark the geometry check as passed when the staged MLP sharpness and NTK condition number are at most twice the ResNet-init values and at most 0.3 times the vanilla-direct-init values. Write one spectrum table and one bar figure.

options.A:
Goal: Measure the locked Poisson ResNet staged run on extra seeds, then test staged training on PirateNets.

Plan: Rerun the locked Poisson staged configuration that uses loss weights 1, 10000, and 10000 with seed 1 and seed 2. Rerun that same configuration with boundary weight 10 and with the collaborator stage split. Then train PirateNets with 6 layers on Poisson2D_Classic and Heat2D_VaryingCoef. For staged training, search a boundary-weight multiplier in 1000, 5000, and 10000 together with learning rate, initialization scale, and stage split. For direct training, search learning rate and initialization scale. Report relative L2 error on interior points at 20000 steps.
options.B:
Goal: Measure staged training against direct training on Poisson2D_Classic and Heat2D_VaryingCoef with the PINNacle default loss weights.

Plan: Set every loss weight to 1.0 for both methods and keep this value out of the search. Use ResNet with 6 layers and width 100, tanh activation, Glorot normal initialization, a constant learning rate, no gradient clipping, and 20000 training steps. Search learning rate and initialization scale for direct training. Search learning rate, the two stage learning-rate ratios, initialization scale, and stage split for staged training. Train both methods for 20000 steps and compare relative L2 error on interior points on these two PDEs.

options.A:
Goal: Collect a staged-versus-direct result for Poisson2D_Classic on the PINNacle setup-B ResNet with 6 layers.

Plan: Use the existing Poisson2D_Classic direct result of relative L2 error 0.6791 as the baseline. Change staged training so stage 1 and stage 2 each use their own initialization scale. Search the staged method at 20000 steps over stage-1 learning rate, stage-2 learning-rate ratio, stage-3 learning-rate ratio, stage-1 initialization scale in [0.3, 6.0], stage-2 initialization scale in [0.3, 6.0], stage-1 step fraction in [0.1, 0.7], and stage-2 step fraction in [0.05, 0.7]. Start two seed trials from the current Poisson staged best and from the collaborator Poisson best setting. Run 40 trials at 20000 steps, then choose the next change from those 40 trials.
options.B:
Goal: Collect a staged-versus-direct result for Heat2D_VaryingCoef on the PINNacle setup-B ResNet with 6 layers.

Plan: Keep the Poisson2D_Classic numbers at direct relative L2 error 0.6791 and staged relative L2 error 0.6802. Run Heat2D_VaryingCoef next. Search Heat direct with 30 trials at 20000 steps over learning rate and initialization scale. Search Heat staged with 30 trials at 20000 steps over learning rate, initialization scale, stage-2 learning-rate ratio, stage-3 learning-rate ratio, stage-1 step fraction in [0.2, 0.5], and stage-2 step fraction in [0.1, 0.5]. Start one Heat staged trial and one Heat direct trial from the collaborator Heat best hyperparameters.

options.A:
Goal: Map the Poisson2D_Classic staged hyperparameter landscape under the PINNacle BC=1 setup.

Plan: Let the running Poisson3D_CG and HeatND jobs finish and store the run files. Leave the Poisson direct baseline at L2RE 0.6791. On Poisson staged training with a ResNet of 6 layers and width 100, start from the current staged best values lr=0.000381, init_scale_s1=1.107, init_scale_s2=3.256, s2_lr_ratio=2.94, s3_lr_ratio=0.124, s1_frac=0.476, and s2_frac=0.056. For each of these seven knobs, run 10 trials at 20k iterations while holding the other six knobs at those values, for 70 trials in total. Record the L2RE versus knob curves, the range where L2RE rises by about 50 percent, and any trial that beats 0.5975. Use those bands as the search ranges for later Poisson width-200 and depth-12 cells, and scale the learning-rate band with width.
options.B:
Goal: Set the paper table for staged versus direct training from the current PINNacle BC=1 cells and the two unfinished PDEs.

Plan: Put the new PoissonBoltzmann2D numbers of staged L2RE 0.4736 versus direct L2RE 0.4954 into the main table. Let the Poisson3D_CG and HeatND jobs finish and add those two cells as well. After this seven-cell table is complete, write a report with four paper options. Option (a) keeps a PINNacle BC=1 main table whose ratios are 1.01 to 1.24. Option (b) moves the main table to PDEs where a direct PINN fails. Option (c) changes the data setup, including the BC weight, and looks for ratios of 5 to 10. Option (d) keeps option (a) as the main table and puts the older BC=5000 to 10000 results of 5 to 963 into an appendix. Follow option (d) and do not start a new hyperparameter sweep until this paper-structure choice is made.

options.A:
Goal: Search MLP Poisson again after the last MLP Heat staged run, and start ResNet on four missing PDEs, using earlier same-PDE runs to set the search box.

Plan: On MLP Poisson, set each knob box from the smaller of the ResNet and PirateNets Poisson bests divided by 30 to the larger of those two bests multiplied by 30. Run 15 direct trials and 30 staged trials in that box, and put the ResNet Poisson best and the PirateNets Poisson best in as the first trials. On ResNet Helmholtz2D, PoissonND, Heat2D_Multiscale, and Wave2D_Heterogeneous, use the current wide search box, with learning rate from 3e-4 to 0.03 and the other knobs on their present ranges. Run 15 direct trials and 30 staged trials on each of those four ResNet PDEs.
options.B:
Goal: Search MLP Poisson again after the last MLP Heat staged run, and start ResNet on four missing PDEs, using earlier best hyperparameters as the first trials.

Plan: Keep the current wide search box on every cell, with learning rate from 3e-4 to 0.03 and the other knobs on their present ranges. Put the best hyperparameter set from a nearby backbone in as trial 0. Run 15 direct trials and 30 staged trials on each cell. On MLP Poisson, run one more search in that wide box with the ResNet Poisson best and the PirateNets Poisson best as the first trials. On ResNet Helmholtz2D, PoissonND, Heat2D_Multiscale, and Wave2D_Heterogeneous, use the same wide box and add a related prior as trial 0 when one exists.

options.A:
Goal: Take the next ResNet PINNacle step as one 6-hour slice of four cells, then read the results before planning more cells.

Plan: Launch four cells that include staged widen on PoissonND, Burgers2D, and KuramotoSivashinsky, plus one remaining PDE such as Poisson1D or NS2D_BackStep. Run staged search on a PDE that already has a finished direct result. Set trial timeout to 180 or 240 minutes on the slow PDEs and keep the search ranges wide. After the four cells finish, read L2RE, whether the best hyperparameters sit on a search bound, and whether error stays near 1. Use that reading to choose the next four cells.
options.B:
Goal: Finish the ResNet PINNacle 22-PDE grid by running the six remaining PDEs in one batch.

Plan: Launch Poisson1D, Poisson2D_ManyArea, Heat2D_LongTime, Wave2D_LongTime, NS2D_BackStep, and NS2D_LongTime. For each PDE run a 15-trial direct search and a 30-trial staged search, so the batch has 12 cells. Set trial timeout to 120 minutes on Poisson1D, 180 minutes on Poisson2D_ManyArea and NS2D_BackStep, and 240 minutes on the three LongTime PDEs. Enqueue same-family Optuna priors and keep the current wide search ranges. Collect all 12 cells before the next audit, with a wall of about 5 to 6 hours and a cap of 8 hours. Treat KuramotoSivashinsky, PoissonND, and Burgers2D as finished PINN-fail or trivially-trainable cases. After this ResNet grid is complete, start PirateNets on the remaining PDEs.

options.A:
Goal: Decide the next step for cells where staged error is still above direct error after the three-backbone PINNacle grid.

Plan: Build a table of the best staged error, the best direct error, and the best hyperparameters for every backbone and every PDE. Check whether Burgers2D, NS2D_BackStep, and PoissonND use one staged hyperparameter tuple on more than one backbone. Rerun staged training for those three PDEs on MLP, ResNet, and PirateNets with 20 random trials at the start of the search, 60 trials in total, and no trial taken from an earlier study. Keep the current direct baselines and the current three-stage recipe.
options.B:
Goal: Decide the next step for cells where staged error is still above direct error after the three-backbone PINNacle grid.

Plan: Build a table of the best staged error, the best direct error, and the best hyperparameters for every backbone and every PDE. Take PoissonND as a case where staged training stays worse than direct training on MLP, ResNet, and PirateNets. Take the MLP result on NS2D_BackStep as a result about direct training. Then either train the remaining cells with a new boundary-condition weight, with more stages, or with the Muon optimizer, or start writing the paper and put those cells in the discussion.

options.A:
Goal: Run the five-hyperparameter shared-stage setting on all three backbones of Burgers2D, PoissonND, and NS2D_BackStep.

Plan: Run that setting on the nine cells given by these three PDEs and MLP, ResNet, and PirateNets. If the best point of a hyperparameter sits on a search bound, widen that bound and search again. Continue until all nine cells have been run and each of the five hyperparameters has its best point away from the search bounds.
options.B:
Goal: Write the paper from the current 64 of 69 staged-versus-direct pass rate.

Plan: Keep the 64 cells that already pass as the main table. Report ResNet on PoissonND, ResNet and PirateNets on Burgers2D, ResNet on KS, and PirateNets on GrayScott at their current best points in a limitation section. Begin paper writing from this table.

options.A:
Goal: Write the paper from the 69-cell 5-hp grid and the V78 cross-backbone transfer result.

Plan: Use the 3-backbone 23-PDE 5-hp seed 0 table as the main result. Put the V33, V74, and V78 staged-versus-7-hp scores into a paper section on cross-backbone hyperparameter transfer. Draft sections 1 through 6 and the figures around that table, the 7-hp baseline design issue, and the P2DMA MLP case.
options.B:
Goal: Check the 5-hp and 7-hp cell results, then run two-stage training with shared init and learning rate and add Burgers2D trials.

Plan: Read every 5-hp and 7-hp study and list cells that still need runs. Train two-stage PINNs on five PDEs times three backbones, with the two stages sharing init scale and learning rate, and compare staged L2RE with direct training. Continue Burgers2D on MLP, ResNet, and PirateNets until each backbone has at least 20 complete trials.

options.A:
Goal: Write a paper from the 69-cell five-hyperparameter seed-0 grid and the PoissonND hyperparameter transfer.

Plan: Use the staged-versus-direct relative L2 error table on 23 PDEs and 3 network types as the main result. Add a results section that applies one PoissonND five-hyperparameter setting from MLP to ResNet and to PirateNets. Discuss the seven-hyperparameter staged search and the Poisson2D_MA MLP case. Draft the method, results, and discussion around these tables. Then collect three random seeds on cells whose staged-to-direct ratio is near 1.1.
options.B:
Goal: Test shared stage hyperparameters on representative cells and fill the missing Burgers2D trials.

Plan: Recheck all five-hyperparameter and seven-hyperparameter cells for missing runs. Add Burgers2D trials on MLP, ResNet, and PirateNets until each network type has at least 20 finished trials. On five PDEs and all three network types, share initialization and learning rate across the two stages and compare staged relative L2 error with direct training. Use 30 trials and seed 0 on each of these 15 cells.

options.A:
Goal: Test whether progressive staged training on Poisson2D Classic gets better as K increases from 2 to 4.

Plan: Train MLP, ResNet, and PirateNets on Poisson2D Classic, starting from the existing K2, K3, and K4 progressive checkpoints. At each growth step, compare the full network output, the PDE residual, and the L2RE before and after the new block is attached. Compare a copied output head with a newly initialized head, and check whether a 3-layer ResNet cut changes the residual pairing of the copied layers. Replay the final fine-tune with more steps at the same hyperparameters. Then rerun the K2, K3, and K4 comparison under the growth setting chosen by those checks.
options.B:
Goal: Test whether progressive staged training on Poisson2D Classic gets better as K increases from 2 to 4.

Plan: Train MLP, ResNet, and PirateNets on Poisson2D Classic with a fixed 3-layer growth block, so K2 ends at 6 layers, K3 ends at 9 layers, and K4 ends at 12 layers. Give each growth block 6666 steps, and keep a 6-layer schedule that uses the same total steps as K4. Search each schedule from a new sampler to 40 complete trials with the same hyperparameter bounds. Then rerun the best setting on train seeds 1 through 4. Report terminal L2RE and compare K2, K3, K4, and the same-compute 6-layer schedule.

options.A:
Goal: Read the three-backbone depth result from K-loss and step-loss figures on the existing Poisson-2D Classic trials.

Plan: Use the current seed-0 Poisson-2D Classic K2, K3, and K4 trials for MLP, ResNet, and PirateNets. For each backbone, draw one K-loss figure of final relative L2 error at K2, K3, and K4, and one step-loss figure of relative L2 error and training loss versus optimizer step, with the growth-stage boundaries marked. Read whether error falls as K grows from these six figures.
options.B:
Goal: Complete the fine-tune and growth diagnostics and then re-run the three-backbone Poisson-2D Classic depth gate.

Plan: Take the current K4 < K3 < K2 count of 0 out of 3 on MLP, ResNet, and PirateNets as the depth result. Finish the fine-tune budget probes and the growth-preservation variants on the existing K3 and K4 checkpoints. After those diagnostics, choose a growth or fine-tune change and re-run seed-0 Poisson-2D Classic for the three backbones at K2, K3, K4, and the same-compute K2 extra schedule, with pass defined as K4 < K3 < K2 and K4 < K2 extra.

options.A:
Goal: Continue the Poisson2D_Classic repair work after the six loss figures.

Plan: Treat the new K-loss and step-loss plots as a picture of the known jump when a new block is added on Poisson2D_Classic. Next, run a shared-absolute learning-rate fine-tune grid on the same Poisson2D_Classic K3 and K4 checkpoints, finish two replay runs from the same saved state for MLP, ResNet, and PirateNets, and search for a growth step that keeps the old network output on each backbone. If all three backbones pass that growth-step gate, rerun the Poisson2D_Classic K2, K3, and K4 main grid with the rule that K4 must beat K3 and K2. Put Wave2D_Heterogeneous and other hard PDEs in a later round after that seed-0 Poisson2D_Classic gate.
options.B:
Goal: Test the growth step on a PDE where a one-block net still has large error.

Plan: After each growth step, record the full network output, the PDE residual, and the training loss, and check that the loss falls below the previous stage after the jump. On Wave2D_Heterogeneous, and with Heat2D_VaryingCoef as a second check, run K1, K2, and K3 under the current growth rule and under a repaired growth rule from the same saved state. Call a case hard when K1 L2RE is at least 0.90, K2 is at most 0.90 times K1, and K2 is still at least 0.30. If a candidate misses that gate, switch to the next hard PDE and repeat the same K1 to K3 comparison. Start any K4 run only after the repaired K3 curve stays below K2.

options.A:
Goal: Select hard PDEs on which K=1 fails and K=2 improves but remains large.

Plan: Mark K=1 as a failure when the network collapses to a trivial pattern, such as every method staying near a loss of 0.5, or when relative L2 error is at least 0.40 if that collapse is not scored directly. Also require the K=2 error to be at most 0.90 times the K=1 error and still at least 0.30. Run a separate K=1 search and a separate K=2 search for MLP, ResNet, and PirateNets. Keep a PDE only when all three networks meet every cutoff. If the K=1 error is below 0.40, reject that PDE and apply the same 0.40 rule to the next candidate.
options.B:
Goal: Select hard PDEs on which K=1 fails and K=2 improves but remains large.

Plan: Mark K=1 as a failure when its relative L2 error is at least 0.90, the band near an untrained predictor. Also require the K=2 error to be at most 0.90 times the K=1 error and still at least 0.30. Run a separate K=1 search and a separate K=2 search for MLP, ResNet, and PirateNets. Keep a PDE only when all three networks meet every cutoff. If the K=1 error is below 0.90, reject that PDE and apply the same 0.90 rule to the next candidate.

options.A:
Goal: Measure whether the reported SDT gain comes from optimizer restart or from shallow initialization, and pass a post-growth loss recovery test before LongTime staged training.

Plan: Reuse the selected Vanilla and SDT runs on Heat2D-Multiscale, Poisson3D-Complex, and Navier-Stokes2D-Lid-Driven for MLP and PirateNets. Train two extra arms with those same hyperparameters. Vanilla plus Restart keeps the full deep network from step 0 and resets the optimizer and the stage learning rate at the SDT switch times. Shallow Warm-Start trains a shallow net, adds layers, and then trains every layer. Continue the LongTime vanilla jobs that are already running, and give the ablation the first open training slots. Keep LongTime staged training unlaunched until, on both LongTime PDEs and three backbones, the training loss after each added block falls below the value from before the add within 200 steps.
options.B:
Goal: Measure whether the reported SDT gain comes from optimizer restart or from shallow initialization, and run LongTime staged training that copies a trained prefix and trains a new block.

Plan: Reuse the selected Vanilla and SDT runs on Heat2D-Multiscale, Poisson3D-Complex, and Navier-Stokes2D-Lid-Driven for MLP and PirateNets. Train two extra arms with those same hyperparameters. Vanilla plus Restart keeps the full deep network from step 0 and resets the optimizer and the stage learning rate at the SDT switch times. Shallow Warm-Start trains a shallow net, adds layers, and then trains every layer. Continue the LongTime vanilla jobs that are already running, and give the ablation the first open training slots. In the same round, start staged training on Heat2D-LongTime and NS2D-LongTime. At each growth step copy the trained prefix, keep those layers fixed, train a newly initialized block, and finish with one full-network fine-tune.

options.A:
Goal: Test whether current_reset growth on Heat2D_LongTime and NS2D_LongTime recovers a lower objective after the network is deepened.

Plan: Run six K2 growth tests, one for each pair of Heat2D_LongTime or NS2D_LongTime with MLP, ResNet, or PirateNets. At the growth step, copy the old prefix into a deeper network and randomly initialize the new layers and the output head. Record the training objective and real-GT L2RE before the first update and after 200 steps. Count a test as a pass only if the post-growth objective is at most twice the pre-growth objective, L2RE is at most 1.05 times the pre-growth L2RE, and the objective falls below 0.95 times the pre-growth value within 200 steps. If any of the six tests fails, keep the staged LongTime K1 to K5 studies unstarted and continue the vanilla K-grid. If all six pass, start the 30 staged LongTime studies with the same final depth and step budget as the vanilla runs.
options.B:
Goal: Measure K-staged training on Heat2D_LongTime and NS2D_LongTime for PirateNets and MLP at K equal to 3, 4, and 5.

Plan: Run 12 Optuna studies, one for each pair of Heat2D_LongTime or NS2D_LongTime, PirateNets or MLP, and K in {3,4,5}. Keep the existing K=1 and K=2 results as the K=1 and K=2 points. For a chosen K, train K growth stages and then one full-network fine-tune, so the run has K+1 training stages. In growth stage n, copy the prefix trained in the first n-1 stages, leave those prefix weights unchanged, and train only the new randomly initialized block and head. Use the same learning rate and step count for the first K stages, and use a separate learning rate for the last fine-tune stage. Set each Optuna search from the K=1 and K=2 hyperparameter basins already obtained on the same PDE and backbone.

options.A:
Goal: Get K-staged L2RE curves on Heat2D_LongTime and NS2D_LongTime for MLP and PirateNets.

Plan: Start 12 Optuna searches for K=3, 4, and 5 on those two PDEs and two backbones. Each growth stage adds a 3-layer block, so the trained nets have 9, 12, and 15 layers. Keep the prefix frozen while the new block trains, then run one full-network fine-tune. Use the finished vanilla runs as the K=1 points and the historical n6 staged runs as the K=2 points, and set the growth and fine-tune learning-rate search from the selected K=2 hyperparameters of the same PDE and backbone.
options.B:
Goal: Get K-staged L2RE curves on Heat2D_LongTime and NS2D_LongTime for MLP and PirateNets.

Plan: Start Optuna searches for K=1 through K=6 on those two PDEs and two backbones. Each growth stage adds one layer, so K=1 trains a 1-layer net and K=6 trains a 6-layer net. Keep the prefix frozen while the new layer trains, then run one full-network fine-tune. Set the search from the known 6-layer optima with depth-muP: map the growth learning rate and init scale to the 1-layer versions, map the fine-tune learning rate to the matching K-layer version, and search around those centers.

options.A:
Goal: Compare staged depth training and vanilla training on Heat 2D varying coefficient and Poisson-Boltzmann 2D as the network grows by three-layer blocks.

Plan: Use Heat 2D varying coefficient and Poisson-Boltzmann 2D with MLP and PirateNets. Grow the net by a three-layer block at each stage for K = 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5, so the final depths are 3, 6, 9, 12, and 15 layers. Reuse the existing K = 2 runs at depth 6, and run a hyperparameter search for K = 1, 3, 4, and 5 on each PDE and backbone, which is 16 searches. For each of those depths, train a vanilla net from scratch at the same final depth, and reuse the existing depth-6 vanilla runs. Set the hyperparameter ranges from the known K = 2 hyperparameter centers and from the earlier basin sizes.
options.B:
Goal: Compare staged depth training and vanilla training on Heat 2D long time and Navier-Stokes 2D long time as the network grows one layer at a time.

Plan: Use Heat 2D long time and Navier-Stokes 2D long time with MLP and PirateNets. Grow the net by one layer at each stage for K = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6, so the final depths are 1 through 6 layers. For each K, train a vanilla net from scratch at the same final depth. Set the hyperparameter ranges by depth-muP scaling from the known 6-layer hyperparameters. Plot L2RE against K for each PDE and backbone pair with a staged curve and a vanilla curve.

options.A:
Goal: Test whether adding more stages lowers error on Heat 2D with varying coefficient and Poisson-Boltzmann 2D.

Plan: Use these two equations with MLP and PirateNets. Grow the network by a block of 3 layers at each stage. Set K to 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5, so the final depths are 3, 6, 9, 12, and 15. Reuse the K=2 runs, and run 16 hyperparameter searches for the remaining K values. Set each search range from the known K=2 optimum and basin on that equation and backbone. Train a vanilla network at each matching final depth.
options.B:
Goal: Test whether adding more stages lowers error on Heat 2D long time and Navier-Stokes 2D long time.

Plan: Use these two long-time equations with MLP and PirateNets. Grow the network by one layer at each stage. Set K to 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6, so the final depth equals K. Use the staged runs and the same-depth vanilla runs collected at each K. Plot relative L2 error against K for staged training and vanilla training on each equation and each backbone.

options.A:
Goal: Measure staged-depth training and vanilla training from depth 3 to depth 15 on Heat2D-VaryingCoeff and Poisson-Boltzmann2D.

Plan: On both PDEs, run MLP and PirateNets staged training at K=1, 3, 4, and 5 with a 3-layer growth block, and run vanilla training at n=3, 9, 12, and 15 as independent studies. Run the K=1 staged cell as a two-phase 3-layer search and run the n=3 vanilla cell as a from-scratch search. Reuse the existing setup-B results for K=2 and n=6. After collection, plot L2RE against K with a staged curve and a vanilla curve for each PDE and backbone.
options.B:
Goal: Measure staged-depth training and vanilla training from depth 3 to depth 15 on Heat2D-VaryingCoeff and Poisson-Boltzmann2D.

Plan: On both PDEs, run MLP and PirateNets staged training at K=3, 4, and 5 with a 3-layer growth block, and run vanilla training at n=9, 12, and 15. For depth 3, run one from-scratch 3-layer study and use that result as staged K=1 and as vanilla n=3. Reuse the existing setup-B results for K=2 and n=6. After collection, plot L2RE against K with a staged curve and a vanilla curve for each PDE and backbone.

options.A:
Goal: Add a second PB2D staged hyperparameter search so that L2RE falls as K grows and the reused K=2 point sits on the K=1 to K=3 line.

Plan: Keep the finished PB2D staged studies for MLP and PirateNets. Convert the reused K=2 five-hyperparameter best run into a growth learning rate, a last-stage learning rate, and an init scale, and insert that triple as the first new trial. Search those three knobs on a log scale in a factor of 5.6 above and below each of those values. Add twelve new complete trials to each of the K=1, 3, 4, and 5 studies. Keep the current step counts, which stay near 6667 steps per stage for every K.
options.B:
Goal: Add a second PB2D staged hyperparameter search so that L2RE falls as K grows and the reused K=2 point sits on the K=1 to K=3 line.

Plan: Keep the finished PB2D staged trials for MLP and PirateNets. Take each backbone's K=2 study that used one shared learning rate, one shared init scale, and one last-stage ratio. Keep the trials with loss at most twice the best, drop those with last-stage ratio above 1, and fit a quadratic on the rest to set the three search ranges, with last-stage learning rate defined as learning rate times that ratio. Train 6000 steps in each stage, keep the growth ranges the same for every K, and scale the last-stage learning-rate range by 6 over 3K. Run ten search trials for K=3, 4, and 5, and add another batch if a best trial sits on a bound.

options.A:
Goal: Find hyperparameters for K-stage MLP training on Poisson-Boltzmann 2D at K=1, 3, 4, and 5.

Plan: Continue the existing Optuna studies for those four K values. Keep the eight finished trials. Add twelve new trials to each study. Insert as trial 0 the effective hyperparameters from the finished K=2 five-knob run: growth learning rate 5.35e-3, fine-tune learning rate 1.38e-4, and init scale 2.693. Search each of those three quantities log-uniform from the center divided by 5.6 to the center times 5.6, which is growth learning rate 9.6e-4 to 3.0e-2, fine-tune learning rate 2.5e-5 to 7.7e-4, and init scale 0.48 to 15.1. For K=1, search only fine-tune learning rate and init scale. Keep seed 0, width 100, and AdamW.
options.B:
Goal: Find hyperparameters for K-stage MLP training on Poisson-Boltzmann 2D at K=1, 3, 4, and 5.

Plan: Open a new 10-trial Optuna search for those four K values. Use the finished three-knob Poisson-Boltzmann 2D MLP study that uses one learning rate and one init scale for the growth stages. From the trials whose loss is at most twice the best trial, remove the points with last-stage learning-rate ratio above 1 and a low growth learning rate, then set the boxes from the remaining points. Search growth learning rate from 0.00072 to 0.0159 and init scale from 0.0711 to 2.398, with no depth scaling. Search the last-stage fine-tune learning rate as learning rate times last-stage ratio from 2.45e-6 to 0.00322, and multiply that box by 6 divided by 3 times K. Give every stage 6000 steps, so each run has 6000 times (K+1) steps.

options.A:
Goal: Measure the deeper-K effect on three new PDEs and on two extra random seeds.

Plan: Start deeper-K experiments on Poisson 3D with complex geometry, Navier-Stokes 2D lid-driven flow, and Heat 2D with complex geometry. Use the MLP backbone and the PirateNets backbone. Use depths K=2, K=3, and K=5. Train with staged depth training and with vanilla training. Use random seeds 0, 1, and 2. In each new study, run 10 complete Optuna trials. On Poisson-Boltzmann 2D, run the existing depth cells again at seed 1 and seed 2. Keep the best hyperparameters from seed 0 and do not run a new hyperparameter search.
options.B:
Goal: Run Optuna trials on Poisson-Boltzmann 2D at K=3, K=4, and K=5 for staged depth training and for vanilla training.

Plan: Use random seed 0. On Poisson-Boltzmann 2D, add 10 complete Optuna trials to staged depth training at K=3, K=4, and K=5. Add 10 complete Optuna trials to vanilla training at 9 layers, 12 layers, and 15 layers. Use the hyperparameter ranges from the last Poisson-Boltzmann 2D search. After this batch, fit a straight line to the log of K against the log of L2RE for staged depth training. If the R2 of that fit is below 0.95, add another batch of 10 trials on the same cells.

options.A:
Goal: Extend the deeper-K grid to three new PDEs and three random seeds.

Plan: Run staged depth training and same-depth vanilla training with MLP and PirateNets on Poisson-3D complex geometry, Navier-Stokes 2D lid-driven flow, and Heat-2D complex geometry. Use depths K=2, 3, and 5, and run seeds 0, 1, and 2. Give each study 10 complete Optuna trials. On Poisson-Boltzmann 2D, rerun the current K-grid cells on seeds 1 and 2 with the seed-0 best hyperparameters held fixed.
options.B:
Goal: Search hyperparameters at K=3, 4, and 5 for staged and vanilla training on Poisson-Boltzmann 2D and Heat-2D complex geometry.

Plan: On Poisson-Boltzmann 2D at seed 0, add 10 more complete Optuna trials at K=3, 4, and 5 for staged depth training. Give vanilla training the same trial count at n=9, 12, and 15. After this batch, fit ln(K) versus ln(loss) for the staged runs, and if R-squared is below 0.95 add another 10-trial batch. Run the same depth grid on Heat-2D complex geometry at seed 0.

options.A:
Goal: Improve the Heat2D_ComplexGeometry log-log depth fit using the three depths n=6, n=9, and n=15.

Plan: Keep Heat2D_ComplexGeometry at K=2, K=3, and K=5. For MLP and PirateNets, train both staged depth training and vanilla. Add ten more hyperparameter trials to each of the eight studies at K=3 and K=5, so each of those studies has twenty finished trials. Reuse the existing K=2 studies as the n=6 anchors. After this batch, fit the staged log-log line on n=6, n=9, and n=15.
options.B:
Goal: Improve the Heat2D_ComplexGeometry log-log depth fit using the five depths n=3, n=6, n=9, n=12, and n=15.

Plan: Keep the Heat2D_ComplexGeometry measurements at K=2, K=3, and K=5. Add K=1 at depth n=3 and K=4 at depth n=12 for MLP and PirateNets. For K=1, train one n=3 study per backbone; staged training at K=1 is the same run as vanilla. For K=4, train both staged depth training and vanilla. Search each new study with ten finished hyperparameter trials, then fit the staged log-log line on n=3, n=6, n=9, n=12, and n=15.

options.A:
Goal: Search PoissonBoltzmann2D at K=3, K=4, and K=5 together, and add H2DCG K=4 plus more K=3 and K=5 trials, to raise staged log-log R² to 0.98 or higher.

Plan: On PoissonBoltzmann2D, add ten complete trials to each K=3, K=4, and K=5 cell for MLP and PirateNets under both staged and vanilla training. Continue CMA-ES on the K=4 staged studies and TPE on K=3 and K=5, and enqueue each backbone's best K=3 trial into the K=5 study and the best K=5 trial into the K=3 study. On H2DCG, add K=4 with ten complete trials per backbone and training mode, and add ten more complete trials to the staged K=3 and K=5 cells.
options.B:
Goal: Finish the remaining H2DCG batch-2 vanilla K=5 cells, then jointly review PoissonBoltzmann2D and H2DCG and design the next PoissonBoltzmann2D search for staged log-log R² of 0.98 or higher.

Plan: Continue the current H2DCG batch-2 studies until the remaining vanilla K=5 cells for MLP and PirateNets each have 20 complete trials. Keep PoissonBoltzmann2D at the collected K=4 rescue table, where staged log-log R² is about 0.85 for MLP and 0.93 for PirateNets. After both the PoissonBoltzmann2D rescue and this H2DCG batch have no remaining runs, send the two PDEs through one joint audit and one scientist round that designs the next PoissonBoltzmann2D hyperparameter search under the R² of 0.98 or higher criterion.

options.A:
Goal: Raise the PoissonBoltzmann2D SDT log-log R² after the latest collected K-grid batch.

Plan: Start a new PoissonBoltzmann2D batch that adds ten complete trials to each of twelve cells at K=3, K=4, and K=5 for MLP and PirateNets, covering both SDT and vanilla. Run a CMA-ES study on MLP SDT at K=5 that enqueues the current K=3, K=4, and PirateNets K=5 best hyperparameters, then adds ten CMA-ES trials. Continue CMA-ES on the MLP and PirateNets K=4 SDT cells, and run TPE on the remaining cells.
options.B:
Goal: Raise the PoissonBoltzmann2D SDT log-log R² after the latest collected K-grid batch.

Plan: Add the new PoissonBoltzmann2D trials to MLP SDT at K=5, and add the same number of new vanilla trials at K=5. Run a CMA-ES study on that K=5 SDT cell starting from the current MLP K=5 best hyperparameters. After the new trials finish, refit the MLP log-log R² on the five points from K=1 through K=5, and compare the new K=5 SDT minimum with the new K=5 vanilla minimum.

options.A:
Goal: Continue the deeper-K study so that SDT log-log R² on Poisson-Boltzmann 2D and Heat2D CG can reach 0.98.

Plan: Finish the remaining PirateNets cells on Poisson-Boltzmann 2D, then review that PDE. Design the next Poisson-Boltzmann 2D hyperparameter round from the new MLP and PirateNets results. Finish the running Heat2D CG depth cells in a second planning cycle and review Heat2D CG when that batch is collected.
options.B:
Goal: Continue the deeper-K study so that SDT log-log R² on Poisson-Boltzmann 2D and Heat2D CG can reach 0.98.

Plan: Finish the remaining PirateNets cells on Poisson-Boltzmann 2D and the running Heat2D CG depth cells under one planning cycle. When either remaining group stops, review both PDEs. Design the next experiment batch from that checkpoint, including the next Poisson-Boltzmann 2D hyperparameter round.

options.A:
Goal: Search PoissonBoltzmann2D MLP staged-depth training at K=5, and measure Heat2D_ComplexGeometry at K=1 with final depth 3.

Plan: On PoissonBoltzmann2D with MLP, run a hyperparameter search for staged-depth training at K=5, and run vanilla training at depth 15 with the same number of completed evaluations as the K=5 staged-depth search. K=1, K=2, K=3, and K=4 in this MLP staged-depth series use the evaluations already collected. On Heat2D_ComplexGeometry, run K=1 with final depth 3 for MLP and for PirateNets.
options.B:
Goal: Test whether PoissonBoltzmann2D MLP hyperparameters from K=4 transfer to K=5, and continue Heat2D_ComplexGeometry at K=2, K=3, K=4, and K=5.

Plan: On PoissonBoltzmann2D with MLP at K=5, train seven networks that mix the K=5 parent values and the K=4 values of growth learning rate, init scale, and fine-tune learning rate. Then train seventeen vanilla networks of depth 15 so that staged-depth and vanilla at K=5 each have 57 completed evaluations. On Heat2D_ComplexGeometry, continue the running MLP and PirateNets studies at K=2, K=3, K=4, and K=5.

options.A:
Goal: Analyze the Heat2D_ComplexGeometry K-grid when TG-G has eight terminal cells, and continue TG-J and TG-K as a second PoissonBoltzmann2D experiment.

Plan: Let Heat2D_ComplexGeometry TG-G finish its remaining cells. When all eight cells are terminal, compute for that PDE whether SDT and vanilla have the same number of completed hyperparameter evaluations at each K, whether the SDT K-loss R² for each backbone meets 0.98, and whether the K=1 n=3 point is present. Design the next Heat2D_ComplexGeometry runs from those checks, and run the missing K=1 n=3 search in that batch. Continue PoissonBoltzmann2D TG-J and TG-K to match evaluation counts and to search MLP K5.
options.B:
Goal: Finish TG-J and TG-K on PoissonBoltzmann2D, then recompute the same-count SDT versus vanilla comparison and the K-loss R².

Plan: Make TG-J and TG-K the next experiment step. TG-J adds hyperparameter evaluations on the four PoissonBoltzmann2D cells where SDT and vanilla now have different completed-evaluation counts, until both sides match. TG-K runs a CMA-ES search on MLP K5 around the current elite range and adds the same number of new vanilla evaluations. After both groups finish, recompute the eight-cell SDT versus vanilla table and the K-loss R² for each backbone. Keep Heat2D_ComplexGeometry TG-G running, and start analysis of that PDE after this PoissonBoltzmann2D recomputation.

options.A:
Goal: Bring Heat2D complex-geometry log-log R² to 0.98 on the staged-training depth grid.

Plan: Run the next experiments on Heat2D with complex geometry for MLP and PirateNets. Add K=1 points at depth n=3 with 30 hyperparameter trials for each backbone, using search ranges taken from the K=2 runs. Expand the K=4 staged and vanilla searches to 30 trials from the current 10-trial studies, and bring the vanilla searches at K=2, K=3, and K=5 to 30 trials from their current studies.
options.B:
Goal: Bring Poisson-Boltzmann 2D MLP log-log R² to 0.98 and continue the Heat2D complex-geometry depth grid.

Plan: Run the next experiments on both Poisson-Boltzmann 2D and Heat2D with complex geometry. On Poisson-Boltzmann 2D MLP, add more hyperparameter trials at K=3 and K=4, or test gradient-clip thresholds between the 95th and 97th percentiles, until the K-loss log-log R² reaches 0.98. On Heat2D with complex geometry, expand the K=4 staged and vanilla searches to 30 trials, bring every vanilla search to 30 trials, and start 30-trial K=1 runs at depth n=3 for MLP and PirateNets.

options.A:
Goal: Find PoissonND ResNet SDT and PirateNets SDT hyperparameters that beat the existing vanilla L2RE.

Plan: Start an Optuna TPE search for PoissonND ResNet SDT and an Optuna TPE search for PoissonND PirateNets SDT. Use 30 trials for each cell. Do not train vanilla. For ResNet, put the MLP transfer hyperparameters in as trial 0, keep s3_lr_ratio below 1, and search in the ranges estimated from earlier PoissonND trials. For PirateNets, put the growth learning-rate multiplier 0.149 in as trial 0 and 0.0149 in as trial 1, and search in the ranges that include 0.149. After the 30 trials, report the best L2RE of each cell against 0.000798 and 0.000467.
options.B:
Goal: Find PoissonND ResNet SDT and PirateNets SDT hyperparameters that beat the existing vanilla L2RE.

Plan: Start an Optuna TPE search for PoissonND ResNet SDT and an Optuna TPE search for PoissonND PirateNets SDT. Use 10 trials for each cell. Do not train vanilla. For ResNet, put the MLP transfer hyperparameters in as trial 0, keep s3_lr_ratio below 1, and search in the ranges estimated from earlier PoissonND trials. For PirateNets, put the growth learning-rate multiplier 0.149 in as trial 0 and 0.0149 in as trial 1, and search in the ranges that include 0.149. After the 10 trials, inspect whether the best point hits a bound or looks abnormal, and then design the next search.

options.A:
